children.title: Dense Monomial Gram Lifts
children.top_down_role: Canonical monomial-basis representations of SOS cones.

knowledge_statements.title: Dense Monomial Gram Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense degree-d Gram representation of the SOS cone in n variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(v_d(x)=(x^\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le d}\). A polynomial \(p\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) of degree at most \(2d\) is a sum of squares of polynomials of degree at most \(d\) if and only if there exists \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^{\binom{n+d}{d}}\) such that
\[p(x)=v_d(x)^\mathsf TQv_d(x).\]
Coefficient matching is the linear system \(p_\gamma=\sum_{\alpha+\beta=\gamma}Q_{\alpha\beta}\) for every \(\gamma\) with \(|\gamma|\le2d\). Thus the SOS cone is the linear image of a positive-semidefinite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degree-2d polynomial is SOS exactly when it has a positive-semidefinite Gram matrix indexed by every monomial of degree at most d.
assumptions_latex: \(p\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\)
\(\deg p\le 2d\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\in\Sigma[x]_{2d}\iff \exists Q\succeq0:\ p=v_d^\mathsf TQv_d\).

notation.meaning: Vector of all monomials of total degree at most d.
Cone of N-by-N real positive-semidefinite matrices.
SOS polynomials admitting summands of degree at most d.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical Gram-matrix characterization of finite-degree SOS polynomials

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically standard and fits the dense monomial Gram-lift container, but no inspectable source with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator is cited.

children.title: Support-Reduced Gram Lifts
children.top_down_role: Gram representations reduced through polynomial support geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Reduced Gram Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton-polytope reduction of the monomial index set in a Gram lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(p\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), define \(S(p)=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n:2\alpha\in\operatorname{New}(p)\}\) and \(z_{S(p)}=(x^\alpha)_{\alpha\in S(p)}\). If \(p\) is SOS, every squared summand may be chosen with support contained in \(S(p)\); consequently,
\[p=z_{S(p)}^\mathsf TQz_{S(p)}\quad\text{for some }Q\succeq0.\]
Conversely, every such positive-semidefinite Gram representation is an SOS decomposition. Hence monomials outside half the Newton polytope may be removed without changing SOS membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SOS membership can be tested with monomials whose doubled exponent lies in the polynomial's Newton polytope; all other Gram indices are unnecessary.
assumptions_latex: \(p\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\in\Sigma[x]\iff \exists Q\succeq0:\ p=z_{S(p)}^\mathsf TQz_{S(p)}\).

notation.meaning: Convex hull of exponent vectors in the support of p.
Integer exponent vectors in one half of the Newton polytope.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard Newton-polytope support theorem for SOS decompositions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Newton-polytope support reduction is stated precisely and the representation kind fits the container, but the nontrivial support theorem has no cited source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Quotient-Basis Gram Lifts
children.top_down_role: Gram representations expressed through bases of polynomial quotient spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Quotient-Basis Gram Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gram representation of sums of squares in a polynomial quotient algebra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\), let \(A=\mathbb R[x]/I\), and let \(W\subseteq A\) be finite-dimensional with basis \(b=(b_1,\ldots,b_N)^\mathsf T\). For \(\bar p\in A\),
\[\bar p\in\left\{\sum_{k=1}^r s_k^2:r\ge0,\ s_k\in W\right\}\]
if and only if there exists \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^N\) satisfying \(\bar p=b^\mathsf TQb\) in \(A\). Equality in the quotient is equivalently the polynomial congruence \(p-b^\mathsf TQb\in I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residue class is SOS from a chosen quotient subspace exactly when it has a positive-semidefinite Gram matrix in any basis of that subspace.
assumptions_latex: \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) is an ideal.
\(W\subseteq\mathbb R[x]/I\) is finite-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar p\in\Sigma(W)\iff \exists Q\succeq0:\ \bar p=b^\mathsf TQb\).

notation.meaning: Finite-dimensional quotient subspace used for SOS summands.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Gram factorization applied in a finite-dimensional quotient subspace

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-dimensional quotient Gram representation is internally consistent and appropriately classified as a representation, but it lacks a source with a specific locator.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: an SOS Gram term is nonnegative and an equality-ideal term vanishes on the real equality set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SOS Gram certificates modulo polynomial equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h_1,\ldots,h_s,p\in\mathbb R[x]\), let \(I=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_s\rangle\), and let \(b=(b_1,\ldots,b_N)^\mathsf T\) be a selected polynomial basis vector whose residue classes represent a finite-dimensional quotient subspace. If there exist \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^N\) and \(q_1,\ldots,q_s\in\mathbb R[x]\) such that
\[p=b^\mathsf TQb+\sum_{j=1}^s q_jh_j,\]
then \(p(x)\ge0\) for every \(x\in V_{\mathbb R}(I)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:h_j(x)=0,\ j=1,\ldots,s\}\). Imposing explicit degree bounds on \(b\) and each \(q_jh_j\) gives a truncated certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial identity consisting of a positive-semidefinite Gram term plus an equality-ideal term certifies nonnegativity on the common real zero set of the equalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Ideal Gram Reduction

children.title: Relaxation-Order Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Interaction between reduced Gram spaces plus hierarchy order.

assumptions_latex: \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) is an ideal.
\(V_d\subseteq V_{d+1}\subseteq\mathbb R[x]/I\) are finite-dimensional.
\(V_{\mathbb R}(I)\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_d\subseteq C_{d+1}\) and \(\rho_d\le\rho_{d+1}\le\inf_{x\in V_{\mathbb R}(I)}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Degree-d truncated subspace of the quotient algebra.
Cone of sums of squares of elements of V_d.
Order-d certified lower bound defined in the quotient algebra.
Residue class of f modulo I.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: cone nesting follows from inclusion of truncated quotient spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested quotient spaces preserve feasibility and monotonicity across SOS relaxation orders.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) be an ideal, let \(V_d\subseteq V_{d+1}\subseteq\mathbb R[x]/I\) be finite-dimensional quotient subspaces, and define
\[C_d=\left\{\sum_{k=1}^r s_k^2:r\in\mathbb N,\ s_k\in V_d\right\}.\]
Then \(C_d\subseteq C_{d+1}\). If a basis of \(V_d\) is extended to a basis of \(V_{d+1}\), every Gram matrix \(Q\succeq0\) at order \(d\) embeds as \(\operatorname{diag}(Q,0)\succeq0\) at order \(d+1\). For \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\), assume \(V_{\mathbb R}(I)\ne\varnothing\), write \(\bar f\) for its residue class, and define
\[\rho_d=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:\bar f-\gamma\in C_d\}.\]
Then
\[\rho_d\le\rho_{d+1}\le\inf_{x\in V_{\mathbb R}(I)}f(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested quotient subspaces embed every lower-order Gram certificate at higher order, so the quotient-SOS lower bounds are monotone and remain valid on the nonempty real variety.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Order Compatibility

children.title: Gram-Fiber Nonuniqueness
children.top_down_role: Multiplicity of Gram representatives associated with a fixed SOS polynomial.

knowledge_statements.title: Gram-Fiber Nonuniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterization of multiple positive-semidefinite Gram matrices representing one polynomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a basis vector \(z\) and the linear Gram map \(\mathcal A(Q)=z^\mathsf TQz\). The Gram fiber of \(p\) is \(\mathcal G(p)=\{Q\succeq0:\mathcal A(Q)=p\}\). It contains two distinct matrices if and only if there exist \(Q\in\mathcal G(p)\) and nonzero \(H\in\ker\mathcal A\) such that \(Q+H\succeq0\). In particular, if \(Q\succ0\) lies in the fiber and \(\ker\mathcal A\ne\{0\}\), then sufficiently small perturbations \(Q+tH\) give infinitely many Gram matrices for \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gram matrices are nonunique exactly when a nonzero coefficient-invisible matrix direction preserves positive semidefiniteness from some point of the Gram fiber.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal G(p)\ne\varnothing\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\mathcal G(p)|>1\iff \exists Q\in\mathcal G(p),\ 0\ne H\in\ker\mathcal A:\ Q+H\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Linear map sending a symmetric matrix to its Gram polynomial.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: affine-fiber characterization under a linear Gram map

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine-kernel characterization is correct, explicit, and appropriately classified as a property, but no inspectable source is cited for the Gram-fiber claim.

children.title: Minimal-Face Geometry
children.top_down_role: Smallest semidefinite faces supporting Gram representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal-Face Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal positive-semidefinite face containing a nonempty Gram fiber.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal G(p)\) be a nonempty Gram fiber and set \(N_p=\bigcap_{Q\in\mathcal G(p)}\ker Q\). The minimal face of \(\mathbb S_+^N\) containing the entire fiber is
\[F_p=\{X\succeq0:N_p\subseteq\ker X\}=\{X\succeq0:\operatorname{range}X\subseteq N_p^\perp\}.\]
Equivalently, if \(U_p=\operatorname{span}\{\operatorname{range}Q:Q\in\mathcal G(p)\}\), then \(F_p=\{X\succeq0:\operatorname{range}X\subseteq U_p\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimal PSD face containing a Gram fiber is determined by the fiber's common kernel, equivalently by the span of all represented matrix ranges.
assumptions_latex: \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal G(p)\subseteq\mathbb S_+^N\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{face}_{\min}(\mathcal G(p))=\{X\succeq0:N_p\subseteq\ker X\}\).

notation.meaning: Common kernel of every matrix in the Gram fiber.
Span of the ranges of matrices in the Gram fiber.
Minimal PSD face containing the Gram fiber.

children.title: Fiber–Face Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Geometric links between Gram fibers plus their supporting faces.

knowledge_statements.title: Fiber–Face Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subspace parametrization of PSD faces and their containment relation with Gram fibers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each subspace \(U\subseteq\mathbb R^N\), define \(F_U=\{Q\succeq0:\operatorname{range}Q\subseteq U\}\). The assignment \(U\mapsto F_U\) is a bijection from linear subspaces of \(\mathbb R^N\) to faces of \(\mathbb S_+^N\), with \(F_U\subseteq F_V\) exactly when \(U\subseteq V\). For a nonempty Gram fiber \(\mathcal G(p)\),
\[\mathcal G(p)\subseteq F_U\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad U_p\subseteq U,\]
where \(U_p\) is the span of the ranges of its Gram matrices. Thus \(F_{U_p}\) is the unique smallest face containing the fiber.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PSD faces correspond to matrix-range subspaces; a face contains a Gram fiber exactly when its subspace contains every range occurring in that fiber.
assumptions_latex: \(U,V\subseteq\mathbb R^N\) are linear subspaces.
\(\mathcal G(p)\ne\varnothing\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal G(p)\subseteq F_U\iff U_p\subseteq U\), with minimal containing face \(F_{U_p}\).

notation.meaning: PSD face consisting of matrices whose ranges lie in U.
Span of ranges over the Gram fiber of p.

knowledge_statements.title: Putinar Quadratic-Module Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Archimedean quadratic-module certificate for strict positivity on a basic closed set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) and
\[M(g)=\left\{\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i:\sigma_i\in\Sigma[x]\right\}.\]
Assume \(M(g)\) is Archimedean, meaning that \(R-\|x\|_2^2\in M(g)\) for some \(R>0\). If \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\) satisfies \(f(x)>0\) for every \(x\in K\), then \(f\in M(g)\); equivalently, \(f=\sigma_0+\sum_i\sigma_i g_i\) for SOS multipliers \(\sigma_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the Archimedean condition, every polynomial strictly positive on the feasible set equals an SOS plus SOS-weighted defining inequalities.

notation.meaning: Quadratic module generated by the inequality polynomials.
Cone of sums of squares in R[x].

children.title: Schmüdgen Preordering Certificates
children.top_down_role: Preordering certificate family using products of defining inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Schmüdgen Preordering Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact-set positivity certificate using square-free products of defining inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) be compact, and define the preordering
\[T(g)=\left\{\sum_{\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}^m}\sigma_\varepsilon\prod_{i=1}^m g_i^{\varepsilon_i}:\sigma_\varepsilon\in\Sigma[x]\right\}.\]
If \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\) is strictly positive on \(K\), then \(f\in T(g)\). Thus \(f\) has an SOS certificate involving all square-free products of the defining inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact basic closed set, every strictly positive polynomial has an SOS certificate weighted by square-free products of the defining inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(K=\{x:g_i(x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) is compact.
\(f(x)>0\) for every \(x\in K\).

notation.meaning: Preordering generated by the inequality polynomials.
Selector of a square-free product of generators.
Cone of sums of squares in R[x].

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Ideal Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree-truncated ideal component generated by polynomial equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given equality polynomials \(h=(h_1,\ldots,h_s)\) and an order \(d\), their degree-\(2d\) truncated ideal component is
\[I_{2d}(h)=\left\{\sum_{j=1}^s q_jh_j:q_j\in\mathbb R[x],\ \deg(q_jh_j)\le2d\right\}.\]
Every element of \(I_{2d}(h)\) vanishes on \(V_{\mathbb R}(h)=\{x:h_1(x)=\cdots=h_s(x)=0\}\). No sign restriction is imposed on the multipliers \(q_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The equality component at order d consists of arbitrary polynomial multiples of the equalities whose individual products have degree at most 2d.
assumptions_latex: \(h_1,\ldots,h_s\in\mathbb R[x]\)
\(d\in\mathbb N\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I_{2d}(h)=\{\sum_jq_jh_j:\deg(q_jh_j)\le2d\}\).

notation.meaning: Degree-2d truncated ideal generated by h.
Common real zero set of the equality polynomials.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard truncated equality-ideal component in polynomial optimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and its vanishing property are precise and fit the equality-component leaf, but the selected truncation convention has no cited source with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Inequality-Module Components
children.top_down_role: Quadratic-module portions associated with inequality constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Inequality-Module Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree-truncated quadratic-module component generated by polynomial inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Set \(g_0=1\) for inequality generators \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\). At relaxation order \(d\), the truncated quadratic-module component is
\[M_d(g)=\left\{\sum_{i=0}^m\sigma_i g_i:\sigma_i\in\Sigma[x],\ \deg(\sigma_i g_i)\le2d\right\}.\]
Every element of \(M_d(g)\) is nonnegative on \(K=\{x:g_i(x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\). Equivalently, \(\sigma_i\) may be represented by a positive-semidefinite Gram matrix using monomials through degree \(d-\lceil\deg(g_i)/2\rceil\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The order-d inequality component consists of SOS multipliers times individual inequality generators, with each weighted term restricted to degree at most 2d.
assumptions_latex: \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\)
\(d\in\mathbb N\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_d(g)=\{\sum_{i=0}^m\sigma_i g_i:\sigma_i\in\Sigma[x],\ \deg(\sigma_i g_i)\le2d\}\).

notation.meaning: Basic closed set defined by the inequalities.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Polynomials Nonnegative on Real Varieties p. 37

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an ideal \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\), its real radical is \[\sqrt[\mathbb R]{I}=\left\{p\in\mathbb R[x]:p^{2k}+\sum_{\ell=1}^r q_\ell^2\in I\text{ for some }k\geq1\text{ and }q_\ell\in\mathbb R[x]\right\}.\] One has \(I\subseteq\sqrt[\mathbb R]{I}\) and \(V_{\mathbb R}(I)=V_{\mathbb R}(\sqrt[\mathbb R]{I})\). Consequently, replacing \(I\) by \(\sqrt[\mathbb R]{I}\) preserves the real feasible set while enlarging the coupled certificate cone from \(I+Q(g)\) to \(\sqrt[\mathbb R]{I}+Q(g)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Real-radical replacement preserves the real equality variety but enlarges the algebraic certificate cone, potentially yielding stronger finite SOS relaxations.
knowledge_statements.title: Real-Radical Certificate Refinements

children.title: Radicality Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural limitations arising from nonradical or incorrectly identified ideals.

assumptions_latex: \(I=\langle x^2\rangle\subset\mathbb R[x]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\) vanishes on \(V_{\mathbb R}(I)\) but \(p\notin I\), while \(p\in\sqrt[\mathbb R]{I}=\langle x\rangle\).

notation.meaning: Principal ideal generated by a polynomial.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure caused by using a non-real-radical equality ideal.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Polynomials Nonnegative on Real Varieties p. 37
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Take \(I=\langle x^2\rangle\subset\mathbb R[x]\). Its real variety is \(V_{\mathbb R}(I)=\{0\}\), so \(p=x\) vanishes identically on that variety. Nevertheless, \(x\notin\langle x^2\rangle\), whereas \[\sqrt[\mathbb R]{\langle x^2\rangle}=\langle x\rangle.\] Hence a certificate system using only multiples of the original generator \(x^2\) cannot identify every polynomial equality valid on the real feasible set. The gap disappears after real-radical replacement and shows exactly where radicality-dependent conclusions can fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ideal generated by x squared defines the point zero but omits x itself; thus ordinary ideal certificates can miss equalities valid on the real variety.
knowledge_statements.title: Radicality Failure Boundaries

children.title: Weighted Certificate Families
children.top_down_role: Positivity certificates modified by prescribed polynomial weights.

assumptions_latex: \(w\in\mathbb R[x]\) satisfies \(w(x)>0\) for every \(x\in K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(wf\in Q(g)\), which implies \(f(x)\geq0\) on \(K\).

notation.meaning: Strictly positive polynomial weight on the feasible set.
Quadratic module generated by the constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomially weighted SOS certificates for positivity without assuming the unweighted module is Archimedean.

source_refs.locator: 2.5.1 Representations via sums of squares p. 28

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(K=\{x:g_i(x)\geq0\}\) and a polynomial weight \(w\) strictly positive on \(K\), a weighted certificate for \(f\) is an identity \[wf=\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i,\qquad \sigma_i\in\Sigma[x].\] Since every term on the right is nonnegative on \(K\) and \(w\) has no zero there, the identity certifies \(f\geq0\) on \(K\). A weighted hierarchy fixes or systematically enlarges an admissible family of weights and truncates the degrees of all products.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive polynomial weight multiplies the target into the constraint quadratic module; division by the positive weight then certifies nonnegativity on the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Certificate Families

children.title: Denominator Certificate Families
children.top_down_role: Certificate systems permitting controlled denominator factors.

assumptions_latex: \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\) is nonnegative on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists a nonzero \(q\in\Sigma[x]\) such that \(qf\in\Sigma[x]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Artin-type global denominator certificate for nonnegative real polynomials.

source_refs.locator: 2.5.1 Representations via sums of squares p. 28
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A polynomial \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\) is nonnegative on \(\mathbb R^n\) if and only if there exists a nonzero sum-of-squares polynomial \(q\in\Sigma[x]\) for which \[qf\in\Sigma[x].\] Equivalently, there are sums-of-squares polynomials \(q\neq0\) and \(s\) satisfying \(qf=s\), so \(f=s/q\) wherever \(q\neq0\). The reverse implication extends to zeros of \(q\) by polynomial continuity. Degree bounds on \(q\) and \(s\) define denominator-certificate hierarchy levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally nonnegative polynomial is a quotient of two sums of squares, equivalently a nonzero SOS multiplier turns it into an SOS polynomial.
knowledge_statements.title: Denominator Certificate Families

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a possibly noncompact set \(K=\{x:g_i(x)\geq0\}\), a weighted certificate is applicable whenever one can choose \(w\in\mathbb R[x]\) with \(w(x)>0\) on \(K\) and verify \[wf=\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i,\qquad \sigma_i\in\Sigma[x].\] These conditions are sufficient for \(f\geq0\) on \(K\) and do not require boundedness of \(K\). Completeness requires additional assumptions on \(K\), \(f\), and the permitted weight family; it does not follow from noncompactness alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a noncompact set, a positive weight and an SOS module identity give a sound certificate, while completeness depends on additional geometric and growth assumptions.

children.title: Moment-Matrix Blocks
children.top_down_role: Moment-matrix components of finite hierarchy levels.

assumptions_latex: \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\leq2d}\) is a real truncated sequence indexed by \(\mathbb N^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_y(p^2)\geq0\) for all \(p\in\mathbb R[x]_d\) if and only if \(M_d(y)\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Riesz functional defined by the truncated sequence.
Vector of monomials of degree at most \(d\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite multivariate moment block and its positive-semidefinite characterization.

source_refs.locator: 3.2.1 Moment and localizing matrix p. 58
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\leq2d}\), define \(L_y(\sum_\alpha p_\alpha x^\alpha)=\sum_\alpha p_\alpha y_\alpha\). The order-\(d\) moment matrix is indexed by monomials \(x^\alpha,x^\beta\) of degree at most \(d\) and satisfies \[[M_d(y)]_{\alpha,\beta}=y_{\alpha+\beta}.\] Equivalently, \(L_y(p^2)=p^{\mathsf T}M_d(y)p\) for every coefficient vector of \(p\in\mathbb R[x]_d\). Hence positivity of the truncated functional on all such squares is exactly the semidefinite constraint \(M_d(y)\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The moment block is the Hankel-type matrix indexed by monomials; its positive semidefiniteness is equivalent to nonnegativity of the truncated functional on squares.
knowledge_statements.title: Moment-Matrix Blocks

children.title: Localizing-Matrix Blocks
children.top_down_role: Constraint-localized moment components of hierarchy levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Localizing-Matrix Blocks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint-localized moment block at a truncation-compatible order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\leq 2d}\) and write \(g(x)=\sum_\gamma g_\gamma x^\gamma\). Set \(r=d-\lceil\deg(g)/2\rceil\geq0\). The localizing matrix indexed by monomials of degree at most \(r\) is \[[M_r(gy)]_{\alpha,\beta}=\sum_\gamma g_\gamma y_{\alpha+\beta+\gamma}.\] For every \(p\in\mathbb R[x]_r\), one has \(L_y(gp^2)=p^{\mathsf T}M_r(gy)p\). Therefore \(M_r(gy)\succeq0\) if and only if \(L_y(gp^2)\geq0\) for every \(p\in\mathbb R[x]_r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A localizing block shifts moment entries by a constraint polynomial; its positive semidefiniteness is equivalent to nonnegativity of the truncated functional on every compatible product of that constraint with a square.
assumptions_latex: \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\leq2d}\) is a real truncated sequence and \(g\in\mathbb R[x]\).
\(r=d-\lceil\deg(g)/2\rceil\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_y(gp^2)\geq0\) for every \(p\in\mathbb R[x]_r\) if and only if \(M_r(gy)\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Localizing matrix for polynomial \(g\) and sequence \(y\).

children.title: Equality-Localizing Moment Blocks
children.top_down_role: Truncated moment blocks encoding polynomial equality constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(h\in\mathbb R[x]\), \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\leq2d}\), and \(r=d-\lceil\deg(h)/2\rceil\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_r(hy)=0\) if and only if \(L_y(hpq)=0\) for all \(p,q\in\mathbb R[x]_r\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero localizing blocks encoding polynomial equality constraints in a finite moment relaxation.

source_refs.locator: 3.2.1 Moment and localizing matrix p. 58
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an equality polynomial \(h(x)=\sum_\gamma h_\gamma x^\gamma\), define the compatible block by \[[M_r(hy)]_{\alpha,\beta}=\sum_\gamma h_\gamma y_{\alpha+\beta+\gamma},\qquad r=d-\left\lceil\frac{\deg(h)}2\right\rceil.\] The equality constraint at order \(d\) is \(M_r(hy)=0\). Entrywise, this is equivalent to \(L_y(hx^{\alpha+\beta})=0\) for all \(|\alpha|,|\beta|\leq r\), or, by bilinearity, to \(L_y(hpq)=0\) for every \(p,q\in\mathbb R[x]_r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equality is imposed on moments by setting its compatible localizing matrix to zero, equivalently annihilating all degree-admissible products containing the equality polynomial.
knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Localizing Moment Blocks

children.title: Quotient-Moment Representations
children.top_down_role: Moment data represented on polynomial quotient spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Quotient-Moment Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment functionals represented on a precisely defined finite-dimensional quotient by degree-visible equality relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbb R[x]_{2d}\) be the vector space of polynomials of degree at most \(2d\), let \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) be an ideal, and set \(I_{2d}=I\cap\mathbb R[x]_{2d}\). A linear functional \(L:\mathbb R[x]_{2d}\to\mathbb R\) induces a functional on the vector-space quotient \(\mathbb R[x]_{2d}/I_{2d}\) by \[\bar L([p])=L(p)\] if and only if \(L(q)=0\) for every \(q\in I_{2d}\). Indeed, two representatives \(p,q\in\mathbb R[x]_{2d}\) define the same class exactly when \(p-q\in I_{2d}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A truncated moment functional descends to the quotient by all degree-visible ideal relations exactly when it annihilates the intersection of the ideal with its polynomial degree domain.
assumptions_latex: \(d\in\mathbb N\), \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) is an ideal, and \(I_{2d}=I\cap\mathbb R[x]_{2d}\).
\(L:\mathbb R[x]_{2d}\to\mathbb R\) is linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rule \(\bar L([p])=L(p)\) is well defined on \(\mathbb R[x]_{2d}/I_{2d}\) if and only if \(L(q)=0\) for every \(q\in I_{2d}\).

notation.meaning: Finite-dimensional vector-space quotient by degree-visible ideal relations.
Class of \(p\) in the finite-dimensional quotient.

children.top_down_role: Relationship between equality-localizing blocks plus quotient-space moment models.

knowledge_statements.title: Localization–Quotient Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-order equivalence between zero equality-localizing blocks and a functional on the quotient by the relations represented by those blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_s\rangle\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\), let \(L_y\) be defined on \(\mathbb R[x]_{2d}\), and for every \(j\) with \(r_j=d-\lceil\deg(h_j)/2\rceil\geq0\) define \[W_d=\operatorname{span}\{h_jpq: p,q\in\mathbb R[x]_{r_j},\ j=1,\ldots,s,\ r_j\geq0\}\subseteq\mathbb R[x]_{2d}.\] All compatible equality-localizing blocks \(M_{r_j}(h_jy)\) vanish if and only if \(L_y(w)=0\) for every \(w\in W_d\). Equivalently, \(L_y\) induces a well-defined linear functional on the vector-space quotient \(\mathbb R[x]_{2d}/W_d\) by \[\bar L_y([p])=L_y(p).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero equality-localizing blocks are equivalent to annihilating exactly the equality relations represented by those blocks, and hence to a functional on the quotient by their span.
assumptions_latex: \(I=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_s\rangle\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) and \(L_y:\mathbb R[x]_{2d}\to\mathbb R\) is linear.
For every represented generator, \(r_j=d-\lceil\deg(h_j)/2\rceil\geq0\).
\(W_d=\operatorname{span}\{h_jpq:p,q\in\mathbb R[x]_{r_j}\}\), with the span taken over all represented generators.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{r_j}(h_jy)=0\) for every represented \(j\) if and only if \(L_y\) descends to \(\mathbb R[x]_{2d}/W_d\).

knowledge_statements.title: Moment-Degree Truncation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree compatibility for a moment relaxation of order \(d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), write \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), and let \(y=(y_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n,\ |\alpha|\le 2d}\). For \(p=\sum_{|\alpha|\le 2d}p_\alpha x^\alpha\in\mathbb R[x]_{2d}\), define \(L_y(p)=\sum_{|\alpha|\le 2d}p_\alpha y_\alpha\). The order-\(d\) moment matrix is \(M_d(y)=(y_{\alpha+\beta})_{|\alpha|,|\beta|\le d}\). Thus \(L_y\) is defined on polynomials of degree at most \(2d\), and every entry of \(M_d(y)\) uses an available moment because \(|\alpha+\beta|\le 2d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An order-d relaxation in n variables stores moments through degree 2d; these moments define the Riesz functional on degree-2d polynomials and every entry of the order-d moment matrix.

y=(y_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n,\ |\alpha|\le 2d}

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Order Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatible localizing-matrix block sizes at a fixed truncation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), and let \(y=(y_\gamma)_{\gamma\in\mathbb N^n,\ |\gamma|\le2d}\). For \(g_i\in\mathbb R[x]\), set \(d_i=\lceil\deg(g_i)/2\rceil\) and assume \(d\ge d_i\). The compatible localizing block is \(M_{d-d_i}(g_i y)\), indexed by monomials \(x^\alpha\) with \(|\alpha|\le d-d_i\), and its \((\alpha,\beta)\)-entry is \(L_y(g_i x^{\alpha+\beta})\). Since \(\deg(g_i x^{\alpha+\beta})\le\deg(g_i)+2(d-d_i)\le2d\), every entry uses only moments contained in \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a truncated moment sequence through degree 2d, a constraint with half-degree offset d_i uses a localizing block of order d−d_i, ensuring that every block entry requires only available moments.

g_i\in\mathbb R[x]
d_i=\lceil\deg(g_i)/2\rceil
d\ge d_i
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_{d-d_i}(g_i y)\text{ uses only }y_\gamma\text{ with }|\gamma|\le2d

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Degree Alignment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree rule for SOS multipliers in a truncated quadratic module.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), write \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), let \(g_0=1\), and let \(g_i\in\mathbb R[x]\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Set \(d_0=0\) and \(d_i=\lceil\deg(g_i)/2\rceil\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). At relaxation order \(d\ge\max_{0\le i\le m}d_i\), choose SOS multipliers \(\sigma_i\in\Sigma[x]\) satisfying \(\deg(\sigma_i)\le2(d-d_i)\). Then \(\deg(\sigma_i g_i)\le2d\) for every \(i=0,\ldots,m\), so an identity \(f-\gamma=\sum_{i=0}^m\sigma_i g_i\) is coefficientwise meaningful within degree \(2d\) whenever \(f\in\mathbb R[x]_{2d}\) and \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At order d, the SOS multiplier for generator g_i has degree at most 2(d−d_i), ensuring that every multiplier product has degree at most 2d.
assumptions_latex: n,m\in\mathbb N
g_0=1,\quad g_i\in\mathbb R[x]\ (i=1,\ldots,m)
d_0=0,\quad d_i=\lceil\deg(g_i)/2\rceil\ (i=1,\ldots,m)
d\ge\max_{0\le i\le m}d_i
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \deg\sigma_i\le2(d-d_i)\Longrightarrow\deg(\sigma_i g_i)\le2d\quad(i=0,\ldots,m)

knowledge_statements.title: Unconstrained Moment-SOS Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal moment and dual SOS bounds without a compactness-based convergence claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(n\in\mathbb N\), let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), take \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\), and let \(d\ge\lceil\deg(f)/2\rceil\). For a truncated sequence \(y=(y_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n,\ |\alpha|\le2d}\), let \(L_y\) be its Riesz functional and \(M_d(y)\) its order-\(d\) moment matrix. Define \(p_d^{\mathrm{mom}}=\inf\{L_y(f):y_0=1,\ M_d(y)\succeq0\}\) and \(p_d^{\mathrm{sos}}=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma\in\Sigma[x]_{2d}\}\). Weak SDP duality and point-evaluation moment sequences give \(p_d^{\mathrm{sos}}\le p_d^{\mathrm{mom}}\le\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\). Equality or convergence is not automatic on the noncompact domain \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an unconstrained polynomial in n variables, the positive-semidefinite moment relaxation and its SOS counterpart give lower bounds on the global infimum; noncompactness prevents an automatic convergence claim.
assumptions_latex: n\in\mathbb N
f\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]
d\ge\lceil\deg(f)/2\rceil
y=(y_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n,\ |\alpha|\le2d}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_d^{\mathrm{sos}}\le p_d^{\mathrm{mom}}\le\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Order-r Moment–SOS Algorithm with Flat-Rank Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fixed-order SDP procedure for a degree-2r unconstrained polynomial, with exactness and minimizer extraction conditional on existence of an SDP optimizer and moment-matrix rank stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given $f\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]$ with $\deg f=2r$, solve (5.6) for its value $\rho_r$ and, if attained, an optimizer $\mathbf y^*$. If $\mathbf y^*$ exists and $\operatorname{rank}M_{r-1}(\mathbf y^*)=\operatorname{rank}M_r(\mathbf y^*)$, then $f^*=\rho_r$ and at least $\operatorname{rank}M_r(\mathbf y^*)$ global minimizers can be extracted using Algorithm 4.2. Otherwise, the certified conclusion is only $\rho_r\le f^*$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the order-r moment SDP. When an optimizer exists, stabilization of the final two moment-matrix ranks certifies exactness and permits extraction of at least as many global minimizers as the stabilized rank. Without that certificate, the SDP value is only a lower bound.
assumptions_latex: f\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x],\quad \deg f=2r
\text{The flat-rank test requires an optimizer }\mathbf y^*\text{ of (5.6)}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf y^*\in\operatorname{argmin}(5.6),\ \operatorname{rank}M_{r-1}(\mathbf y^*)=\operatorname{rank}M_r(\mathbf y^*)\Longrightarrow f^*=\rho_r\ \text{and at least }\operatorname{rank}M_r(\mathbf y^*)\text{ global minimizers are extractable};\quad\text{otherwise only }\rho_r\le f^*\text{ is certified}.

knowledge_statements.title: Putinar-Type Constrained Hierarchy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic-module hierarchy under the Archimedean hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), let \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), and set \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\). Put \(g_0=1\), \(d_0=0\), and \(d_i=\lceil\deg(g_i)/2\rceil\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). For \(d\ge\max\{\lceil\deg(f)/2\rceil,d_1,\ldots,d_m\}\), the moment relaxation minimizes \(L_y(f)\) subject to \(y_0=1\) and \(M_{d-d_i}(g_i y)\succeq0\) for \(i=0,\ldots,m\). Its SOS counterpart maximizes \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\) subject to \(f-\gamma=\sum_{i=0}^m\sigma_i g_i\), where each \(\sigma_i\) is SOS and \(\deg(\sigma_i g_i)\le2d\). If \(K\ne\varnothing\) and the quadratic module \(M(g)\) is Archimedean, the resulting lower bounds \(p_d\) increase to \(\min_{x\in K}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Putinar’s hierarchy uses one SOS multiplier and one localizing matrix per defining inequality. At every admissible order it gives a lower bound, and under an Archimedean quadratic module these bounds converge upward to the minimum.
assumptions_latex: n,m\in\mathbb N
K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\ne\varnothing
f,g_i\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]
M(g)\text{ is Archimedean}
d\ge\max\{\lceil\deg(f)/2\rceil,d_1,\ldots,d_m\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_d\uparrow\min_{x\in K}f(x)

children.title: Relaxation-Order Filtration
children.top_down_role: Nested degree organization connecting successive hierarchy levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Order Filtration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested primal and dual degree truncations across hierarchy levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), let \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), put \(g_0=1\), and define \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(f^*=\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\). For every admissible order \(d\), let \(Q_d(g)=\{\sum_{i=0}^m\sigma_i g_i:\sigma_i\text{ is SOS and }\deg(\sigma_i g_i)\le2d\}\). Then \(Q_d(g)\subseteq Q_{d+1}(g)\), so \(p_d=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma\in Q_d(g)\}\) satisfies \(p_d\le p_{d+1}\le f^*\). On the moment side, if an order-\(d+1\) sequence satisfies all moment and localizing-matrix constraints of the quadratic-module relaxation, its restriction to moments of degree at most \(2d\) satisfies the corresponding order-\(d\) constraints. Thus increasing the order preserves all earlier constraints while adding higher-degree moments and semidefinite conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive quadratic-module hierarchy levels are nested: truncated modules expand, lower bounds increase, and every higher-order feasible moment sequence restricts to a feasible lower-order sequence.
assumptions_latex: n,m\in\mathbb N
f,g_i\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]
K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}
d\text{ is admissible for all displayed truncations}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q_d(g)\subseteq Q_{d+1}(g),\qquad p_d\le p_{d+1}\le f^*

knowledge_statements.title: Homogeneous-Form Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sphere-normalized hierarchy for an even-degree homogeneous form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be a homogeneous form of degree \(2m\), and set \(s(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2\). Since \(f(tx)=t^{2m}f(x)\), normalized minimization is \(f^*=\min\{f(x):s(x)=1\}\). At order \(d\ge m\), a valid SOS lower bound maximizes \(\gamma\) subject to \(f-\gamma s^m=\sigma+q(1-s)\), where \(\sigma\) is SOS, \(\deg\sigma\le2d\), and \(\deg(q(1-s))\le2d\). Every feasible \(\gamma\) satisfies \(\gamma\le f^*\); increasing \(d\) enlarges the certificate space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogeneity reduces optimization to the unit sphere. Degree-truncated SOS certificates modulo the sphere equation produce nested valid lower bounds for the normalized minimum.
assumptions_latex: f\in\mathbb R[x]\text{ is homogeneous of degree }2m
d\ge m
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f-\gamma s^m=\sigma+q(1-s)\Longrightarrow\gamma\le\min_{s(x)=1}f(x)

knowledge_statements.title: Univariate Domain Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact univariate positivity representations underlying line and interval hierarchies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p\in\mathbb R[x]\), nonnegativity on \(\mathbb R\) is equivalent to \(p\) being SOS. On \([a,b]\), if \(\deg p=2k\), then \(p\ge0\) is equivalent to \(p=\sigma_0+(x-a)(b-x)\sigma_1\) with \(\deg\sigma_0\le2k\) and \(\deg\sigma_1\le2k-2\); if \(\deg p=2k+1\), it is equivalent to \(p=(x-a)\sigma_0+(b-x)\sigma_1\) with \(\deg\sigma_i\le2k\). On \([a,\infty)\), it is equivalent to \(p=\sigma_0+(x-a)\sigma_1\), with SOS \(\sigma_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the line, intervals, and half-lines, nonnegative univariate polynomials have exact SOS-weighted representations, yielding specialized hierarchies with explicit degree control.
assumptions_latex: p\in\mathbb R[x]
a<b
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\ge0\text{ on the stated domain}\Longleftrightarrow p\text{ has the displayed SOS representation}

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Variety Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convergence in the coordinate ring of a finite real variety.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\subset\mathbb R^n\) be finite and let \(I=I(V)\). There exist interpolation polynomials \(\delta_v\) satisfying \(\delta_v(w)=1\) for \(w=v\) and \(0\) otherwise. Hence every polynomial \(p\) nonnegative on \(V\) obeys \(p\equiv\sum_{v\in V}p(v)\delta_v^2\pmod I\). Consequently, for every objective \(f\), an SOS hierarchy formulated in \(\mathbb R[x]/I\) becomes exact once its truncation includes the interpolation polynomials and the congruence, yielding \(\min_{v\in V}f(v)\) at a finite order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite real variety, interpolation expresses every nonnegative function as a sum of squares modulo its vanishing ideal, so the quotient SOS hierarchy is finitely exact.
assumptions_latex: V\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ is finite}
I=I(V)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p|_V\ge0\Longrightarrow p\equiv\sum_{v\in V}p(v)\delta_v^2\pmod I

notation.meaning: polynomial indicator of v on V

knowledge_statements.title: Boolean Quotient Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lasserre hierarchy in the Boolean coordinate ring.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_B=\langle x_i^2-x_i:i=1,\ldots,n\rangle\). At level \(d\), a Boolean pseudoexpectation is a linear functional \(L\) on quotient polynomials of degree at most \(2d\) satisfying \(L(1)=1\) and \(L(q^2)\ge0\) for every quotient polynomial \(q\) of degree at most \(d\). Minimizing \(L(f)\) gives a lower bound for \(\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}f(x)\). At \(d=n\), the Boolean indicator polynomials are available, positivity assigns them nonnegative masses summing to one, and the relaxation is exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boolean equations reduce all polynomials to multilinear form. Positive quotient pseudoexpectations give Lasserre bounds, and level n is exact because all Boolean point indicators are present.
assumptions_latex: I_B=\langle x_i^2-x_i:i=1,\ldots,n\rangle
f\in\mathbb R[x]/I_B
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_n^{\mathrm{Bool}}=\min_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}f(x)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Boolean quotient pseudoexpectation construction and exactness by level n are plausible, but the record supplies no authoritative source or locator for the exactness level.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain Lasserre Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quotient hierarchy for a Cartesian product of finite scalar domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_i\subset\mathbb R\) be finite, set \(D=\prod_{i=1}^nD_i\), and let \(I_D=\langle h_i(x_i):h_i(t)=\prod_{a\in D_i}(t-a)\rangle\). Every quotient class has a representative with \(\deg_{x_i}<|D_i|\). Writing \(S=\sum_i(|D_i|-1)\), the point indicators \(\delta_u\) have degree at most \(S\), and every \(p\ge0\) on \(D\) satisfies \(p\equiv\sum_{u\in D}p(u)\delta_u^2\pmod{I_D}\). Therefore the quotient Lasserre hierarchy is exact by order \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a product of finite scalar domains, quotient reduction bounds coordinate degrees. Point-indicator squares show that the Lasserre hierarchy is exact by an explicit finite order.
assumptions_latex: D_i\subset\mathbb R\text{ is finite and nonempty}
D=\prod_{i=1}^nD_i
S=\sum_i(|D_i|-1)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_S^{D}=\min_{u\in D}f(u)

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete-Domain Specialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quotient-ring moment relaxation over a finite real algebraic domain using its vanishing ideal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty finite set, let \(I(D)=\{p\in\mathbb R[x]:p(u)=0\text{ for every }u\in D\}=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_s\rangle\), and let \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\). At order \(d\), define \(\rho_d\) as the minimum of \(L_y(f)\) subject to \(y_0=1\), \(M_d(y)\succeq0\), and \(L_y(x^\alpha h_j)=0\) whenever \(|\alpha|+\deg h_j\le 2d\). Its dual value is \(\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma\in\Sigma[x]_{2d}+I(D)_{2d}\}\). Because \(D\) is finite, there exists \(d_0\) such that, for every \(d\ge d_0\), both values equal \(\min_{u\in D}f(u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using the real vanishing ideal of a nonempty finite domain, the quotient-ring moment and SOS relaxations become exact at all sufficiently large truncation orders.

\(I(D)=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_s\rangle\) is the real vanishing ideal of \(D\).
\(f\in\mathbb R[x]\).

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Polynomial Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree-two moment lifting for quadratically constrained quadratic optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For quadratic polynomials \(f(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Q_0x+2q_0^{\mathsf T}x+c_0\) and \(g_i(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Q_ix+2q_i^{\mathsf T}x+c_i\), introduce \(X\) for \(xx^{\mathsf T}\). The degree-two moment relaxation is the SDP minimizing \(\langle Q_0,X\rangle+2q_0^{\mathsf T}x+c_0\), subject to \(\langle Q_i,X\rangle+2q_i^{\mathsf T}x+c_i\ge0\) and \(\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\). It is obtained by dropping the nonconvex constraint \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\), equivalently the rank-one condition on the lifted matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratically constrained quadratic problem lifts to an SDP by replacing the rank-one matrix xxᵀ with a positive-semidefinite matrix variable.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_i\in\mathbb S^n\), \(q_i\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(c_i\in\mathbb R\).
The feasible set is defined by \(g_i(x)\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{\mathrm{SDP}}\le\inf\{f(x):g_i(x)\ge0\}\).

notation.meaning: real symmetric n by n matrices

knowledge_statements.title: First-Level SDP Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-one moment relaxation for quadratic objectives and constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given quadratic \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\), the first moment-SOS relaxation uses moments \(y_\alpha\) for \(|\alpha|\le2\). Its primal form minimizes \(L_y(f)\) subject to \(y_0=1\), \(M_1(y)\succeq0\), and \(L_y(g_i)\ge0\). Its dual form maximizes \(\gamma\) subject to \(f-\gamma=\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i g_i\), where \(\sigma_0\) is a quadratic sum of squares and \(\lambda_i\ge0\). Under strict primal or dual feasibility, these two SDP values coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The first SOS level replaces quadratic feasibility by a degree-two moment matrix, with a dual certificate using a quadratic SOS and nonnegative scalar multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and every \(g_i\) have degree at most two.
At least one side of the resulting primal-dual SDP is strictly feasible for strong duality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_1=\sup\{\gamma:f-\gamma=\sigma_0+\sum_i\lambda_i g_i,\ \sigma_0\in\Sigma[x]_2,\ \lambda_i\ge0\}\le f^*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic–SDP Equivalence Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact quadratic lifting and a merely lower-bounding SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a quadratically constrained quadratic problem, the lifted SDP is exact whenever it has an optimal matrix \(Y^*=\begin{pmatrix}1&(x^*)^{\mathsf T}\\x^*&X^*\end{pmatrix}\) of rank one, because then \(X^*=x^*(x^*)^{\mathsf T}\). Without rank-one recovery, equality need not hold. For example, minimizing \(-x_1x_2\) subject to \(x_1^2=1\) and \(x_2^2=1\) is exact, but adding general quadratic constraints does not ensure that every feasible lifted matrix is a convex combination of feasible rank-one matrices; consequently an SDP gap may occur unless an exactness condition is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic lifting is exact when an optimal lifted matrix has rank one; general quadratic constraints alone do not guarantee this, so relaxation gaps may occur.
assumptions_latex: The SDP is the standard degree-two lift of a quadratically constrained quadratic problem.
An optimal SDP solution exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}Y^*=1\Rightarrow\rho_{\mathrm{SDP}}=f^*\); absent rank-one recovery or another exactness theorem, only \(\rho_{\mathrm{SDP}}\le f^*\) is guaranteed.

children.title: Gradient-Ideal Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Unconstrained hierarchies strengthened by critical-point ideals.

knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Ideal Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained SOS hierarchy restricted to the polynomial critical-point variety.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) and define the gradient ideal \(I_\nabla f=\langle \partial f/\partial x_1,\ldots,\partial f/\partial x_n\rangle\). The order-\(d\) gradient-ideal bound is \(\rho_d=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma\in\Sigma[x]_{2d}+(I_\nabla f)_{2d}\}\). Its moment dual imposes \(M_d(y)\succeq0\), \(y_0=1\), and \(L_y(x^\alpha\partial f/\partial x_i)=0\) for all products of degree at most \(2d\). It targets the minimum of \(f\) over its real critical variety.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gradient-ideal hierarchy adds the equations ∇f=0 to SOS relaxations, restricting certificates and moments to critical points of an unconstrained polynomial.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\).
The global minimizers under consideration are attained critical points of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_d\le\min\{f(x):x\in V_{\mathbb R}(I_\nabla f)\}\), and \(\rho_d\) is nondecreasing with \(d\).

notation.meaning: ideal generated by the partial derivatives of f
real variety of an ideal I

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically plausible and fits the container, but no inspectable source supports the precise truncated hierarchy or monotonicity claim.

children.title: KKT Multiplier Hierarchy Family
children.top_down_role: Constrained hierarchy families incorporating polynomial optimality systems.

children.title: KKT-Ideal Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Hierarchy architectures built from polynomial KKT ideals.

knowledge_statements.title: KKT-Ideal Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment-SOS hierarchy on the polynomial KKT variety in primal-multiplier space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\ge0\) and \(h_j(x)=0\), introduce multipliers \(\lambda_i\) and \(\mu_j\). The KKT ideal in \(\mathbb R[x,\lambda,\mu]\) is generated by \(
abla f-\sum_i\lambda_i
abla g_i-\sum_j\mu_j
abla h_j\), the products \(\lambda_i g_i\), and the equations \(h_j\). A KKT-ideal hierarchy applies truncated moment-SOS relaxations to these equations together with \(g_i\ge0\) and \(\lambda_i\ge0\), thereby optimizing \(f\) over polynomially encoded KKT points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A KKT-ideal hierarchy introduces multiplier variables and imposes stationarity, complementarity, equality feasibility, primal inequalities, and multiplier nonnegativity in moment-SOS relaxations.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_i,h_j\in\mathbb R[x]\).
The selected sign convention is \(g_i\ge0\) with \(\lambda_i\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_d^{\mathrm{KKT}}\le\inf\{f(x):(x,\lambda,\mu)\text{ satisfies the encoded KKT system}\}\).

notation.meaning: multiplier for inequality g_i greater than or equal to zero
multiplier for equality h_j equal to zero
ideal generated by stationarity, complementarity, and equality equations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The polynomial KKT encoding is consistent with the stated sign convention, but the hierarchy and bound require an authoritative, specifically located source.

children.title: Multiplier-Expression Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Hierarchy architectures using polynomial expressions for optimization multipliers.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Expression Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT hierarchy after polynomially expressing multipliers in the primal variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose polynomial maps \(p_i(x)\) and \(q_j(x)\) satisfy \(\lambda_i=p_i(x)\) and \(\mu_j=q_j(x)\) at every relevant KKT point. Substitution produces a primal-variable criticality ideal generated by \(
abla f-\sum_i p_i
abla g_i-\sum_j q_j
abla h_j\), \(p_i g_i\), and \(h_j\), with inequalities \(g_i\ge0\) and \(p_i\ge0\). Applying moment-SOS relaxations to this substituted system yields a multiplier-expression hierarchy without independent multiplier variables while preserving every KKT point on which the expressions are valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When KKT multipliers are polynomial functions of x, substituting those functions gives an equivalent primal-variable SOS hierarchy on the relevant KKT set.
assumptions_latex: Polynomial multiplier expressions \(p_i,q_j\in\mathbb R[x]\) are valid at every relevant KKT point.
The original constraints and objective are polynomial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_x(V_{\mathbb R}(I_{\mathrm{KKT}}))\subseteq V_{\mathbb R}(I_{\mathrm{expr}})\), with equality on the regime where the multiplier expressions are valid.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The assumption covers only relevant KKT points, whereas the conclusion asserts an inclusion for the entire projected KKT variety. A source and a precise definition of the validity locus are needed before correcting the mathematical scope.

children.title: Multiplier-Elimination Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes connecting explicit multipliers to eliminated optimality ideals.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Elimination Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic conditions permitting elimination of KKT multipliers without losing relevant critical points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_{\mathrm{KKT}}\subset\mathbb R[x,\lambda,\mu]\) encode the KKT equations, and let \(J=I_{\mathrm{KKT}}\cap\mathbb R[x]\) be its elimination ideal. Multiplier elimination is lossless for relevant real critical points when \(V_{\mathbb R}(J)=\overline{\pi_x(V_{\mathbb R}(I_{\mathrm{KKT}}))}^{\mathrm{Zar}}\) introduces no additional feasible component attaining a smaller objective value. A sufficient expression regime is that the active-constraint gradient matrix has full column rank throughout the relevant locus and admits polynomial or denominator-nonvanishing rational formulas for the multipliers; denominators must be excluded by saturation before constructing the primal-variable hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KKT multipliers may be eliminated when projection adds no harmful feasible components; full-rank active gradients and valid saturated multiplier formulas provide a sufficient regime.
assumptions_latex: \(I_{\mathrm{KKT}}\) is a polynomial ideal in primal and multiplier variables.
Any rational multiplier denominator is nonzero on the relevant locus and is handled by saturation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{(x,\lambda,\mu)\in V_{\mathbb R}(I_{\mathrm{KKT}})}f(x)=\inf_{x\in V_{\mathbb R}(J)\cap K}f(x)\) whenever elimination introduces no lower-valued feasible component.

notation.meaning: elimination ideal in the primal variables

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed equality optimizes over the full real KKT ideal variety on the left without imposing the primal inequalities or multiplier signs. The real-projection and saturation assertions also require a precise elimination theorem.

children.title: Criticality-Variety Hierarchies

children.title: Jacobian-Ideal Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Criticality-based hierarchy architectures using Jacobian ideals.

knowledge_statements.title: Jacobian-Ideal Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criticality hierarchy using Jacobian rank equations for active constraint subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For minimizing \(f\) on \(K=\{x:h_j(x)=0,\ g_i(x)\ge0\}\), form, for each admissible active set \(A\), the Jacobian matrix whose columns are \(
abla f\), \(
abla h_j\), and \(
abla g_i\) for \(i\in A\). Criticality is encoded by its maximal minors, multiplied when necessary by \(\prod_{i
otin A}g_i\) to localize the active-set alternative. A Jacobian-ideal hierarchy adds these polynomial equations to the moment-SOS relaxation of \(K\), restricting feasible moments to the resulting criticality variety.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Jacobian-ideal hierarchy adds minors expressing dependence between the objective gradient and active constraint gradients, thereby restricting moments to critical points.
assumptions_latex: \(f,h_j,g_i\in\mathbb R[x]\).
Active-set minors are chosen with sizes compatible with the number of equality and active inequality gradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_d^{\mathrm{Jac}}\le\inf\{f(x):x\in K\cap V_{\mathbb R}(I_{\mathrm{Jac}})\}\), with bounds nondecreasing in \(d\).

notation.meaning: ideal generated by the selected Jacobian criticality equations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The general idea fits a Jacobian-ideal hierarchy, but “admissible active set,” minor sizes, and inactive-constraint products do not specify a unique valid construction. An authoritative formulation is required.

children.title: Determinantal Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Hierarchy architectures based on minors encoding criticality structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Determinantal Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment-SOS hierarchies strengthened by polynomial rank constraints expressed through minors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A(x)\in\mathbb R[x]^{p\times q}\) be a polynomial matrix whose rank must not exceed \(r\) on the target criticality locus. Define the determinantal ideal \(I_{r+1}(A)\) generated by all \((r+1)\times(r+1)\) minors of \(A(x)\). A determinantal hierarchy augments each order-\(d\) moment relaxation with \(L_y(x^\alpha m(x))=0\) for every generator \(m\in I_{r+1}(A)\) and every product of degree at most \(2d\). Its dual adds the truncated ideal \(I_{r+1}(A)_{2d}\) to the SOS certificate cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A determinantal hierarchy encodes a polynomial matrix rank bound by adding its oversized minors as ideal equations in primal moments and dual SOS certificates.
assumptions_latex: \(A(x)\) is a polynomial matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_{\mathbb R}(I_{r+1}(A))=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\operatorname{rank}A(x)\le r\}\).

notation.meaning: ideal of all minors of size r+1
polynomial matrix encoding the relevant gradients or constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The determinantal rank identity and moment constraints are standard and internally consistent, but the proposed hierarchy has no cited source.

children.title: Rank-Degeneracy Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Geometric regimes where determinantal criticality descriptions become degenerate.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Degeneracy Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of nominal Jacobian-minor encodings when constraint gradients have unexpected rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Jacobian criticality encoding based on a nominal constraint rank \(s\) is reliable only on strata where the selected constraint-gradient matrix has that rank. If its rank drops below \(s\), all nominal maximal minors may vanish independently of stationarity, so the determinantal variety acquires an extraneous singular component. Conversely, if more constraints are active than the selected minor system represents, genuine critical points may be omitted. Correct treatment requires rank stratification, active-set enumeration, or saturation by minors defining the intended full-rank locus before applying the moment-SOS hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unexpected Jacobian rank loss makes nominal minors vanish automatically and creates extraneous components; unrepresented active sets can instead omit genuine critical points.
assumptions_latex: Criticality is encoded using minors chosen for a nominal active-gradient rank.
The feasible set may contain points where this rank changes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}G(x)<s\Rightarrow\text{all }s\text{-minors of }G(x)\text{ vanish without certifying the intended stationarity condition}\).

notation.meaning: nominal rank used by the minor construction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Automatic vanishing under rank loss is correct, but whether genuine critical points are omitted depends on the exact active-set and minor construction. The boundary formulation needs a specifically located source.

children.title: Putinar-Type Tight Variants
children.top_down_role: Tight hierarchy variants based on quadratic-module certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Putinar-Type Tight Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Archimedean quadratic-module certificates strengthened by valid criticality equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x:g_i(x)\ge0,\ h_j(x)=0\}\), let \(I_C\) be an ideal of valid criticality equations, and assume the quadratic module generated by the \(g_i\), modulo \(\langle h\rangle+I_C\), is Archimedean. For every polynomial \(p\) strictly positive on \(K\cap V_{\mathbb R}(I_C)\), a Putinar-type tight certificate has the form \(p=\sigma_0+\sum_i\sigma_i g_i+u+v\), where each \(\sigma_i\) is SOS, \(u\in\langle h_1,\ldots,h_t\rangle\), and \(v\in I_C\). Degree truncation produces strengthened SDP bounds converging to the minimum over the criticality-restricted feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under an Archimedean condition, positivity on the feasible criticality variety is certified by an SOS quadratic module plus equality and criticality ideals.
assumptions_latex: The quadratic module modulo \(\langle h\rangle+I_C\) is Archimedean.
\(p>0\) on \(K\cap V_{\mathbb R}(I_C)\).
Every equation in \(I_C\) is valid on the targeted minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\in\Sigma[x]+\sum_i\Sigma[x]g_i+\langle h\rangle+I_C\).

children.title: Certificate-System Strength Comparison
children.top_down_role: Structural comparison of tight variants across the two certificate systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-System Strength Comparison
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic strength comparison at a fixed order with identical optimality augmentation and truncation conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_r(g)\) be the order-\(r\) truncated quadratic module, let \(T_r(g)\) be the order-\(r\) truncated preordering using the same degree convention, and let \(I_{2r}(h)\) be the common truncated augmentation ideal. Then \[Q_r(g)+I_{2r}(h)\subseteq T_r(g)+I_{2r}(h).\] For \[\rho_r^{\mathrm{Put},h}:=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma\in Q_r(g)+I_{2r}(h)\}\] and \[\rho_r^{\mathrm{Sch},h}:=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma\in T_r(g)+I_{2r}(h)\},\] one has \[\rho_r^{\mathrm{Put},h}\le \rho_r^{\mathrm{Sch},h}\le f^*.\] The Schmüdgen formulation may contain SOS multiplier blocks for up to \(2^m\) square-free products of the \(m\) inequality generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With identical augmentation and degree conventions, the Schmüdgen certificate cone contains the Putinar cone, so its bound is at least as strong and remains a lower bound when the augmentation preserves a global minimizer; it may use up to 2^m product multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m,h_1,\ldots,h_s\in\mathbb R[x]\), and \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\).
The minimum \(f^*=\min_{x\in K}f(x)\) is attained at some \(x^*\in K\) satisfying \(h_\ell(x^*)=0\) for \(\ell=1,\ldots,s\).
The Putinar and Schmüdgen variants use the same augmentation ideal, relaxation order, and termwise degree-truncation convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_r^{\mathrm{Put},h}\le\rho_r^{\mathrm{Sch},h}\le f^*\).

children.title: Measure Optimization View

knowledge_statements.title: Measure Optimization View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact generalized-moment reformulation using probability measures supported on the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P(K)\) denote the Borel probability measures supported on \(K\). Then \[f^*:=\min_{x\in K}f(x)=\min_{\mu\in\mathcal P(K)}\int_K f(x)\,d\mu(x).\] If \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K}f(x)\), then \(\delta_{x^*}\) is an optimal measure. For the moments \(y_\alpha:=\int_Kx^\alpha\,d\mu(x)\), the objective is \(L_y(f)\) and the probability-mass constraint is \(y_0=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing a polynomial on a nonempty compact set is equivalent to minimizing its expectation over supported probability measures, and a Dirac measure at any global minimizer is optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and compact.
\(f\in\mathbb R[x]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in K}f(x)=\min_{\mu\in\mathcal P(K)}\int_K f\,d\mu\), and an optimal Dirac measure exists.

notation.meaning: Borel probability measures supported on the feasible set.
Dirac probability measure concentrated at x.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Polynomial Dual View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite-dimensional dual expressed through exact nonnegativity on the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\operatorname{Pos}(K):=\{p\in\mathbb R[x]:p(x)\ge0\text{ for every }x\in K\}.\] The exact positive-polynomial lower-bound problem is \[\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma\in\operatorname{Pos}(K)\}=f^*.\] The supremum is attained at \(\gamma=f^*\), and this problem is dual to optimization over Borel probability measures supported on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The global minimum is the largest scalar whose subtraction from the objective produces a polynomial nonnegative everywhere on the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and compact.
\(f\in\mathbb R[x]\), and \(f^*=\min_{x\in K}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f^*=\max\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma\in\operatorname{Pos}(K)\}\).

Global minimum of the objective on the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Moment Hierarchy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard basic-closed-set moment relaxation with localizing-matrix constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write \(g_j(x)=\sum_\gamma(g_j)_\gamma x^\gamma\), and define \(d_j:=\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\). For \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le2r}\), define \(L_y(p):=\sum_\alpha p_\alpha y_\alpha\), \([M_r(y)]_{\alpha,\beta}:=y_{\alpha+\beta}\), and \([M_{r-d_j}(g_jy)]_{\alpha,\beta}:=\sum_\gamma(g_j)_\gamma y_{\alpha+\beta+\gamma}\) on their natural monomial index sets. The order-\(r\) primal moment relaxation is \[p_r:=\inf_{y\in\mathbb R^{\mathbb N^n_{2r}}}\bigl\{L_y(f):y_0=1,\ M_r(y)\succeq0,\ M_{r-d_j}(g_jy)\succeq0\text{ for }j=1,\ldots,m\bigr\}.\] Its values satisfy \[p_r\le p_{r+1}\le f^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each admissible order, the primal hierarchy minimizes the objective over normalized truncated sequences whose moment and localizing matrices are positive semidefinite; its optimal values are nondecreasing lower bounds on the global minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), and \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) is nonempty.
\(f^*=\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\) is finite.
\(r\ge\max\{\lceil\deg(f)/2\rceil,d_1,\ldots,d_m\}\), where \(d_j=\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\).

Localizing matrix associated with the inequality polynomial g_j.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual SOS Lower-Bound Hierarchy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Putinar-type finite-level dual paired with the standard localizing-matrix relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(g_0:=1\) and define \[Q_r(g):=\left\{\sum_{j=0}^m\sigma_jg_j:\sigma_j\in\Sigma[x],\ \deg(\sigma_jg_j)\le2r\text{ for }j=0,\ldots,m\right\}.\] The order-\(r\) SOS lower-bound problem is \[d_r:=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma\in Q_r(g)\}.\] The hierarchy satisfies \[d_r\le d_{r+1}\le f^*.\] For the correspondingly truncated primal moment relaxation with value \(p_r\), weak conic duality gives \(d_r\le p_r\); equality holds under an applicable finite-dimensional conic regularity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each dual level maximizes a lower bound certified by membership of the objective gap in a truncated quadratic module; these bounds increase with the order and do not exceed the paired primal value or the global infimum.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), and \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) is nonempty.
\(f^*=\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\) is finite.
The order \(r\) is large enough that \(f\) and every permitted multiplier product have degree at most \(2r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_r\le d_{r+1}\le f^*\) and \(d_r\le p_r\).

knowledge_statements.title: Truncated Moment Cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representable, rather than merely moment-matrix-positive, truncated sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbb N^n_{2r}:=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n:|\alpha|\le2r\}\), and let \(\mathcal M_{+,2r}(K)\) be the finite nonnegative Borel measures supported on \(K\) whose absolute moments are finite through degree \(2r\). Define \[\mathcal R_{2r}(K):=\left\{y\in\mathbb R^{\mathbb N^n_{2r}}:\exists\mu\in\mathcal M_{+,2r}(K)\text{ such that }y_\alpha=\int_Kx^\alpha\,d\mu(x)\text{ for every }\alpha\in\mathbb N^n_{2r}\right\}.\] The set \(\mathcal R_{2r}(K)\) is a convex cone, and its slice \(y_0=1\) consists exactly of truncated moment sequences of Borel probability measures in \(\mathcal M_{+,2r}(K)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The truncated moment cone consists of moment sequences through degree 2r of supported nonnegative measures having finite moments through that degree; its normalized slice represents probability measures.

\(r\in\mathbb N\).

children.title: Strict-Feasibility Regimes
children.top_down_role: Hierarchy levels admitting standard conic regularity.

assumptions_latex: The order-\(r\) relaxation is a finite-dimensional primal-dual conic pair with finite optimal value.
At least one side has a feasible point satisfying all affine constraints and lying in the relative interior of its cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The order-\(r\) primal and dual values are equal, and the optimum on the opposite side is attained under the standard Slater theorem.

notation.meaning: Affine constraint map of the conic formulation.
Closed convex cone used by the finite-level relaxation.
Relative interior of a convex set.

review_flags: a hierarchy-specific conic-regularity source is required
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-level Slater regularity, stated relative to the cone's affine hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a primal conic level \(\inf\{\langle c,z\rangle:\mathcal A z=b,\ z\in C\}\), primal strict feasibility means that there exists \(\bar z\in\operatorname{ri}(C)\) with \(\mathcal A\bar z=b\). In a moment SDP this requires a normalized sequence satisfying the linear equations with every nonstructurally-zero moment and localizing block positive definite on its natural subspace. Dually, strict feasibility means that some dual slack belongs to the relative interior of \(C^*\). Under the usual finite-dimensional Slater hypotheses and finiteness, strict feasibility of one side excludes a duality gap and guarantees attainment on the opposite side.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A level is strictly feasible when its affine constraints meet the relative interior of the conic domain; standard Slater assumptions then give zero gap and opposite-side attainment.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Feasibility Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the appropriate kind, but the statement does not distinguish precisely between primal and dual strict feasibility, which side must have a finite optimum, and which opposite-side attainment conclusion follows. The hierarchy-specific positive-definiteness characterization also requires an inspectable conic-duality source.

children.top_down_role: Hierarchy levels supported on proper semidefinite faces.

children.title: Empty-Interior Regimes
children.top_down_role: Finite-level conic models lacking ambient strict feasibility.

assumptions_latex: \(F=\{z\in C:\mathcal A z=b\}\) is the feasible set of a finite-dimensional conic relaxation.
\(C\) is a closed convex cone and \(F\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime has empty ambient interior when \(F\cap\operatorname{ri}(C)=\varnothing\), equivalently when Slater feasibility fails relative to \(C\).

notation.meaning: Feasible affine slice of the conic relaxation.

review_flags: source for the intended moment-SOS empty-interior taxonomy is required
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of strict feasibility in the original cone, without asserting a duality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An order-\(r\) conic relaxation is in an empty-interior regime when its feasible affine slice satisfies
\[F\cap\operatorname{ri}(C)=\varnothing.\]
For a semidefinite moment formulation, this means every feasible tuple of moment and localizing matrices is singular on at least one subspace not forced solely by the chosen ambient representation. Feasibility may nevertheless hold, because \(F\) can lie entirely in a proper face of \(C\). Empty interior invalidates direct use of Slater's condition in the original cone, but by itself implies neither a positive primal-dual gap nor failure of attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The feasible slice is nonempty but misses the cone's relative interior, so every feasible SDP representation lies on a proper face and ordinary Slater regularity fails.
knowledge_statements.title: Empty-Interior Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed condition characterizes failure of relative Slater feasibility, not “empty ambient interior”: an affine feasible slice can have empty ambient interior while still meeting the cone's relative interior. A source defining the intended moment-SOS regime is required before choosing and correcting the precise formulation.

children.title: Minimal-Face Regimes
children.top_down_role: Hierarchy levels supported on proper semidefinite faces.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a nonempty convex feasible set contained in a closed convex cone \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\min}=\bigcap\{G:G\unlhd C,\ F\subseteq G\}\) is the unique minimal face of \(C\) containing \(F\).

notation.meaning: G is a face of C.
Minimal face of the ambient cone containing the feasible set.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: minimal-face construction in finite-dimensional conic geometry
source for the hierarchy-specific facial-reduction regime is required
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic relaxation restricted to the smallest face supporting all feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The minimal face supporting the feasible set is
\[C_{\min}:=\bigcap\{G:G\unlhd C\ \text{and}\ F\subseteq G\}.\]
In finite dimensions this intersection is a face and is the unique smallest face of \(C\) containing \(F\). A relaxation is in a minimal-face regime when its conic model is regarded over \(C_{\min}\) rather than over \(C\). If \(F\cap\operatorname{ri}(C)=\varnothing\) but \(F\cap\operatorname{ri}(C_{\min})\ne\varnothing\), strict feasibility fails in the original cone yet is restored after restriction to the minimal face, without changing the feasible set or objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimal face is the smallest face of the ambient cone containing every feasible point; restricting to it can restore relative-interior feasibility without changing values.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimal-Face Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The minimal-face definition is standard and definition is an appropriate kind, but no source supports the hierarchy-specific regime or the stated restoration of strict feasibility after restriction. An inspectable facial-reduction or conic-geometry source is required.

children.title: Facial-Reduction Interface
children.top_down_role: Structural use of supporting faces in irregular hierarchy levels.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional inner-product space.
The conic system \(Ax=b,\ x\in K\) is feasible, with minimal containing face \(F\unlhd K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing \(K\) by \(F\) preserves the feasible set and primal value, while dualizing over \(\operatorname{span}F\) can restore relative strict feasibility.

notation.meaning: Minimal face of the cone containing every feasible primal point.
Dual cone of the reduced face in its linear span.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(p^*=\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\), and let \(F\) be the unique minimal face of \(K\) containing \(\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\). Then
\[
\{x\in K:Ax=b\}=\{x\in F:Ax=b\},
\]
so the reduced primal over \(F\) has value \(p^*\). Facial reduction constructs \(F\) by successive intersections with exposing hyperplanes valid for the feasible set. If the reduced system contains \(\bar x\in\operatorname{ri}F\) with \(A\bar x=b\), its dual is formed with \(F^*\) in \(\operatorname{span}F\), placing conic duality in the relative-Slater regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Facial reduction replaces the original cone by the minimal face supporting all feasible moments, preserving the primal problem and potentially restoring relative strict feasibility.
