children.title: Primal Attainment Regimes
children.top_down_role: Existence behavior for optimal truncated moment solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Attainment Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment criterion for the primal moment conic program at one relaxation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, let \(K\subseteq E\) be a closed convex cone, and let \(A:E\to\mathbb R^m\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in E\). Define
\[
X_P:=\{x\in K:Ax=b\},\qquad p^*:=\inf_{x\in X_P}\langle c,x\rangle.
\]
If \(X_P\ne\varnothing\) and \(p^*\in\mathbb R\), primal attainment means
\[
\exists x^*\in X_P\quad \langle c,x^*\rangle=p^*.
\]
Equivalently, \(p^*\in\{\langle c,x\rangle:x\in X_P\}\). Compactness of the nonempty set \(X_P\) is sufficient for attainment, whereas equality of primal and dual values alone is not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite primal value is attained exactly when a feasible moment vector realizes the infimum; zero duality gap alone does not ensure attainment.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space and \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone.
\(A:E\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c\in E\), \(X_P\ne\varnothing\), and \(p^*\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal attainment holds exactly when \(p^*\in\{\langle c,x\rangle:x\in X_P\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Attainment Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment criterion for the dual SOS conic program at one relaxation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, let \(K\subseteq E\) be a closed convex cone, and let \(A:E\to\mathbb R^m\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in E\). With \(A^*:\mathbb R^m\to E\) denoting the adjoint, define
\[
Y_D:=\{y\in\mathbb R^m:c-A^*y\in K^*\},\qquad d^*:=\sup_{y\in Y_D}\langle b,y\rangle.
\]
If \(Y_D\ne\varnothing\) and \(d^*\in\mathbb R\), dual attainment means
\[
\exists y^*\in Y_D
eqqcolon y^*\quad \langle b,y^*\rangle=d^*.
\]
Equivalently, one feasible finite-degree SOS certificate realizes the best dual bound at the selected relaxation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The finite dual optimum is attained when a feasible multiplier, equivalently a finite-degree SOS certificate in the relevant realization, realizes the best dual bound.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space and \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone.
\(A:E\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c\in E\), \(Y_D\ne\varnothing\), and \(d^*\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual attainment holds exactly when some \(y^*\in Y_D\) satisfies \(\langle b,y^*\rangle=d^*\).

children.title: Joint Attainment Regimes
children.top_down_role: Finite-level settings where both sides attain their optimal values.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Attainment Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous attainment and value equality for a fixed finite moment-SOS relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, let \(K\subseteq E\) be a closed convex cone, and let \(A:E\to\mathbb R^m\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in E\). Define
\[
p^*:=\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in K\},\qquad d^*:=\sup\{\langle b,y\rangle:c-A^*y\in K^*\}.
\]
The joint-attainment, zero-gap regime holds exactly when there exist \(x^*\in K\) and \(y^*\in\mathbb R^m\) such that
\[
Ax^*=b,\qquad c-A^*y^*\in K^*,\qquad \langle c,x^*\rangle=\langle b,y^*\rangle.
\]
Under weak duality, these conditions imply \(p^*=d^*\) and attainment of both extrema; conversely, attained equal finite values yield such optimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint attainment with no gap occurs exactly when feasible primal and dual solutions exist with equal objective values.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone, \(A:E\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in E\).
The primal and dual problems are feasible, have finite optimal values, and satisfy weak duality \(d^*\le p^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Joint attainment with strong duality is equivalent to the existence of feasible \(x^*\) and \(y^*\) satisfying \(\langle c,x^*\rangle=\langle b,y^*\rangle\).

children.title: Finite-Level Duality Gaps
children.top_down_role: Finite hierarchy levels exhibiting unequal primal plus dual values.

assumptions_latex: A primal-dual moment-SOS conic pair is fixed at relaxation order \(r\).
Both finite optimal values \(p_r^*\) and \(d_r^*\) are defined under the minimization convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A finite-level duality gap occurs precisely when \(d_r^*<p_r^*\); strict feasibility on either appropriate side rules it out under standard conic duality hypotheses.

notation.meaning: Primal and dual values at relaxation order r.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive conic duality gap at a fixed hierarchy level, distinct from nonattainment.

source_refs.locator: 5.1 The Primal and Dual Perspectives p. 110

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At order \(r\), weak duality gives \(d_r^*\le p_r^*\). The finite-level gap is
\[
\Delta_r:=p_r^*-d_r^*.
\]
A finite-level duality gap is present when \(p_r^*,d_r^*\in\mathbb R\) and \(\Delta_r>0\). This failure is logically independent of attainment: either optimum may or may not be realized. For a finite-dimensional closed-cone formulation, a primal Slater point \(x\in\operatorname{int}K\) with \(Ax=b\), together with finite primal value, yields \(p_r^*=d_r^*\) and dual attainment; the symmetric dual regularity regime yields the corresponding primal conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-level gap is the strict inequality between finite primal and dual values. It is separate from whether either optimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Level Duality Gaps

The added one-sided Slater attainment conclusions require inspection of a conic-duality theorem with its exact feasibility, finiteness, and cone-interior hypotheses.

children.title: Primal Nonattainment
children.top_down_role: Moment relaxations with unattained finite-level optima.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Nonattainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite infimum without an optimizing truncated moment sequence at the fixed order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, let \(K\subseteq E\) be a closed convex cone, and let \(A:E\to\mathbb R^m\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in E\). Define
\[
X_P:=\{x\in K:Ax=b\},\qquad p^*:=\inf_{x\in X_P}\langle c,x\rangle.
\]
If \(X_P\ne\varnothing\) and \(p^*\in\mathbb R\), primal nonattainment is the condition
\[
\langle c,x\rangle>p^*\quad\text{for every }x\in X_P.
\]
Equivalently, a sequence \((x_k)\subseteq X_P\) has \(\langle c,x_k\rangle\to p^*\), but no point of \(X_P\) realizes \(p^*\). This condition is distinct from a positive primal-dual value gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal nonattainment means feasible moment vectors approach the finite infimum, but no feasible moment vector realizes it.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone, \(A:E\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in E\).
The primal feasible set \(X_P\) is nonempty and its infimum \(p^*\) is finite.

children.title: Dual Nonattainment
children.top_down_role: Certificate relaxations with unattained finite-level optima.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Nonattainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite supremum without an optimizing SOS certificate at the fixed order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, let \(K\subseteq E\) be a closed convex cone, and let \(A:E\to\mathbb R^m\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in E\). With \(A^*:\mathbb R^m\to E\), define
\[
Y_D:=\{y\in\mathbb R^m:c-A^*y\in K^*\},\qquad d^*:=\sup_{y\in Y_D}\langle b,y\rangle.
\]
If \(Y_D\ne\varnothing\) and \(d^*\in\mathbb R\), dual nonattainment is the condition
\[
\langle b,y\rangle<d^*\quad\text{for every }y\in Y_D.
\]
Equivalently, a sequence \((y_k)\subseteq Y_D\) has \(\langle b,y_k\rangle\to d^*\), but no feasible multiplier realizes \(d^*\). In an SOS realization, fixed-degree certificates approach the best bound without attaining it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual nonattainment means fixed-degree SOS certificates approach the finite best bound, but no feasible certificate realizes it.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, \(K\subseteq E\) is a closed convex cone, \(A:E\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in E\).
The dual feasible set \(Y_D\) is nonempty and its supremum \(d^*\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual nonattainment means \(\langle b,y\rangle<d^*\) for every \(y\in Y_D\), although feasible dual values converge to \(d^*\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Set \(g_0:=1\). A level-\(r\) global lower-bound certificate for \(f\) is a scalar \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\) and sums of squares \(\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_m\) such that
\[
f-\gamma=\sum_{j=0}^m\sigma_jg_j,
\qquad \deg(\sigma_jg_j)\le 2r.
\]
Equivalently, \(f-\gamma\in Q_r(g)\). For every \(x\in K\), each \(\sigma_j(x)\ge0\) and each \(g_j(x)\ge0\), hence \(f(x)-\gamma\ge0\). The identity is therefore a finitely checkable certificate that \(\gamma\le f^*:=\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SOS quadratic-module identity for the objective minus a scalar proves that scalar is a valid lower bound everywhere on the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Lower-Bound Certificates

children.title: Global Optimality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificate families matching feasible candidates with global bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matching a feasible objective value with an SOS-certified global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\), let \(K:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), and set \(g_0:=1\). Suppose \(x^*\in K\), \(r\in\mathbb N\), and there exist \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\) and sums of squares \(\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_m\) such that
\[
f-\gamma=\sum_{j=0}^m\sigma_jg_j,\qquad \deg(\sigma_jg_j)\le2r,\qquad f(x^*)=\gamma.
\]
Then
\[
f^*:=\inf_{x\in K}f(x)=\gamma=f(x^*),
\]
and \(x^*\) is a global minimizer. Thus the feasible point and matching SOS lower bound form a finite global-optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point is globally optimal when its objective value equals a lower bound certified by a finite-degree SOS identity.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\), \(K:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), and \(x^*\in K\).
For some \(r\in\mathbb N\), a degree-bounded quadratic-module identity certifies the lower bound \(f\ge\gamma\) on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(f(x^*)=\gamma\), then \(x^*\) is a global minimizer and \(f^*=\gamma\).

knowledge_statements.title: Semialgebraic Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic-module refutation of feasibility at a finite SOS order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\), define \(K:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), and set \(g_0:=1\). A finite-order semialgebraic infeasibility certificate is an identity
\[
-1=\sum_{j=0}^m\sigma_jg_j,
\qquad \sigma_j\text{ is SOS},
\qquad \deg(\sigma_jg_j)\le2r,
\]
for some \(r\in\mathbb N\). Such an identity certifies
\[
K=\varnothing.
\]
It is finitely checkable through SOS Gram representations and coefficient equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An identity expressing minus one in the truncated quadratic module proves that no point satisfies all polynomial inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\), \(K:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), and \(r\in\mathbb N\).
There exist sums of squares satisfying the displayed degree-bounded polynomial identity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The identity \(-1\in Q_r(g)\) certifies that \(K=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Truncated quadratic module generated by the inequalities.

children.title: Representing-Measure Certificates
children.top_down_role: Moment certificates supporting measure and optimizer recovery.

assumptions_latex: \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le2r}\) satisfies the moment and localizing positive-semidefinite constraints for \(K\).
A flat extension condition holds at an order sufficient for all constraint degrees.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The truncated sequence has a finitely atomic representing measure supported on \(K\), whose atoms can be recovered from the moment matrices.

notation.meaning: Number of atoms certified by the flat rank.
Linear functional represented by the moments.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Flat truncated-moment certificate for finite atomic measure and optimizer recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(d_K:=\max_j\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\). Suppose
\[
M_r(y)\succeq0,
\qquad M_{r-\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil}(g_jy)\succeq0,
\qquad \operatorname{rank}M_r(y)=\operatorname{rank}M_{r-d_K}(y)=s.
\]
Under the flat-extension theorem, these conditions certify a representing measure
\[
\mu=sum_{i=1}^s w_i\delta_{x^{(i)}},
\qquad w_i>0,
\qquad x^{(i)}\in K,
\]
such that \(y_\alpha=int_Kx^\alpha\,d\mu\) for every \(|\alpha|\le2r\). Multiplication operators derived from a basis of the column space of \(M_r(y)\) recover the atoms; if \(y\) is optimal, the atoms are global minimizers when their objective average equals the relaxation value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive localizing matrices plus flat rank certify a finitely atomic feasible measure; its atoms can be extracted and may recover global minimizers.
knowledge_statements.title: Representing-Measure Certificates

children.title: Nested-Bound Monotonicity
children.top_down_role: Monotonicity associated with the relaxation-order filtration.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested-Bound Monotonicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order filtration and monotonicity of minimization lower bounds in the SOS hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\), define \(K:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), and set \(g_0:=1\). For each admissible order \(r\), define
\[
Q_r(g):=\left\{\sum_{j=0}^m\sigma_jg_j:\sigma_j\text{ is SOS},\ \deg(\sigma_jg_j)\le2r\right\},
\qquad
\rho_r:=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma\in Q_r(g)\}.
\]
Since \(Q_r(g)\subseteq Q_{r+1}(g)\), the bounds satisfy
\[
\rho_r\le\rho_{r+1}\le f^*:=\inf_{x\in K}f(x).
\]
Thus \((\rho_r)\) is a nondecreasing sequence of valid global lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasing the relaxation order enlarges the certificate cone, so SOS lower bounds cannot decrease and never exceed the true minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\), and \(Q_r(g)\subseteq Q_{r+1}(g)\) for consecutive admissible hierarchy orders.
Each bound is \(\rho_r:=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma\in Q_r(g)\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lower bounds are nested and monotone: \(\rho_r\le\rho_{r+1}\le f^*\).

SOS lower bound at order r.
Global minimum over the feasible set.

children.title: Asymptotic Optimal-Moment Behavior
children.top_down_role: Limiting behavior of optimal moment sequences and minimizing measures.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) is compact and the moment relaxations enforce \(y_0=1\).
At every order \(d\), an optimal truncated moment vector \(y^{(d)}\) exists.
The relaxation values converge to \(f^*=\min_K f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every coordinatewise accumulation sequence represents an optimal probability measure on \(K\).

notation.meaning: optimal truncated moment vector at order d
set of global minimizers of f on K

review_flags: exact compactness and representability hypotheses need a direct moment-hierarchy source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise subsequential behavior of normalized optimal moments in a compact convergent hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Extend each \(y^{(d)}\) only through its available coordinates. Compactness bounds every fixed coordinate, so a diagonal subsequence \(y^{(d_j)}\) converges coordinatewise to a full sequence \(y^*\). If the limiting positivity constraints ensure that \(y^*\) has a representing probability measure \(\mu^*\) supported on \(K\), then \[\int_K f\,d\mu^*=L_{y^*}(f)=f^*.\] Since \(f-f^*\ge0\) on \(K\), this equality implies \(\mu^*(K\setminus K^*)=0\), where \(K^*=\{x\in K:f(x)=f^*\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any representable coordinatewise limit of normalized optimal moments is an optimal probability measure and is supported on the global minimizers.
knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Optimal-Moment Behavior

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conclusion claims that every coordinatewise accumulation sequence represents an optimal measure, whereas the statement only reaches that conclusion conditionally if the limit has a representing measure. Compactness and value convergence alone do not state the precise positivity and representability hypotheses needed. A direct moment-hierarchy source is required to fix the theorem.

children.title: Coercive Objective Regimes
children.top_down_role: Noncompact optimization settings controlled by coercive objective behavior.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is closed and nonempty.
\(f:K\to\mathbb R\) is continuous and coercive on \(K\), meaning \(f(x_k)\to+\infty\) whenever \(x_k\in K\) and \(\|x_k\|\to\infty\).

review_flags: source locator for the coercive noncompact SOS regime is missing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-induced compactness before selecting a noncompact SOS certificate family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), let \(K_\alpha=\{x\in K:f(x)\le\alpha\}\). Coercivity makes \(K_\alpha\) bounded, while continuity of \(f\) and closedness of \(K\) make it closed; hence \(K_\alpha\) is compact. If \(f\) is bounded below on \(K\), choose \(x_0\in K\). Any minimizing sequence eventually lies in the compact set \(K_{f(x_0)}\), and therefore has a cluster point \(x^*\in K\) satisfying \[f(x^*)=\min_{x\in K}f(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous coercive objective on a closed feasible set has compact finite sublevels and attains its global minimum.

children.title: Sublevel-Compact Regimes
children.top_down_role: Noncompact feasible sets with compact objective sublevels.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty.
\(f:K\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is lower semicontinuous and proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime holds exactly when every finite sublevel \(K_\alpha\) is compact.

notation.meaning: objective sublevel on the feasible set

review_flags: source locator for objective-compact SOS convergence is missing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inf-compactness condition separating objective compactness from compactness of the entire feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The objective is sublevel-compact on \(K\) precisely when \[K_\alpha=\{x\in K:f(x)\le\alpha\}\quad\text{is compact for every finite }\alpha.\] If \(f^*=\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\) is finite, then any \(\alpha>f^*\) has nonempty compact \(K_\alpha\), and lower semicontinuity yields a point \(x^*\in K_\alpha\) with \(f(x^*)=f^*\). Thus optimization localizes to a compact sublevel even when \(K\) itself is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sublevel-compact regime requires every finite objective sublevel to be compact; a finite infimum is then attained within one such sublevel.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly describes inf-compactness and its attainment consequence, but it has no source or explicit standard-field rationale. Its explanatory attainment argument is proof text and should not remain in the final knowledge statement.

children.title: Coercivity–Compactness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits of correspondence between coercivity plus sublevel compactness.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set is \(K=\mathbb R^2\).
The polynomial is \(f(x,y)=(xy-1)^2+x^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) has infimum zero but is neither coercive nor sublevel-compact and does not attain its infimum.
review_flags: direct source for this boundary example is missing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete boundary showing that boundedness below does not imply coercivity, compact sublevels, or attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The polynomial satisfies \(f(x,y)>0\) for every \((x,y)\in\mathbb R^2\): equality would require simultaneously \(xy=1\) and \(x=0\). Nevertheless, along \(z_R=(R^{-1},R)\), \[\|z_R\|\longrightarrow\infty,\qquad f(z_R)=R^{-2}\longrightarrow0.\] Hence \(\inf_{\mathbb R^2}f=0\) is not attained. For every \(\alpha>0\), the sublevel \(\{f\le\alpha\}\) contains all sufficiently large \(z_R\), so it is unbounded and noncompact; consequently \(f\) is not coercive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial can be bounded below yet have escaping near-minimizers, noncompact sublevels, and no minimizer; this example has infimum zero only at infinity.
knowledge_statements.title: Coercivity–Compactness Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The polynomial is a valid counterexample for the stated coercivity-compactness boundary, and the counterexample kind fits the leaf. However, no evidence record or explicit standard-field rationale is supplied, and the statement is written as a verification argument rather than a proof-free counterexample statement.

children.title: Homogenized Compactification Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Hierarchy constructions using homogeneous or projective compactification.

assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\), with homogenizations \(\widetilde f,\widetilde g_i\).
The projective feasible set is restricted to the compact hemisphere \(S=\{(x_0,x):x_0\ge0,\ x_0^2+\|x\|^2=1,\ \widetilde g_i(x_0,x)\ge0\}\).
The homogenized formulation has no value-lowering feasible point at \(x_0=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A compact-set moment-SOS hierarchy on \(S\) yields lower bounds converging to the original affine infimum.

notation.meaning: homogenization of a polynomial p to its total degree

review_flags: precise equivalence and hierarchy hypotheses require a homogenization-specific source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projective compactification with an explicit exclusion of value-lowering points at infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a polynomial \(p\) of degree \(d\), set \(\widetilde p(x_0,x)=x_0^d p(x/x_0)\). Affine points map to the hemisphere by \[(x_0,x)=\frac{(1,u)}{\sqrt{1+\|u\|^2}},\] while \(x_0=0\) records directions at infinity. After homogenizing objective comparisons and constraints to common degrees, optimization is represented on \(S\). If feasible points with \(x_0=0\) do not lower the affine value and the quadratic module on \(S\) is Archimedean, the resulting compact moment-SOS bounds converge to the original infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogenization maps an unbounded polynomial problem to a compact hemisphere; convergence transfers when feasible points at infinity cannot improve the affine value.
knowledge_statements.title: Homogenized Compactification Hierarchies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine-to-hemisphere map is standard, but the phrases about homogenizing objective comparisons and excluding value-lowering points at infinity do not specify the exact homogeneous optimization problem or hypotheses ensuring equality of values. A homogenization-specific source is needed before the representation and convergence claim, and its proper terminal kind, can be fixed.

assumptions_latex: \(K=\{x:g_i(x)\ge0\}\) and \(w\in\mathbb R[x]\) satisfies \(w(x)>0\) on \(K\).
A prescribed weighted Positivstellensatz is valid for polynomials strictly positive on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The weighted bounds are valid and converge whenever the prescribed weighted positivity certificates exist for every positive perturbation.

notation.meaning: weighted lower bound at level r,d

review_flags: the intended weighted certificate family and completeness theorem are ambiguous without a direct source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic weighted-certificate hierarchy; the exact admissible weight family must be fixed by a source.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given nonnegative integers \(r,d\), compute \[\rho_{r,d}=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:w^r(f-\gamma)\in Q_d(g)\}.\] Initialize with any degree pair for which all products fit the truncation, increase \(d\) and optionally \(r\), and output the largest certified \(\gamma\). Since \(w>0\) on \(K\), every feasible certificate implies \(f(x)\ge\gamma\) on \(K\). If for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there exist finite \(r,d\) with \(w^r(f-f^*+\varepsilon)\in Q_d(g)\), then any nested exhaustive ordering of the pairs yields bounds converging to \(f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiply the objective gap by a positive growth weight and search for truncated SOS certificates; completeness of that weighted certificate family gives convergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted SOS Hierarchies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed algorithm is only a generic template: neither the admissible weight nor the weighted Positivstellensatz is identified. Without a direct source, the intended weighted hierarchy cannot be distinguished from the denominator hierarchy or checked for completeness and nesting.

children.title: Denominator SOS Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Noncompact hierarchy families using certificates with controlled denominators.

assumptions_latex: \(w\in\mathbb R[x]\) is strictly positive on \(K\).
\(Q_d(g)\) is a degree-truncated quadratic module nonnegative on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each feasible level certifies a lower bound, and exhaustive levels converge under denominator-certificate completeness.
review_flags: the intended denominator Positivstellensatz and admissible denominator class require a direct source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rational SOS certificates with powers of a fixed positive polynomial as denominators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At level \((r,d)\), solve \[\eta_{r,d}=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:w^r(f-\gamma)\in Q_d(g)\}.\] A feasible identity \(w^r(f-\gamma)=\sigma_0+\sum_i\sigma_i g_i\) is equivalently a rational nonnegativity certificate after division by the positive denominator \(w^r\), so \(\eta_{r,d}\le f^*\). Increase \(r,d\) through a nested exhaustive family and return the best bound. If every \(f-f^*+\varepsilon\) admits such a finite denominator certificate, then the returned bounds converge to \(f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A denominator hierarchy certifies lower bounds by clearing a positive polynomial denominator and imposing an SOS identity on the resulting numerator.
knowledge_statements.title: Denominator SOS Hierarchies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lower-bound implication is valid for a fixed positive denominator, but the admissible denominator family, truncation, nesting, and completeness theorem are unspecified. A direct denominator-Positivstellensatz source is required to validate this algorithm as the exact terminal object.

children.title: Weight–Denominator Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Structural comparison of weighting choices versus denominator-based constructions.

assumptions_latex: \(w\in\mathbb R[x]\) is strictly positive on \(K\).
For some \(r\ge0\), \(w^r(f-\gamma)=\sigma_0+\sum_i\sigma_i g_i\) with SOS polynomials \(\sigma_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The polynomial weighted identity and its rational denominator form certify exactly the same lower bound.

notation.meaning: SOS multiplier of the i-th constraint, with g_0=1

review_flags: a source is needed for quantitative degree and conditioning tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic equivalence only; no universal degree or numerical-conditioning superiority is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(g_0=1\), the weighted identity \[w^r(f-\gamma)=\sum_{i=0}^m\sigma_i g_i\] is equivalent, because \(w>0\) on \(K\), to the rational representation \[f-\gamma=\sum_{i=0}^m\frac{\sigma_i}{w^r}g_i.\] Thus increasing the weight exponent enlarges the permitted common-denominator certificate family but also increases numerator degree before truncation. Any comparison of relaxation size or conditioning must account jointly for \(r\), the degrees of \(w^r\sigma_i g_i\), and the chosen truncation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted polynomial certificate becomes the same rational certificate after division by the positive weight; larger exponents trade denominator flexibility for higher numerator degree.
knowledge_statements.title: Weight–Denominator Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Division by a strictly positive weight gives an algebraic equivalence, but this is a representation property rather than a mathematical duality. The assertion that increasing the exponent enlarges the certificate family is not justified for a general positive polynomial because multiplication by the weight need not preserve the quadratic module. A source defining the intended family and quantitative tradeoff is required.

children.title: Infinity-Escape Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Noncompact failure boundaries involving attainment and minimizing behavior at infinity.

children.title: Asymptotic Objective Geometry
children.top_down_role: Objective behavior along unbounded feasible directions.

assumptions_latex: \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\) has degree \(d\) and leading homogeneous form \(f_d\).
\(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is unbounded, with asymptotic feasible directions represented on the unit sphere.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonpositive leading behavior along a feasible direction obstructs coercivity and may permit value escape at infinity.
review_flags: a direct source is needed for the precise feasible-direction and lower-order cancellation criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Leading-form diagnostic for objective behavior along unbounded feasible directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Along a ray \(x=tu\), with \(\|u\|=1\), one has \[f(tu)=t^d f_d(u)+O(t^{d-1})\qquad(t\to\infty).\] Therefore \(f_d(u)<0\) on an asymptotically feasible ray forces \(f(tu)\to-\infty\), while \(f_d(u)=0\) leaves coercivity undecided and exposes the value to lower-order cancellations. Strict positivity of \(f_d\) on every feasible direction is a sufficient leading-order barrier against escape; zeros of \(f_d\) are the boundary at which lower-degree terms and curved feasible paths must be examined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The leading homogeneous objective controls values on feasible rays; negative directions cause unbounded descent, while zero directions form the boundary where lower-order geometry decides escape.
knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Objective Geometry

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ray expansion is correct, but the candidate does not define the asymptotic feasible-direction set precisely. Positivity on feasible rays is not by itself a general coercivity criterion when curved feasible paths at infinity are possible. A direct source is needed to state the correct horizon or projective condition for this failure boundary.

children.title: Moment-Mass Escape
children.top_down_role: Loss of tightness in moment sequences over noncompact domains.

assumptions_latex: For \(R>0\), let \(\mu_R=\delta_{(R^{-1},R)}\) and let \(y^{(R)}\) be its moment sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The measures are minimizing but not tight, and their moment coordinates have no finite coordinatewise limit.

notation.meaning: Dirac probability measure at the escaping point

review_flags: direct source for the moment-mass escape example is missing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit minimizing probability measures whose mass and moments escape to infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The normalized measures satisfy \(y^{(R)}_0=1\) and \[\int f\,d\mu_R=f(R^{-1},R)=R^{-2}\longrightarrow0=\inf_K f.\] Nevertheless, \(\mu_R\) is not tight: every compact set excludes its support for all sufficiently large \(R\). Moreover, the coordinate \(y^{(R)}_{(0,1)}=R\) diverges, and higher \(y\)-moments diverge faster. Thus objective values may converge to the infimum while normalized moment vectors possess no finite coordinatewise accumulation point and no limiting probability measure on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dirac masses along an escaping minimizing sequence achieve asymptotically optimal values while losing tightness and making moment coordinates diverge.
knowledge_statements.title: Moment-Mass Escape

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit Dirac sequence correctly demonstrates loss of tightness and divergence of a moment coordinate, and the counterexample kind fits the leaf. The measures are asymptotically minimizing rather than individually minimizing, and no source or explicit standard-field rationale supports the record.

children.title: Attainment Failure at Infinity
children.top_down_role: Nonattainment associated with minimizing behavior along unbounded directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Attainment Failure at Infinity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete polynomial example of a finite infimum approached only by an unbounded minimizing sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x,y)=(xy-1)^2+x^2\) on \(K=\mathbb R^2\). Then \(f\geq 0\), and along \((x_k,y_k)=(1/k,k)\) one has \(\|(x_k,y_k)\|\to\infty\) and \(f(x_k,y_k)=1/k^2\to0\). Hence \(f^*:=\inf_K f=0\). However, \(f(x,y)=0\) would require simultaneously \(x=0\) and \(xy=1\), which is impossible. Thus the infimum is not attained, and no probability measure on \(K\) realizes objective value \(f^*\), although minimizing mass can escape toward infinity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This polynomial has infimum zero, approached along an unbounded sequence, but has no global minimizer or optimal representing probability measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\inf_{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2}f(x,y)=0\quad\text{and}\quad\operatorname{argmin}_{\mathbb R^2}f=\varnothing.\]

notation.meaning: Infimum of the objective over the feasible set.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit polynomial example is directly checkable

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit example, nonattainment conclusion, and probability-measure consequence are mathematically coherent and fit the failure-boundary container, but the record has no inspectable citation. The standard-field rationale is insufficient to satisfy the statement-review citation requirement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Asymptotic Versus Finite Convergence of the Lasserre Hierarchy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines finite convergence and distinguishes it from Archimedean asymptotic value convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the Archimedean condition, the Lasserre bounds satisfy $f^{(r)}\to f^*$ as $r\to\infty$. Finite convergence holds if $f^{(r)}=f^*$ for some $r\in\mathbb N$. In general, Archimedean asymptotic convergence does not ensure finite convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Archimedeanity makes the Lasserre lower bounds converge to the optimum. Finite convergence means that some finite relaxation order attains the optimum, which need not happen in general.
assumptions_latex: \exists N\in\mathbb N:\ N-\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2\in\mathcal M(g)+I(h)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f^{(r)}\to f^*\text{ as }r\to\infty;\qquad \text{finite convergence means }\exists r\in\mathbb N:\ f^{(r)}=f^*;\qquad\text{finite convergence need not hold.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Moment-SOS Convergence, Finite Exactness, and Flat-Rank Extraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower moment-SOS hierarchy for polynomial optimization under the stated Archimedean ball condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the stated Archimedean ball condition and consider the order-\(t\) moment relaxation \(\rho_t\) and SOS dual \(\rho_t^*\), for \(t\ge t_0\). Then \(\rho_t^*=\rho_t\), and the primal relaxation attains its optimum at every order. If \(S\) has nonempty interior, the dual also attains its optimum. Moreover, \(\rho_t\uparrow f^*\). If LICQ, strict complementarity, and the stated second-order sufficient condition hold at every global minimizer, convergence is finite. Finally, let \(s=\max_{g\in G}t_g\). If, for some order \(t\), an optimal moment functional \(\phi^*\) satisfies \[\operatorname{rank}M_t(\phi^*)=\operatorname{rank}M_{t-s}(\phi^*),\] then \(\rho_t=f^*\), and \(\operatorname{rank}M_t(\phi^*)\) global minimizers can be extracted from \(\phi^*\) by linear algebra.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the ball-based Archimedean assumption, every hierarchy level has no duality gap and an attained primal optimum; nonempty interior additionally guarantees dual attainment. The lower bounds increase to the global optimum. Regularity conditions at every global minimizer imply finite convergence, while the stated flat-rank condition certifies exactness at a particular level and permits extraction of the global minimizers.
assumptions_latex: S\text{ and }G\text{ satisfy the stated Archimedean ball condition}
t\ge t_0
\rho_t\text{ and }\rho_t^*\text{ are the order-}t\text{ moment-SOS primal-dual values}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho_t^*=\rho_t,\quad \rho_t\uparrow f^*;\quad \bigl(\mathrm{LICQ}+\mathrm{SC}+\mathrm{SOSC}\text{ at every global minimizer}\bigr)\Rightarrow\text{finite convergence};\quad \operatorname{rank}M_t(\phi^*)=\operatorname{rank}M_{t-s}(\phi^*)\Rightarrow \rho_t=f^*\text{ and minimizer extraction}

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Degree Certificate Membership
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate characterization of exactness at a fixed order of the quadratic-module SOS hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\geq0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), let \(Q_d(g)\) be the degree-\(2d\) truncated quadratic module and define \(\rho_d=\sup\{\gamma:f-\gamma\in Q_d(g)\}\). If the minimum \(f^*=\min_K f\) exists and \(f-f^*\in Q_d(g)\), then weak duality gives \(\rho_d=f^*\), so the order-\(d\) relaxation is exact. Conversely, if the supremum defining \(\rho_d\) is attained and \(\rho_d=f^*\), then its optimizing certificate gives \(f-f^*\in Q_d(g)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed order, membership of the optimality gap in the truncated quadratic module certifies exactness; the converse holds when the SOS bound is attained.
assumptions_latex: \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\geq0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\neq\varnothing\).
\(f^*=\min_{x\in K}f(x)\) is finite and attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[f-f^*\in Q_d(g)\Longrightarrow \rho_d=f^*,\qquad \rho_d=f^*\text{ attained}\Longrightarrow f-f^*\in Q_d(g).\]

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary-Hessian Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Marshall’s boundary-Hessian condition in local coordinates adapted to active inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u\in K\) be a zero of \(p\), and suppose the active constraints provide local parameters \(t_1,\ldots,t_k\), completed by \(t_{k+1},\ldots,t_n\). The boundary-Hessian condition at \(u\) requires the local expansion \(p=p_1+p_2+\text{terms of order at least three}\), where \(p_1=a_1t_1+\cdots+a_kt_k\) with every \(a_i>0\), and the restriction of \(p_2\) to \(t_1=\cdots=t_k=0\) is positive definite in \((t_{k+1},\ldots,t_n)\). It encodes strict growth inward from the boundary and nondegenerate tangential curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In boundary-adapted coordinates, the polynomial must grow linearly in every active inward direction and quadratically and positively in tangent directions.

\(u\in K\) satisfies \(p(u)=0\), and suitable active constraints form part of a regular local parameter system.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-to-Global Exactness Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convergence obtained by converting local optimality conditions at all global minimizers into a global certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f\) on \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\geq0\}\), and assume the quadratic module \(Q(g)\) is Archimedean. If constraint qualification, strict complementarity, and the second-order sufficiency condition hold at every global minimizer, then \(f-f^*\in Q(g)\). Since this representation uses finitely many SOS polynomials of finite degree, there exists \(d_0\) such that \(f-f^*\in Q_{d_0}(g)\). Consequently every SOS relaxation of order \(d\geq d_0\) has value \(f^*\).

The minimum \(f^*\) is attained.
Constraint qualification, strict complementarity, and second-order sufficiency hold at every global minimizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Generic Finite-Convergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic finite convergence for fixed degree patterns under algebraic nondegeneracy conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix the numbers and degree bounds of the objective and constraints, and restrict to instances whose quadratic module is Archimedean. Outside a proper algebraic exceptional set of coefficient data, the constraint qualification, strict-complementarity, and second-order sufficiency conditions hold at every local minimizer whenever the feasible minimum exists. Therefore, for such generic instances, the local-to-global exactness theorem yields an order \(d_0<\infty\) for which the Lasserre hierarchy satisfies \(\rho_d=f^*\) for every \(d\geq d_0\). The exceptional algebraic conditions depend only on the prescribed degree pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For fixed polynomial degrees, nondegenerate coefficient data generically satisfy the local conditions that imply finite convergence of an Archimedean SOS hierarchy.
assumptions_latex: The objective and constraint degree pattern is fixed.
The generated quadratic module is Archimedean.
The feasible minimum exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{For generic coefficient data, }\exists d_0<\infty\ \forall d\geq d_0:\ \rho_d=f^*.\]

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Variety Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convergence when equality constraints define a finite real variety.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_r\rangle\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) be real radical with finite real variety \(V_{\mathbb R}(I)\), and let \(K=V_{\mathbb R}(I)\cap\{x:g_j(x)\geq0\}\). For every polynomial \(f\), if \(K\neq\varnothing\) and \(f^*=\min_K f\), then the residue class of \(f-f^*\) admits a finite SOS/quadratic-module certificate on the zero-dimensional coordinate ring. Equivalently, \(f-f^*\in I+Q(g)\). Hence this certificate occurs in some finite truncation, and the associated hierarchy is exact from that order onward.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real-radical equality ideal with finite real variety reduces positivity to finite-dimensional interpolation, producing a finite-degree exactness certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) is real radical and \(|V_{\mathbb R}(I)|<\infty\).
\(K=V_{\mathbb R}(I)\cap\{g_j\geq0\}\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[f-f^*\in I+Q(g),\qquad \exists d_0\ \forall d\geq d_0:\ \rho_d=f^*.\]

notation.meaning: Equality ideal generated by the polynomial equations.
Real variety of the equality ideal.
Quadratic module generated by the inequalities.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The claimed finite-variety certificate is plausible and fits the theorem container, but no source is supplied for the precise implication f-f^* in I+Q(g), its real-radical hypotheses, or the resulting hierarchy exactness. An authoritative theorem or section locator is required before accepting this formulation.

children.title: Finite-Set Exactness
children.top_down_role: Finite convergence associated with finite real feasible sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Set Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness of a hierarchy explicitly augmented by the vanishing ideal of a finite feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{u_1,\ldots,u_s\}\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and include its vanishing ideal \(I(K)\) among the equality constraints. There exist interpolation polynomials \(e_i\) satisfying \(e_i(u_j)=\delta_{ij}\). For any polynomial \(f\), with \(f^*=\min_i f(u_i)\), one has \(f-f^*\equiv\sum_{i=1}^s(f(u_i)-f^*)e_i^2\pmod{I(K)}\). The right side is SOS because every coefficient is nonnegative. Thus \(f-f^*\in I(K)+\Sigma[x]\), and the equality-constrained SOS hierarchy is exact at some finite order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite feasible set, interpolation expresses the optimality gap as an SOS modulo the set’s vanishing ideal, yielding finite exactness.
assumptions_latex: \(K=\{u_1,\ldots,u_s\}\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and finite.
The hierarchy includes the equality ideal \(I(K)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[f-f^*\equiv\sum_{i=1}^s\bigl(f(u_i)-f^*\bigr)e_i^2\pmod{I(K)},\qquad f-f^*\in I(K)+\Sigma[x].\]

notation.meaning: Ideal of polynomials vanishing on the finite set.
Lagrange interpolation polynomial selecting the point \(u_i\).
Cone of sums of squares of real polynomials.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-set interpolation statement is mathematically standard, internally consistent, and appropriately classified as a theorem, but it has no inspectable authoritative citation. The standard-field rationale does not replace the required source locator.

children.title: Finite Quotient-Dimension Interface

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Quotient-Dimension Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic representation linking zero-dimensional quotient rings to finite-degree SOS certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=I(V)\) for a finite real set \(V=\{u_1,\ldots,u_s\}\). Then the evaluation map identifies the quotient algebra \(A=\mathbb R[x]/I\) with \(\mathbb R^s\). Under this identification, a residue class \([p]\in A\) is nonnegative on \(V\) exactly when it is a square-sum in \(A\): choosing interpolation idempotents \([e_i]\), one has \([p]=\sum_{i=1}^s p(u_i)[e_i]^2\). Consequently nonnegativity in the finite-dimensional quotient lifts to an SOS identity modulo \(I\), with a finite degree determined by representatives of a basis of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite real variety, its coordinate ring is a finite product of real fields, where pointwise nonnegativity is exactly sums-of-squares representability.
assumptions_latex: \(V\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and finite.
\(I=I(V)\) is its real vanishing ideal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathbb R[x]/I\cong\mathbb R^s,\qquad p|_V\geq0\Longleftrightarrow [p]\in\Sigma(\mathbb R[x]/I).\]

notation.meaning: Residue class of a polynomial modulo \(I\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the quotient-dimension interface, and the finite-product coordinate-ring formulation is coherent for I=I(V). No authoritative source with a specific locator is supplied, so the representation cannot yet be accepted under the citation requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomially Convex Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT-based exactness criterion for convex polynomial optimization without assuming SOS-convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(f\) and \(-g_j\) are convex polynomials, \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\geq0\}\) satisfies Slater’s condition, and \(u\) is a minimizer. Convex KKT theory provides multipliers \(\lambda_j\geq0\) such that \(L=f-f(u)-\sum_j\lambda_jg_j\) is globally nonnegative, with \(L(u)=0\) and \(\nabla L(u)=0\). If, in addition, this KKT Lagrangian is SOS, then \(f-f^*=L+
obreak\sum_j\lambda_jg_j\) is a finite-degree quadratic-module certificate. Ordinary polynomial convexity supplies KKT validity, while SOS membership of \(L\) is the extra condition needed for SOS exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexity and Slater give a nonnegative KKT Lagrangian; finite SOS exactness follows when that Lagrangian is itself a sum of squares.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(-g_j\) are convex polynomials, and a minimizer exists.
There is \(x^0\) with \(g_j(x^0)>0\) for every \(j\).
The KKT Lagrangian polynomial \(L\) is SOS.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[f-f^*=L+\sum_{j=1}^m\lambda_jg_j\in Q(g),\qquad \lambda_j\geq0.\]

notation.meaning: Quadratic module generated by the constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: SOS-Convex Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-step exactness for Slater-regular SOS-convex polynomial programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume \(f\) and \(-g_j\) are SOS-convex, \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\geq0\}\) satisfies Slater’s condition, and a minimizer \(u\) exists. KKT multipliers \(\lambda_j\geq0\) give \(L=f-f(u)-\sum_j\lambda_jg_j\) with \(L(u)=0\) and \(\nabla L(u)=0\). The polynomial \(L\) is SOS-convex; an SOS-convex polynomial vanishing together with its gradient at a point is SOS. Hence \(f-f^*=L+
obreak\sum_j\lambda_jg_j\), so the SOS relaxation is exact at any order containing these degrees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SOS-convexity turns the KKT Lagrangian into an SOS polynomial, giving a finite, often first-available-order, exact certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(-g_j\) are SOS-convex.
Slater’s condition holds for \(g_j\geq0\).
A global minimizer exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[f-f^*=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\lambda_jg_j,\qquad \sigma_0\in\Sigma[x],\quad \lambda_j\geq0.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: First-level exactness for convex and SOS-convex polynomial programs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient conditions for exactness of the first relaxation in the fixed-level intermediate hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the polynomial program \(P\). Suppose \(f\) and \(-g_j\) are convex for every \(j=1,\ldots,m\), Slater's condition holds, and \(f^*>-\infty\). Then
\[
\max\{\deg f,\deg g_1,\ldots,\deg g_m\}\le2
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\rho_1=f^*\quad\text{for }k=1.
\]
More generally, if
\[
\max\{\deg f,\deg g_1,\ldots,\deg g_m\}\le2k
\]
and \(f,-g_1,\ldots,-g_m\) are SOS-convex, then \(\rho_1=f^*\) for the hierarchy parameterized by \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex polynomial program satisfying Slater's condition and having finite optimal value, the first relaxation is exact for quadratic data at k=1. More generally, first-level exactness holds at level k when the objective and negated constraint polynomials are SOS-convex and have degree at most 2k.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Order Exactness Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Motzkin polynomial obstruction to exactness of the natural-degree unconstrained SOS relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m(x,y)=x^4y^2+x^2y^4-3x^2y^2+1\). The arithmetic-geometric mean inequality gives \(m(x,y)\geq0\), and equality occurs at \((1,1)\), so \(m^*=0\). Nevertheless, \(m\) is not SOS. For the degree-six unconstrained relaxation \(\rho_3=
obreak\sup\{\gamma:m-
obreak\gamma\in\Sigma[x]_6\}\), exactness with an attained bound would require \(m\in\Sigma[x]_6\). Moreover, since the finite-dimensional SOS cone is closed, even \(\rho_3=0\) as a finite supremum would force \(m\) to be SOS. Thus the natural low-order SOS relaxation cannot have value zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonnegative Motzkin polynomial has minimum zero but is not SOS, so its natural degree-six unconstrained SOS relaxation is not exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[m^*=0,
obreak\qquad m
otin\Sigma[x]_6,
obreak\qquad \rho_3<0\ \text{or}\ ho_3=-
obreak\infty.\]

Natural degree-six unconstrained SOS lower bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Flat-Extension Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curto–Fialkow flat extension criterion for an unconstrained truncated real moment sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le 2d}\) be a real truncated multisequence, and let \(M_d(y)\) be its moment matrix. If \(M_d(y)\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}M_d(y)=\operatorname{rank}M_{d-1}(y)=r\), then \(y\) admits a unique representing measure \(\mu=\sum_{i=1}^{r}w_i\delta_{x^{(i)}}\), where the points \(x^{(i)}\in\mathbb R^n\) are distinct and the weights satisfy \(w_i>0\). Equivalently, the columns indexed by monomials of degree at most \(d-1\) span the column space of \(M_d(y)\), so multiplication by each coordinate closes on an \(r\)-dimensional quotient space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive semidefinite moment matrix whose rank does not increase at the last degree has a unique representing measure supported on exactly that many points.
assumptions_latex: \(y\in\mathbb R^{\{\alpha:|\alpha|\le2d\}}\) with \(d\ge1\).
\(M_d(y)\succeq0\).
\(\operatorname{rank}M_d(y)=\operatorname{rank}M_{d-1}(y)=r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_\alpha=\sum_{i=1}^{r}w_i(x^{(i)})^\alpha\) for every \(|\alpha|\le2d\), with a unique \(r\)-atomic representing measure.

knowledge_statements.title: Value Exactness without Extractability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact relaxation value does not imply flatness of a selected optimal moment solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=[-1,1]\), let \(f(x)=0\), and consider any order-\(d\) moment relaxation with \(d\ge1\). The moment sequence of normalized Lebesgue measure on \(K\) is feasible and optimal, because both the true minimum and every relaxation objective value equal \(0\). Nevertheless, its moment matrix \(M_d(y)\) is positive definite: for every nonzero polynomial \(p\) of degree at most \(d\), one has \(p^{\mathsf T}M_d(y)p=\int_Kp(x)^2\,d\mu(x)>0\). Hence \(\operatorname{rank}M_d(y)=d+1\), so no terminal rank plateau occurs and this optimal moment solution does not directly yield a finitely atomic measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The zero objective on an interval is value-exact at every order, yet a non-atomic optimal measure produces full-rank moment matrices and no flat extraction.
assumptions_latex: \(\mu\) is normalized Lebesgue measure on \(K\).
\(y_\alpha=\int_Kx^\alpha\,d\mu(x)\) through degree \(2d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_d=f^*=0\) while \(\operatorname{rank}M_d(y)=d+1>\operatorname{rank}M_{d-1}(y)\).

notation.meaning: Normalized Lebesgue measure on the interval.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Dimensional Minimizer Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-dimensional optimal sets permit exact non-atomic optimal moments and defeat mandatory flat extraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) be compact and let \(Z=\{x\in K:f(x)=f^*\}\) contain a positive-dimensional compact component carrying a measure \(\mu\) whose support is infinite. The moments of \(\mu\) are feasible for every moment relaxation and attain objective value \(f^*\). If no nonzero polynomial of degree at most \(d\) vanishes \(\mu\)-almost everywhere, then \(M_d(y)\) is positive definite and has rank \(\binom{n+d}{d}\). Thus exact hierarchy values can coexist with growing ranks; positive-dimensional minimizer geometry prevents flatness from being a necessary detector of finite value convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuum of minimizers can support exact non-atomic optimal measures whose moment ranks keep growing, so flatness is sufficient but not necessary for value exactness.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is compact and \(f=f^*\) on \(\operatorname{supp}\mu\subseteq Z\).
\(\operatorname{supp}\mu\) is infinite.
No nonzero \(p\in\mathbb R[x]_{\le d}\) vanishes \(\mu\)-almost everywhere.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_y(f)=f^*\) and \(\operatorname{rank}M_d(y)=\binom{n+d}{d}\), so the optimal truncation need not be flat.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Minimizer Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of finite-convergence criteria based on nonsingular KKT and second-order geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider polynomial optimization over \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge0\}\). At a minimizer \(x^*\), finite-convergence theorems based on regular optimality conditions require, in a common formulation, linear independence of active constraint gradients, strict positivity of active multipliers, and positive definiteness of the Lagrangian Hessian on the constraint tangent space. If the active gradients are dependent, multipliers are degenerate, or the restricted Hessian is singular, those hypotheses fail. Their failure does not logically imply either finite convergence or nonconvergence; it marks a boundary where the cited regularity-based certificate cannot decide whether \(f-f^*\) belongs to a finite truncation of the quadratic module.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degenerate active constraints or a singular tangent Hessian invalidate standard regularity-based finite-convergence criteria but do not themselves determine convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(x^*\in K\) is a global minimizer.
The hierarchy uses truncations \(Q_d(g)\) of the quadratic module generated by the constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of regular KKT geometry leaves the membership assertion \(f-f^*\in Q_d(g)\) undecided for every unspecified finite \(d\).

notation.meaning: Degree-2d truncation of the quadratic module generated by the constraints.

review_flags: needs a source stating the exact regularity-based finite-convergence theorem

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record appropriately says that failure of regularity hypotheses is inconclusive rather than asserting nonconvergence. A source is necessary because finite-convergence theorems use differing constraint qualifications, complementarity conditions, and second-order hypotheses.

children.title: Finite-Convergence Decision Complexity

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Convergence Decision Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite prefixes cannot decide eventual exactness without an independent order bound or nonmembership certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an SOS hierarchy with bounds \(f_d\uparrow f^*\), finite convergence is the existential property \(\exists d\in\mathbb N\) such that \(f-f^*\in Q_d(g)\). Verifying exactness at a particular order supplies a positive certificate, but observing \(f_j<f^*\) for all \(j\le d\) excludes only those orders. Therefore no finite prefix of unsuccessful relaxations decides non-finite convergence unless additional information provides either a valid upper bound on a possible exactness order or a certificate that \(f-f^*\notin\bigcup_{j\ge0}Q_j(g)\). This is an information boundary, not by itself a formal undecidability or hardness theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact order certifies finite convergence, whereas any finite list of inexact orders cannot rule out exactness later without an external bound or nonmembership certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(f_d\) is the order-d SOS lower bound and \(f_d\le f^*\).
Exactness at order \(d\) is equivalent to \(f-f^*\in Q_d(g)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigl(\forall j\le d,\ f_j<f^*\bigr)\) does not imply \(\forall j>d,\ f_j<f^*\).
review_flags: source needed for any stronger decidability or hardness claim

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement gives a logical observation about finite prefixes and explicitly disclaims any undecidability or hardness result. It therefore does not fill the terminal container's role concerning computational decision complexity, and failure_boundary is not a substitute for an actual complexity or decidability result.

knowledge_statements.title: Effective Positivstellensatz Degree Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer from an effective positivity certificate to a sufficient SOS relaxation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge0\}\) be compact, let \(Q(g)\) be Archimedean, and let \(p\in\mathbb R[x]\) satisfy \(p(x)\ge\eta>0\) on \(K\). Suppose an effective Positivstellensatz guarantees a representation \(p=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^{m}\sigma_jg_j\) with sums of squares \(\sigma_j\) and \(\deg(\sigma_jg_j)\le D\), where \(D\) depends explicitly on dimension, input degrees and sizes, the geometry of \(K\), and \(\eta\). Then \(p\in Q_{\lceil D/2\rceil}(g)\). Applied to \(p=f-(f^*-\varepsilon)\), the order \(\lceil D(\varepsilon)/2\rceil\) SOS bound satisfies \(f_d\ge f^*-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any explicit degree bound for a positive Positivstellensatz certificate immediately yields a sufficient SOS order for the same target accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(g)\) is Archimedean and \(K\ne\varnothing\).
\(p\ge\eta>0\) on \(K\).
An effective certificate degree bound \(D\) is valid for the specified input normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\ge\lceil D/2\rceil\) implies \(p\in Q_d(g)\); for \(p=f-(f^*-\varepsilon)\), this gives \(0\le f^*-f_d\le\varepsilon\).

children.title: Canonical-Domain Convergence Rates
children.top_down_role: Rate families for boxes, spheres, simplices, and finite domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonical-Domain Convergence Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rate function for normalized polynomial optimization on a fixed canonical compact domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a compact canonical domain \(K\) and a normalized polynomial class \(\mathcal F\). For each \(f\in\mathcal F\), let \(f_d\) be its order-\(d\) SOS lower bound and \(f^*=\min_K f\). The worst-case hierarchy error is represented by \(R_{K,\mathcal F}(d)=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}(f^*-f_d)\). A claimed rate \(\rho(d)\) for a box, sphere, simplex, or finite domain means \(R_{K,\mathcal F}(d)\le\rho(d)\) under the stated normalization. Equivalently, if every \(f-(f^*-\varepsilon)\) has certificate degree at most \(D_{K,\mathcal F}(\varepsilon)\), then \(R_{K,\mathcal F}(d)\le\varepsilon\) whenever \(2d\ge D_{K,\mathcal F}(\varepsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A canonical-domain rate is the worst normalized relaxation gap, equivalently controlled by the certificate degree required for an epsilon-positive objective shift.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a fixed compact canonical domain.
\(\mathcal F\) specifies degree and coefficient or norm normalization.
The SOS hierarchy and its constraint description of \(K\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(2d\ge D_{K,\mathcal F}(\varepsilon)\) implies \(R_{K,\mathcal F}(d)\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Worst-case order-d relaxation error over the normalized class.
Uniform certificate-degree bound at accuracy epsilon.

review_flags: domain-specific rate theorems require separate sources

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record defines an abstract worst-case error but gives no rate for a box, sphere, simplex, or finite domain. Moreover, a certificate-degree bound implies the displayed error bound, but the converse requires attainment or membership hypotheses and is not established by the word 'Equivalently.' It does not supply the domain-specific rate family required by the leaf.

children.title: Sparse-Hierarchy Convergence Rates
children.top_down_role: Rate families governed by sparse support and clique geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse-Hierarchy Convergence Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clique-wise certificate degrees determine a sufficient order for a sparse SOS hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let variable cliques \(I_1,\ldots,I_s\) satisfy the running-intersection property, and suppose \(f=\sum_{\ell=1}^{s}f_\ell(x_{I_\ell})\) with every constraint assigned to a containing clique. If, for a target \(\varepsilon>0\), there exist clique-local quadratic-module certificates whose sum equals \(f-(f^*-\varepsilon)\) and whose clique-\(\ell\) terms have degree at most \(D_\ell(\varepsilon)\), then the sparse hierarchy is \(\varepsilon\)-accurate at every order \(d\ge\max_\ell\lceil D_\ell(\varepsilon)/2\rceil\). Thus the rate is governed by the largest local certificate degree, while semidefinite block sizes depend on the clique cardinalities rather than the full variable count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given compatible clique-local certificates, sparse hierarchy accuracy requires the largest local certificate order, and matrix sizes scale with clique sizes.
assumptions_latex: The clique family satisfies the running-intersection property.
Objective and constraints respect the clique decomposition.
A compatible sum of local certificates exists at accuracy \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\ge\max_\ell\lceil D_\ell(\varepsilon)/2\rceil\) implies \(0\le f^*-f_d^{\mathrm{sparse}}\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Variable index set of clique l.
Degree bound for the local certificate on clique l.

review_flags: source needed for the chosen sparse Positivstellensatz hypotheses
rate depends on decomposition and normalization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement conditionally translates already-assumed local certificate degrees into a relaxation order. It supplies no bound on those degrees as a function of accuracy, clique geometry, or normalized input data, so it is not a sparse-hierarchy convergence-rate or complexity-bound result for this container.

children.title: Slow-Convergence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Problem families without practically useful low-order convergence.

knowledge_statements.title: Slow-Convergence Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal criterion distinguishing arbitrarily slow asymptotic convergence from any uniform useful rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a normalized problem class \(\mathcal P\), write \(e_P(d)=f_P^*-f_{P,d}\ge0\). The hierarchy has no uniform rate over \(\mathcal P\) if for every function \(\rho:\mathbb N\to(0,\infty)\) with \(\rho(d)\downarrow0\), there exists \(P\in\mathcal P\) such that \(e_P(d)>\rho(d)\) for at least one order \(d\). A stronger arbitrarily-slow property requires this inequality for infinitely many \(d\). Pointwise convergence \(e_P(d)\to0\) for each fixed \(P\) is compatible with either property, so asymptotic convergence alone supplies no practically useful uniform relaxation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise convergence can coexist with the absence of every uniform rate; arbitrarily slow families defeat any proposed accuracy schedule at some or infinitely many orders.
assumptions_latex: \(f_{P,d}\le f_P^*\) for every \(P\in\mathcal P\) and \(d\).
The class \(\mathcal P\) includes a fixed input normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall\rho\downarrow0\;\exists P\in\mathcal P\;\exists d:\ f_P^*-f_{P,d}>\rho(d)\) characterizes absence of a uniform rate.

notation.meaning: Order-d hierarchy error for problem P.
Normalized family of polynomial optimization problems.

review_flags: record defines the boundary rather than asserting a particular lower-bound family

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quantifier pattern is a coherent definition of absence of a uniform rate, and failure_boundary fits the leaf. The record cites no source establishing this formulation or any SOS problem family exhibiting the stated boundary.

assumptions_latex: \(M_d(y)\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}M_d(y)=\operatorname{rank}M_{d-1}(y)=r\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction of atoms and weights from a flat positive semidefinite moment matrix.

source_refs.locator: §3.2.2, Positive and flat extensions of moment matrices, p. 61
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a flat matrix \(M_d(y)\) of rank \(r\). Select monomials \(B=\{b_1,\ldots,b_r\}\subseteq\mathbb R[x]_{\le d-1}\) whose columns form a basis and include \(1\). For each coordinate \(x_j\), express every column indexed by \(x_jb_q\) in the basis \(B\), obtaining a multiplication matrix \(X_j\). Compute the joint eigenvalue tuples of the commuting matrices \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\); these tuples are the atoms \(x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(r)}\). Recover the weights by solving \(L_y(b_q)=\sum_{i=1}^{r}w_i b_q(x^{(i)})\) for \(q=1,\ldots,r\). Output \(\mu=\sum_{i=1}^{r}w_i\delta_{x^{(i)}}\) only if the weights are positive and the reconstructed moments satisfy the declared residual tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a moment-column basis of degree at most d-1, construct the coordinate multiplication matrices from available degree-d columns, recover atoms from their joint eigenvalues, and solve the basis-moment system for positive weights.
knowledge_statements.title: Finitely Atomic Measure Recovery

children.title: Optimizer-Support Recovery

knowledge_statements.title: Optimizer-Support Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An exact atomic optimal moment representation certifies every recovered support point as a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y\) be feasible for a moment relaxation of \(f^*=\min_{x\in K}f(x)\), and suppose extraction gives \(y_\alpha=\sum_{i=1}^{r}w_i(x^{(i)})^\alpha\) with \(w_i>0\), \(x^{(i)}\in K\), and \(\sum_iw_i=1\). If the relaxation is value-exact, then \(f^*=L_y(f)=\sum_iw_if(x^{(i)})\). Since feasibility gives \(f(x^{(i)})\ge f^*\) for every atom, positivity of all weights forces \(f(x^{(i)})=f^*\) for each \(i\). Consequently the recovered support is contained in the global minimizer set; equality with that set is not guaranteed when additional minimizers carry no recovered mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an exact optimal atomic moment solution, every positive-weight feasible atom is a global minimizer, though the recovered support may omit other minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(y\) represents the displayed atomic measure through the degree of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{supp}\mu\subseteq\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K}f(x)\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The atomic weights are uniquely recovered as \(w=V^{-1}(y_{\alpha_1},\ldots,y_{\alpha_r})^\mathsf T\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select \(r\) available moments whose evaluation matrix \(V\) is nonsingular and form \(m=(y_{\alpha_1},\ldots,y_{\alpha_r})^\mathsf T\). Since the representing identity gives \(m=Vw\), solve \(Vw=m\). The resulting vector is the unique weight vector supported on the prescribed atoms that matches these moments. It also matches every available moment precisely when \(y_\alpha=\sum_{j=1}^r w_j(x^{(j)})^\alpha\) for all \(|\alpha|\le 2d\). Positivity of the representing measure requires \(w_j>0\) for every \(j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a nonsingular evaluation system using recovered atoms and selected moments; the solution gives the unique atomic weights and must reproduce all available moments.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Dimensional Quotient Algebra and Multiplication Operators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quotient-algebra structure associated with a zero-dimensional polynomial ideal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an ideal $J\subseteq\mathbb R[\mathbf x]$, the quotient algebra $\mathbb R[\mathbf x]/J$ consists of cosets $[f]=f+J$, with $[f]+[g]=[f+g]$, $\lambda[f]=[\lambda f]$, and $[f][g]=[fg]$. If $J$ is zero-dimensional, it is a finite-dimensional real vector space and $\dim_{\mathbb R}(\mathbb R[\mathbf x]/J)\geq |V_{\mathbb C}(J)|$, with equality if $J$ is radical. For every $h\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]$, multiplication by $h$ defines the linear operator $m_h([f])=[fh]$, represented in any quotient basis $\mathcal B_J$ by a multiplication matrix $\mathbf M_h$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quotient by an ideal consists of polynomial cosets and inherits vector-space and algebra operations. For a zero-dimensional ideal it is finite-dimensional, its dimension is at least the number of complex variety points, and equality holds if the ideal is radical. Multiplication by a polynomial induces a linear operator represented by a multiplication matrix in any quotient basis.
assumptions_latex: J\subseteq\mathbb R[\mathbf x]\text{ is an ideal}
J\text{ is zero-dimensional for the finiteness and dimension assertions}
h\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb R[\mathbf x]/J\text{ is a finite-dimensional algebra},\quad \dim_{\mathbb R}(\mathbb R[\mathbf x]/J)\geq |V_{\mathbb C}(J)|,\quad m_h([f])=[fh].

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(r\) linearly independent columns of \(M_d(y)\), indexed by monomials \(B=\{b_1,\ldots,b_r\}\), so that \(M_B\) is nonsingular. For every coordinate \(x_i\) and basis element \(b_j\), solve \(M_Bc^{(i,j)}=M_d(y)[B,x_i b_j]\). Define the \(j\)-th column of \(T_i\) to be \(c^{(i,j)}\). Under flatness, these relations consistently reduce every \(x_i b_j\) to the span of \(B\), and the residue classes of \(B\) constitute a basis of the finite-dimensional quotient algebra associated with the moment kernel.

assumptions_latex: A flat moment sequence yields an \(r\)-dimensional quotient algebra with multiplication matrices \(T_1,\ldots,T_n\).
The matrices commute and are self-adjoint for the positive-definite moment inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The joint eigenvalue tuples of \((T_1,\ldots,T_n)\) are exactly the \(r\) real support points of the representing measure, counted without multiplicity.

The tuples \(x^{(j)}=(x_1^{(j)},\ldots,x_n^{(j)})\) are precisely the atoms of the unique rank-\(r\) representing measure. Equivalently, a generic real linear combination \(T(\xi)=\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_iT_i\) with simple spectrum supplies eigenvectors common to all \(T_i\), and evaluating each \(T_i\) on those eigenvectors recovers the corresponding coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible self-adjoint multiplication matrices admit common eigenvectors, and their joint real eigenvalue tuples are exactly the atoms of the flat representing measure.

children.title: Real-Support Screening
children.top_down_role: Screening of algebraic candidates for real-valued support.

assumptions_latex: Candidate tuples \(z^{(j)}\in\mathbb C^n\) have been obtained from numerical joint spectral extraction.
A screening tolerance \(\tau_{\mathrm{real}}\ge 0\) and a fixed vector norm are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The retained index set is \(J_{\mathrm{real}}=\{j:\|\operatorname{Im}z^{(j)}\|\le\tau_{\mathrm{real}}\}\), with real representatives \(x^{(j)}=\operatorname{Re}z^{(j)}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-based numerical screening; exact arithmetic corresponds to zero tolerance.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A spectral candidate \(z^{(j)}\) passes real-support screening exactly when \(\|\operatorname{Im}z^{(j)}\|\le\tau_{\mathrm{real}}\). For every passing candidate, use \(x^{(j)}=\operatorname{Re}z^{(j)}\) as its real representative. In exact arithmetic, set \(\tau_{\mathrm{real}}=0\), so passing is equivalent to \(z^{(j)}\in\mathbb R^n\). In floating-point extraction, the tolerance must be interpreted relative to the coordinate scaling and backward error; passing this test establishes numerical realness only and does not establish feasibility for the original polynomial constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep candidates whose imaginary parts are below a declared tolerance and replace them by their real parts; this test alone does not establish constraint feasibility.

Nonnegative tolerances \(\tau_g\) and \(\tau_h\) are specified for real candidate points.

With \(\tau_g=\tau_h=0\), this predicate is exactly membership in \(K\). Positive tolerances define only approximate feasibility and should be chosen using polynomial and coordinate scaling. If feasibility is required rigorously, interval evaluation or another certified residual bound must replace unverified floating-point evaluations.

children.title: Spurious Complex Candidates
children.top_down_role: Nonreal algebraic outputs arising during spectral recovery.

assumptions_latex: Exact extraction would produce commuting moment-self-adjoint multiplication matrices.
Numerical construction permits a nonsymmetric perturbation of an extracted multiplication matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Complex spectral candidates can be perturbation artifacts and cannot be interpreted as atoms of a real representing measure merely because their imaginary parts are small.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete numerical mechanism producing nonreal eigenvalues from an exact real support point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an exact two-dimensional zero multiplication operator \(T=0\), whose only spectral coordinate is real. The nonsymmetric perturbation \(\widehat T=\begin{pmatrix}0&-\varepsilon\\ \varepsilon&0\end{pmatrix}\), with \(\varepsilon>0\), has eigenvalues \(\pm i\varepsilon\). Thus an arbitrarily small loss of moment-self-adjointness can create nonreal candidates even when the exact operator has only real spectrum. Such candidates are not atoms of a measure on \(\mathbb R^n\); they must be rejected or treated through a backward-error criterion, and small imaginary parts alone do not prove the existence of nearby feasible atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An arbitrarily small nonsymmetric operator perturbation can create complex eigenvalues from an exact real spectrum, so those candidates are not automatically real measure atoms.
knowledge_statements.title: Spurious Complex Candidates
