knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Based Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic projection of truncated data onto a finite-atomic moment model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(R(w,x)=\sum_{|\alpha|\le d}c_\alpha\left(y_\alpha-\sum_{j=1}^r w_j(x^{(j)})^\alpha\right)^2\). Minimize \(R\) over \(x^{(j)}\in K\), \(w_j\ge 0\), and \(\sum_{j=1}^r w_j=y_0\). Initialize the atoms and weights by a declared deterministic rule, apply the chosen constrained solver until its stated residual or stationarity tolerance is met, and output \(\widehat\mu=\sum_{j=1}^r w_j\delta_{x^{(j)}}\). The output is a global weighted least-squares projection only when global optimality is certified; otherwise it is a computed approximate projection associated with the attained objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fit a constrained finite-atomic measure by minimizing weighted low-degree moment residuals; call the result a global projection only when global optimality is certified.
assumptions_latex: A truncated moment vector \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le d}\), a closed set \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and an atom budget \(r\) are given.
Positive residual weights \(c_\alpha>0\) and a rule for solving the finite optimization problem are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a computed atomic measure with weighted discrepancy \(R\); it minimizes \(R\) over the prescribed model class only if global optimality is certified.

source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(K=[-1,1]\), the probability measures \(\mu_1=\delta_0\) and \(\mu_2=\tfrac12\delta_{-1}+\tfrac12\delta_1\) have identical moments of degrees zero and one: \(\int 1\,d\mu_1=\int 1\,d\mu_2=1\) and \(\int x\,d\mu_1=\int x\,d\mu_2=0\). Their supports differ, and their second moments are respectively \(0\) and \(1\). Hence exact fidelity to a low-degree truncation does not by itself imply support recovery, uniqueness of the representing measure, or fidelity at higher degrees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distinct measures can share all observed low-degree moments while having different supports and higher moments, so low-degree matching alone cannot guarantee faithful optimizer recovery.
knowledge_statements.title: Low-Degree Fidelity Boundaries

children.title: Moment-Data Rounding
children.top_down_role: Candidate construction from approximate moment solutions.

assumptions_latex: A relaxation supplies \(y_0>0\) and first moments \(y_{e_i}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\).
A nonempty closed feasible set \(K\) and a deterministic tie-breaking rule for Euclidean projection are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rounded point is \(x^{\mathrm{rnd}}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K}\|x-m\|_2\), where \(m_i=y_{e_i}/y_0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-moment rounding followed by deterministic Euclidean feasibility projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Normalize the relaxation by setting \(m_i=y_{e_i}/y_0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\). Compute a Euclidean projection \(x^{\mathrm{rnd}}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K}\|x-m\|_2\), using the prescribed tie-breaking rule if the projection is not unique, and return \(x^{\mathrm{rnd}}\). If the projection subproblem is solved only approximately, return a point satisfying the declared projection tolerance. This procedure yields a feasible representative when the projection is computed globally, but the moment relaxation alone supplies no general objective-value guarantee for this rounding rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize the first moments and project their vector onto the feasible set; feasibility requires a global or certified approximate solution of the projection problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Moment-Data Rounding

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projection rule is mathematically well-defined for a nonempty closed set with deterministic tie-breaking, but no source supports adopting this particular first-moment rule in the SOS recovery context.

children.title: Gram-Data Rounding
children.top_down_role: Candidate construction from approximate Gram representations.

assumptions_latex: A positive semidefinite Gram matrix \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^N\) with unit diagonal represents relaxed pairwise products for binary variables.
A factorization \(Q=VV^\mathsf T\), a standard Gaussian vector \(g\), and a fixed reference index \(0\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The randomized rounded vector has coordinates \(x_i=\operatorname{sign}(v_i^\mathsf Tg)\operatorname{sign}(v_0^\mathsf Tg)\in\{-1,1\}\).

notation.meaning: row vectors of a Gram factor

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian hyperplane rounding for binary Gram data, not a universal SOS extraction rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Compute a Gram factorization \(Q=VV^\mathsf T\), with row vectors \(v_0,v_1,
ldots,v_N\). Draw \(g\sim\mathcal N(0,I)\) and set \(s_i=\operatorname{sign}(v_i^\mathsf Tg)\), using a fixed convention at zero. Return \(x_i=s_is_0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,N\). The output belongs to \(\{-1,1\}^N\) and converts Gram correlations into correlated binary decisions. Additional deterministic constraints must be enforced by a separate repair or rejection step, and any approximation guarantee depends on the particular objective and relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor the Gram matrix, cut its vectors with a random Gaussian hyperplane, and orient signs by a reference vector to obtain binary decisions.
knowledge_statements.title: Gram-Data Rounding

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports this specialized binary hyperplane-rounding rule. In addition, \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^N\) conflicts with rows indexed from \(0\) through \(N\), and the statement contains the literal typo “nldots.”

children.title: Randomized Rounding Regimes
children.top_down_role: Recovery variants using randomized candidate selection from relaxation data.

assumptions_latex: A relaxation provides a normalized mean \(m\) and positive semidefinite covariance surrogate \(\Sigma\).
A sampling distribution, feasible repair map \(P_K\), sample count \(N\), and objective \(f\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns the lowest-objective feasible point among \(P_K(m+L\xi^{(1)}),\ldots,P_K(m+L\xi^{(N)})\), where \(LL^\mathsf T=\Sigma\).

notation.meaning: covariance surrogate derived from relaxation data

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic covariance-based sampling, repair, and incumbent selection for nonflat relaxation data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(L\) with \(LL^\mathsf T=\Sigma\). Independently draw \(\xi^{(s)}\) from the declared centered unit-covariance distribution for \(s=1,\ldots,N\), form \(z^{(s)}=m+L\xi^{(s)}\), and compute \(x^{(s)}=P_K(z^{(s)})\). Discard any point that fails the stated feasibility check. Stop after \(N\) samples or an explicitly declared incumbent criterion, and return a surviving point minimizing \(f(x^{(s)})\); report failure if none survives. Moment and covariance matching specify the sampling regime but do not alone imply an approximation ratio or convergence to an optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample candidates from a distribution fitted to relaxation mean and covariance, repair them to feasibility, and return the best feasible sampled point.
knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Rounding Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic sampling-and-repair scheme is plausible and appropriately disclaims performance guarantees, but it has no supporting source and does not explicitly require the sample count \(N\) to be a positive integer.

children.title: Local Refinement Interface
children.top_down_role: Transfer of hierarchy-derived candidates to local polynomial optimization.

assumptions_latex: The polynomial optimization problem is \(f^*=\min\{f(x):x\in K\}\), where \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\) and \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is closed.
A hierarchy relaxation supplies a feasible candidate \(\hat x\in K\) and a certified lower bound \(\rho\le f^*\).
When initialized at \(\hat x\), the selected local solver returns a point \(x^{\mathrm{loc}}\in K\) without increasing the objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned point \(x^{\mathrm{loc}}\) satisfies \(f(x^{\mathrm{loc}})\le f(\hat x)\), and \(0\le f(x^{\mathrm{loc}})-f^*\le f(x^{\mathrm{loc}})-\rho\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible candidate transfer with an a posteriori global gap, conditional on the selected local solver returning a feasible nonascending point; no claim that local refinement alone finds a global minimizer.

source_refs.locator: 5.1 The Primal and Dual Perspectives p. 110
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

source_refs.locator: 1.2.2 'Globalized' Local Optimization Strategies, Combined with Grid Search or Random Search p. 24
source_refs.source_title: Global Optimization in Action

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the selected local polynomial solver at \(x_0=\hat x\) while retaining the relaxation lower bound \(\rho\). If the solver returns a feasible point \(x^{\mathrm{loc}}\) through nonascending accepted updates, then \(f(x^{\mathrm{loc}})\le f(\hat x)\), and \(f(x^{\mathrm{loc}})-\rho\) is a computable upper bound on the global suboptimality \(f(x^{\mathrm{loc}})-f^*\). Any stationarity guarantee is the guarantee supplied by the selected local solver and does not by itself certify global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize local refinement at a feasible hierarchy candidate and retain the relaxation lower bound; if the solver returns a feasible nonascending point, its objective minus that bound upper-bounds global suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Refinement Interface

children.title: Unique-Minimizer Regime
children.top_down_role: Moment behavior and extraction associated with a single optimizer.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) is compact and \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\).
The minimizer set is the singleton \(X^*=\{x^*\}\).
Every weak-* accumulation point of the relaxation measures is supported on \(X^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every such limiting measure equals \(\delta_{x^*}\), and its moments satisfy \(y_\alpha=(x^*)^\alpha\) for every multi-index \(\alpha\).

notation.meaning: Dirac probability measure at the minimizer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measure-limit characterization after the hierarchy has established support on the optimizer set.

source_refs.locator: 5.1 The Primal and Dual Perspectives p. 110
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mu\) be any probability measure arising as a weak-* accumulation point of relaxation measures and suppose \(\operatorname{supp}\mu\subseteq X^*\). Since \(X^*=\{x^*\}\), necessarily \(\mu=\delta_{x^*}\). Consequently, for every multi-index \(\alpha\in\mathbb N^n\), \(y_\alpha=\int_K x^\alpha\,d\mu(x)=(x^*)^\alpha\). In particular, the first moments equal \(x^*\), so optimizer extraction from convergent first moments is unique and independent of the chosen convergent subsequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the optimizer is unique, every limiting optimizer-supported probability measure is its Dirac mass, so all limiting moments identify the same point.
knowledge_statements.title: Unique-Minimizer Regime

source_witnesses.locator: 5.1 The Primal and Dual Perspectives p. 110
source_witnesses.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

children.title: Finite Multiple-Minimizer Regime
children.top_down_role: Atomic extraction when several isolated optimizers coexist.

assumptions_latex: The global minimizer set is finite: \(X^*=\{x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(r)}\}\subset K\).
A truncated feasible moment sequence \(y\) admits a representing probability measure supported on \(X^*\).
At some order \(d\), the applicable flat-extension rank condition holds with rank \(s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The representing measure has exactly \(s\le r\) positive atoms among the minimizers and can be recovered from the flat moment data.

notation.meaning: Truncated moment matrix of order d

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite atomic recovery under a hierarchy-appropriate flat-extension condition.

source_refs.locator: 5.1 The Primal and Dual Perspectives p. 110
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Any representing probability measure supported on \(X^*\) has the form \[\mu=\sum_{j=1}^{r}w_j\delta_{x^{(j)}},\qquad w_j\ge0,\qquad\sum_{j=1}^{r}w_j=1.\] If the relevant truncated moment matrix satisfies the flat-extension condition and \(\operatorname{rank}M_d(y)=s\), then the positive-weight support contains exactly \(s\) points. These atoms and their weights are recoverable from multiplication operators, or an equivalent flat-moment extraction procedure, and every recovered atom lies in \(X^*\). Zero-weight minimizers need not be recovered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A flat optimizer-supported moment sequence on finitely many minimizers represents a finite atomic measure whose positive-weight atoms and weights are algebraically extractable.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Multiple-Minimizer Regime

source_witnesses.locator: 5.1 The Primal and Dual Perspectives p. 110
source_witnesses.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-atomic representation fits the leaf, but the phrase "applicable flat-extension rank condition" does not state the actual rank equality or its degree offset. Those details determine whether exactly rank-many atoms and feasible optimizer extraction follow. The cited general section is not a sufficiently specific locator for this extraction theorem, so an authoritative theorem or section is required.

children.title: Continuum-Minimizer Regime
children.top_down_role: Measure-valued limits and nonunique extraction for positive-dimensional minimizer sets.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is compact, and the global minimizer set \(X^*\subseteq K\) is not finite.
A relaxation measure has a weak-* accumulation point \(\mu\) that is a probability measure satisfying \(\operatorname{supp}\mu\subseteq X^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\mu\) has infinite support, its moments do not admit finite flat extraction of its entire support; if optimizer-supported accumulation measures are not unique, moment convergence need not select a unique optimizer.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of finite atomic identification for optimizer-supported accumulation measures with infinite support; an infinite minimizer set alone does not imply that every supported measure is non-atomic.

source_refs.locator: 5.1 The Primal and Dual Perspectives p. 110
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an optimizer-supported accumulation measure \(\mu\), define \(y_\alpha=\int_{X^*}x^\alpha\,d\mu(x)\) for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb N^n\). If \(\mu\) has infinite support, its full moment matrix has infinite rank, so finite flat extraction cannot recover its entire support as finitely many atoms. Distinct optimizer-supported accumulation measures may produce distinct moment limits, and a first-moment barycenter \(\int_{X^*}x\,d\mu(x)\) need not lie in a nonconvex set \(X^*\). Consequently, absent an additional selection or finite-support condition, moment convergence does not generally determine a unique optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimizer-supported limit measure with infinite support cannot have its entire support recovered by finite flat extraction, and nonunique limit measures need not select a unique optimizer or a feasible barycenter.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuum-Minimizer Regime

children.title: Correlative-Sparsity Graphs
children.top_down_role: Variable-interaction representations used to organize sparse hierarchy blocks.

assumptions_latex: The problem contains an objective polynomial \(f\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) and constraint polynomials \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The graph records precisely which variable pairs occur together in at least one monomial support relevant to the polynomial optimization problem.

notation.meaning: Support of a polynomial in multi-index space

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: correlative sparsity is conventionally encoded by co-occurrence of variables in objective or constraint monomials
source_gap: supplied locators do not specifically document correlative-sparsity graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monomial co-occurrence version of the correlative-sparsity graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The correlative-sparsity graph is the undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) with \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). For distinct \(i,j\in V\), put \(\{i,j\}\in E\) when there exists \(p\in\{f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\}\) and \(\alpha\in\operatorname{supp}(p)\) such that \(i,j\in\operatorname{supp}(\alpha)\), where \(\operatorname{supp}(\alpha)=\{k:\alpha_k>0\}\). A chosen chordal extension may add edges before maximal cliques are formed, but those fill edges are distinguished from the original interaction edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variables are adjacent when they occur together in a monomial of the objective or a constraint; chordal completion may add fill edges for decomposition.
knowledge_statements.title: Correlative-Sparsity Graphs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A definition is the correct content kind, but no citation is supplied. Moreover, standard sparse-SOS formulations vary on whether variables appearing anywhere in the same constraint are made adjacent or only variables co-occurring in one monomial are adjacent. The selected convention materially affects clique assignment and must be tied to a specific authoritative source.

children.title: Clique-Tree Regularity Structure
children.top_down_role: Clique geometry supporting sparse certificate consistency and convergence.

children.title: Sparsity Clique Covers
children.top_down_role: Clique decompositions of correlative-sparsity graphs.

assumptions_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be the correlative-sparsity graph, possibly after a chosen chordal extension.
Let \(I_1,\ldots,I_q\subseteq V\) be clique index sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every polynomial datum is assigned to a clique containing all variables on which it depends, enabling clique-local moment and SOS blocks.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sparse SOS decompositions require each polynomial datum to fit inside an assigned variable clique
source_gap: no supplied locator specifically supports clique covers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clique cover condition for assigning objective terms and constraints to sparse hierarchy blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The family \(\mathcal I=\{I_1,\ldots,I_q\}\) is a sparsity clique cover when \(\bigcup_{k=1}^{q}I_k=V\), every edge of \(G\) is contained in some \(I_k\), and each \(I_k\) induces a clique in the selected chordal extension. In addition, the objective must admit \(f=\sum_{k=1}^{q}f_k\) with \(f_k\in\mathbb R[x_{I_k}]\), and every constraint \(g_j\) must be assigned to at least one clique \(I_k\) satisfying \(\operatorname{var}(g_j)\subseteq I_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid clique cover contains every variable interaction and assigns every objective term and constraint to a clique containing all of its variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity Clique Covers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the terminal container and is internally coherent, but it combines a graph clique cover, an objective decomposition, and whole-constraint assignment without any inspectable citation. A sparse-SOS source must establish the intended convention and assignment requirements.

children.title: Running-Intersection Property
children.top_down_role: Clique-order structure supporting consistent sparse decompositions.

assumptions_latex: The clique sets are ordered as \(I_1,\ldots,I_q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each noninitial clique attaches through an overlap wholly contained in one earlier clique.

notation.meaning: Parent index chosen for clique k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: displayed containment is the standard running-intersection predicate
source_gap: no supplied locator specifically supports the running-intersection property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered-clique form of the running-intersection property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The ordered family \(I_1,\ldots,I_q\) has the running-intersection property if, for every \(k\in\{2,\ldots,q\}\), there exists an index \(p(k)<k\) such that \[I_k\cap\left(\bigcup_{j<k}I_j\right)\subseteq I_{p(k)}.\] Equivalently, the cliques can be arranged as a clique tree for which, whenever a variable index belongs to two clique nodes, it belongs to every clique along the unique tree path joining those nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cliques satisfy running intersection when each new clique's overlap with all earlier cliques is contained in one earlier parent clique.
knowledge_statements.title: Running-Intersection Property

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed containment and clique-tree equivalence are the standard running-intersection condition, and the content kind is correct. However, the record has no source with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator, so it cannot pass evidence review.

children.title: Clique-Tree Consistency Consequences
children.top_down_role: Implications of clique-tree structure for local certificate compatibility.

assumptions_latex: The clique family satisfies the running-intersection property.
For every clique \(I_k\), \(\mu_k\) is a probability measure on a common product Borel space.
Adjacent clique measures have identical marginals on their separator variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists a global probability measure whose marginal on every clique equals the prescribed clique measure.

notation.meaning: Separator between clique k and its parent
Coordinate projection onto an index set

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: consistent probability marginals on a junction tree admit a global gluing
source_gap: exact measure-gluing theorem and hypotheses require an authoritative sparse-moment source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Junction-tree gluing consequence for exact clique measures, not merely truncated pseudo-moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every nonroot clique \(I_k\), require separator consistency \[(\pi_{S_k})_{\#}\mu_k=(\pi_{S_k})_{\#}\mu_{p(k)},\qquad S_k=I_k\cap I_{p(k)}.\] Then there exists a probability measure \(\mu\) on the variables indexed by \(\bigcup_k I_k\) such that \((\pi_{I_k})_{\#}\mu=\mu_k\) for all \(k\). Thus all clique expectations of the same overlap polynomial agree. The assertion concerns genuine measures; positive semidefinite truncated local moment matrices without representing measures do not by themselves satisfy its hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a running-intersection clique tree, genuine clique measures with matching separator marginals can be glued into one global measure with those clique marginals.
knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Tree Consistency Consequences

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A theorem is the correct role for this clique-tree consequence, and the distinction between genuine measures and truncated pseudo-moments is appropriate. No source is provided for the gluing theorem or for the needed measurable-space hypotheses, so the conclusion cannot be accepted as sourced candidate-review knowledge.

children.title: Clique-Local Moment Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Moment blocks restricted to variable cliques.

assumptions_latex: The objective decomposes as \(f=\sum_k f_k\) with \(f_k\in\mathbb R[x_{I_k}]\).
Each constraint \(g_j\) is assigned to a clique containing its variables.
A relaxation order \(d\) is at least half every required polynomial degree, rounded upward.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed semidefinite program is the order-\(d\) clique-local moment lower-bound relaxation.

notation.meaning: Truncated moment sequence on clique k
Riesz functional associated with local moments

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic clique-local primal SDP with localizing constraints and overlap-moment equalities.

source_refs.locator: 5.1 The Primal and Dual Perspectives p. 110
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r_j=\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\), the clique-local order-\(d\) relaxation is \[\inf_{\{y^{(k)}\}}\ \sum_k L_{y^{(k)}}(f_k)\] subject to \(y^{(k)}_0=1\), \(M_d(y^{(k)})\succeq0\), and \(M_{d-r_j}(g_jy^{(k)})\succeq0\) for every constraint \(g_j\) assigned to clique \(I_k\). For each clique pair and every monomial supported on \(I_k\cap I_\ell\) of degree at most \(2d\), impose equality of the corresponding entries of \(y^{(k)}\) and \(y^{(\ell)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sparse primal relaxation uses one moment matrix per clique, localizing matrices for assigned constraints, and equality of moments shared by clique overlaps.

source_witnesses.locator: 5.1 The Primal and Dual Perspectives p. 110

Because these choices affect the exact primal and its dual, a sparse-moment hierarchy source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Clique-Local SOS Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Certificate blocks restricted to variable cliques.

assumptions_latex: The objective and constraints have the clique assignments used by the local moment relaxation.
The relaxation order is \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Maximizing \(\gamma\) over the displayed clique-local SOS identity gives the dual sparse lower bound.

notation.meaning: SOS multiplier for constraint j in clique k
SOS cone in clique variables with degree at most 2d

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clique-supported quadratic-module certificate dual to a compatible local moment formulation.

source_refs.locator: 5.1 The Primal and Dual Perspectives p. 110
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The clique-local SOS relaxation maximizes \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\) subject to an identity \[f-\gamma=\sum_{k=1}^{q}\left(\sigma_{0k}+\sum_{j\in J_k}\sigma_{jk}g_j\right),\] where \(\sigma_{0k}\in\Sigma[x_{I_k}]_{2d}\), each \(\sigma_{jk}\in\Sigma[x_{I_k}]\), and \(\deg(\sigma_{jk}g_j)\le2d\). Here \(J_k\) contains constraints assigned to clique \(I_k\). Any feasible identity implies \(f(x)\ge\gamma\) for every point satisfying all \(g_j(x)\ge0\), so \(\gamma\) is a certified global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sparse dual writes the objective minus a lower bound as a sum of clique-supported SOS terms and clique-local constraint multipliers.
knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Local SOS Relaxations

source_witnesses.locator: 5.1 The Primal and Dual Perspectives p. 110
source_witnesses.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The clique-supported SOS identity is a valid lower-bound certificate, and representation is an appropriate kind. However, the supplied locator does not establish that this precise identity is the dual of the preceding overlap-coupled moment program. Explicit overlap equalities can introduce separator-polynomial dual variables, so the exact parameterization requires a specific sparse-SOS source.

children.title: Local Primal–Dual Coupling
children.top_down_role: Finite-level pairing between clique-local moment plus certificate blocks.

assumptions_latex: The clique-local moment SDP and SOS SDP are a finite-dimensional primal-dual pair at the same order.
The local moment formulation has a strictly feasible point satisfying all overlap equalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal and dual optimal values coincide, and the SOS optimum is attained when the common value is finite.

notation.meaning: Clique-local moment optimum at order d
Clique-local SOS optimum at order d

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-order conic duality under primal Slater feasibility.

source_refs.locator: 5.1 The Primal and Dual Perspectives p. 110
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Weak conic duality always gives \(p_d^{\mathrm{sos}}\le p_d^{\mathrm{mom}}\). If there exists a collection of clique-local moment sequences satisfying the affine normalization and overlap constraints while every required moment and localizing matrix lies in the relative interior of its prescribed positive semidefinite cone, then semidefinite-programming strong duality yields \[p_d^{\mathrm{sos}}=p_d^{\mathrm{mom}}.\] When this common value is finite, the dual SOS optimum is attained. The overlap-moment equalities are affine coupling constraints, and their dual variables supply the separator-polynomial terms in an explicitly coupled dual formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed order, compatible clique moment and SOS programs satisfy weak duality, and a suitable Slater point removes the gap and yields dual attainment.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Primal–Dual Coupling

source_witnesses.locator: 5.1 The Primal and Dual Perspectives p. 110
source_witnesses.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Duality is the correct content kind, and the stated Slater consequence is standard for a correctly identified finite-dimensional conic pair. Here the preceding primal and SOS formulations have not been shown to be exact duals, and the cited general section does not resolve the separator-variable formulation or relative-interior hypothesis. A source for the selected coupled SDP pair is required.

children.title: Clique Compatibility-Extraction Interface
children.top_down_role: Compatibility and recovery interfaces for local moment data.

children.title: Clique-Overlap Consistency
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of local moment data across overlapping cliques.

assumptions_latex: For each clique \(I_k\), a truncated sequence \(y^{(k)}\) contains moments through degree \(2d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Consistency means that every shared monomial receives the same moment value from every clique containing its variables.

notation.meaning: Truncated local moment sequence for clique k
Overlap of cliques k and l

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: overlap consistency is equality of all shared truncated moments
source_gap: no supplied locator specifically supports sparse clique extraction compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree-\(2d\) equality predicate for truncated moments on clique intersections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The clique-local sequences are overlap-consistent through degree \(2d\) if, for every pair \(k,\ell\) and every multi-index \(\alpha\in\mathbb N^n\) satisfying \(\operatorname{supp}(\alpha)\subseteq S_{k\ell}=I_k\cap I_\ell\) and \(|\alpha|\le2d\), one has \[y^{(k)}_\alpha=y^{(\ell)}_\alpha.\] On a clique tree it suffices to impose these equalities on tree edges, because equality propagates along paths when the running-intersection property holds. For extracted atomic measures, moment equality is necessary but, at a fixed truncation order, need not imply equality of the full overlap marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clique moments are compatible when all moments up to the relaxation degree agree on every shared variable set; tree-edge equalities suffice under running intersection.
knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Overlap Consistency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly expresses equality of shared truncated moments and appropriately warns that finite moment agreement need not imply equality of full marginals. The tree-edge sufficiency claim also depends on running intersection. With no cited source or locator, the record does not satisfy the evidence requirement.

children.title: Sparse Measure Extraction
children.top_down_role: Recovery of global measure information from clique-local moment data.

assumptions_latex: The clique family (I_t)_{t=1}^m has the running-intersection property.

Each truncated clique moment sequence y^{(t)} has a positive semidefinite moment matrix satisfying \operatorname{rank}M_d(y^{(t)})=\operatorname{rank}M_{d-r}(y^{(t)}) for a valid flat-extension offset r.
The extracted clique measures have identical marginals on every separator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each flat clique sequence determines a finite atomic measure \mu_t on \mathbb R^{I_t}. Root the clique tree and successively couple each child measure to its parent along their common separator, using their shared separator marginal. The running-intersection property ensures that this construction produces a finite global measure \mu on \mathbb R^n satisfying (\pi_{I_t})_{\#}\mu=\mu_t for every t. Consequently, all moments indexed within a clique agree with the corresponding moments of \mu; when the clique atoms and separator matchings are explicitly computed, the construction yields a sparse atomic global representing measure.

notation.meaning: Variable index set of clique t.
Truncated moment sequence on clique t.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite atomic extraction on a running-intersection clique tree with flat local moment matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Each flat clique sequence determines a finite atomic measure \mu_t on \mathbb R^{I_t}. Root the clique tree and successively couple each child measure to its parent along their common separator, using their shared separator marginal. The running-intersection property ensures that this construction produces a finite global measure \mu on \mathbb R^n satisfying (\pi_{I_t})_{\#}\mu=\mu_t for every t. Consequently, all moments indexed within a clique agree with the corresponding moments of \mu; when the clique atoms and separator matchings are explicitly computed, the construction yields a sparse atomic global representing measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible flat clique moment sequences on a running-intersection clique tree can be joined into a finite atomic global measure having the prescribed clique marginals.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Measure Extraction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the extraction leaf, but no citation supports the flat-extension offset or the local-to-global gluing theorem. The statement also places TeX commands outside math delimiters; source-supported revision is required.

children.title: Local-to-Global Extraction Failures
children.top_down_role: Compatibility boundaries preventing assembly of globally valid recovered solutions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Let X_1,X_2,X_3 take values in \{0,1\}, and use cliques \{1,2\}, \{2,3\}, and \{1,3\}. On the first two cliques take the uniform measure on \{(0,0),(1,1)\}, while on the third take the uniform measure on \{(0,1),(1,0)\}. Every singleton marginal is uniform, so all pairwise clique-overlap consistency conditions hold. A global measure would nevertheless imply simultaneously X_1=X_2, X_2=X_3, and X_1\ne X_3 almost surely, which is impossible. Thus locally representable, overlap-consistent clique data need not admit a global representing measure when the clique hypergraph lacks an acyclic running-intersection structure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A three-cycle of binary pairwise marginals exhibits failure without running intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let X_1,X_2,X_3 take values in \{0,1\}, and use cliques \{1,2\}, \{2,3\}, and \{1,3\}. On the first two cliques take the uniform measure on \{(0,0),(1,1)\}, while on the third take the uniform measure on \{(0,1),(1,0)\}. Every singleton marginal is uniform, so all pairwise clique-overlap consistency conditions hold. A global measure would nevertheless imply simultaneously X_1=X_2, X_2=X_3, and X_1\ne X_3 almost surely, which is impossible. Thus locally representable, overlap-consistent clique data need not admit a global representing measure when the clique hypergraph lacks an acyclic running-intersection structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Three pairwise binary measures can agree on every singleton overlap yet be globally inconsistent, showing why running-intersection structure is essential for local-to-global extraction.
knowledge_statements.title: Local-to-Global Extraction Failures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary three-cycle is a valid counterexample and the content kind fits the failure leaf, but it has no cited source and its TeX notation is not explicitly delimited.

children.title: Term-Support Graphs
children.top_down_role: Graph representations of monomial interactions.

assumptions_latex: A finite monomial basis B\subseteq\mathbb N^n and a target exponent support A\subseteq B+B are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The term-support graph associated with (B,A) is the undirected graph G(B,A)=(B,E_A) whose vertices are monomial exponents and whose edges satisfy \{\beta,\gamma\}\in E_A if and only if \beta\ne\gamma and \beta+\gamma\in A. A Gram entry indexed by (\beta,\gamma) contributes to the coefficient of x^{\beta+\gamma}; hence edges record precisely the off-diagonal monomial interactions directly visible in the target support. Diagonal interactions may be represented by loops or, equivalently, tracked separately through the set \{2\beta:\beta\in B\}.

notation.meaning: Finite exponent set indexing a monomial basis.
Term-support graph determined by B and A.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph representation for interactions in a fixed finite monomial basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The term-support graph associated with (B,A) is the undirected graph G(B,A)=(B,E_A) whose vertices are monomial exponents and whose edges satisfy \{\beta,\gamma\}\in E_A if and only if \beta\ne\gamma and \beta+\gamma\in A. A Gram entry indexed by (\beta,\gamma) contributes to the coefficient of x^{\beta+\gamma}; hence edges record precisely the off-diagonal monomial interactions directly visible in the target support. Diagonal interactions may be represented by loops or, equivalently, tracked separately through the set \{2\beta:\beta\in B\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A term-support graph joins two basis monomials exactly when their exponent sum belongs to the target polynomial support.
knowledge_statements.title: Term-Support Graphs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the container, but TSSOS term-support graphs use formulation-specific support and diagonal conventions. No specialized source is cited, and TeX commands occur outside delimiters.

children.title: Monomial-Support Extension
children.top_down_role: Expansion of term supports used to define sparse semidefinite blocks.

assumptions_latex: A finite monomial basis B\subseteq\mathbb N^n and an initial support A^{(0)}\subseteq B+B are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For iteration k\u001b, form G_k=G(B,A^{(k)}) and let \mathcal C_k be its connected components. The component-completion support extension is A^{(k+1)}=A^{(k)}\cup\bigcup_{C\in\mathcal C_k}(C+C), optionally intersected with the admissible truncation B+B. Thus every pair of monomials lying in the same current component contributes its exponent sum at the next step. The update is extensive and monotone: A^{(k)}\subseteq A^{(k+1)}, and enlarging the input support cannot reduce the extended support. Iteration terminates when A^{(k+1)}=A^{(k)}.

notation.meaning: Connected components of the current graph.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Component-based closure of exponent support within a fixed truncation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For iteration k, form G_k=G(B,A^{(k)}) and let \mathcal C_k be its connected components. The component-completion support extension is A^{(k+1)}=A^{(k)}\cup\bigcup_{C\in\mathcal C_k}(C+C), optionally intersected with the admissible truncation B+B. Thus every pair of monomials lying in the same current component contributes its exponent sum at the next step. The update is extensive and monotone: A^{(k)}\subseteq A^{(k+1)}, and enlarging the input support cannot reduce the extended support. Iteration terminates when A^{(k+1)}=A^{(k)}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly complete each connected monomial component and add all resulting exponent sums until the support no longer changes.
knowledge_statements.title: Monomial-Support Extension

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the appropriate kind, but the component-completion update omits potentially formulation-specific shifted constraint supports and lacks a source. TeX notation is also undelimited.

children.title: Chordal Support Completion
children.top_down_role: Graph-completion structures used to organize term-sparse blocks.

assumptions_latex: An undirected term-support graph G=(B,E) and a chordal extension \widehat G=(B,\widehat E) with E\subseteq\widehat E are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Let C_1,\ldots,C_q be the maximal cliques of \widehat G. The chordally completed exponent support is \widehat A=A\cup\{\beta+\gamma:\{\beta,\gamma\}\in\widehat E\}\cup\{2\beta:\beta\in B\}. For a symmetric partial Gram matrix having specified entries on the diagonal and on \widehat E, chordality gives a positive semidefinite completion exactly when every fully specified principal submatrix indexed by C_i is positive semidefinite and the shared entries agree. Accordingly, a term-sparse semidefinite constraint can be represented by clique matrices coupled through their overlaps.

notation.meaning: Maximal cliques of the chordal extension.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chordal completion of a monomial interaction graph and its clique PSD representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let C_1,\ldots,C_q be the maximal cliques of \widehat G. The chordally completed exponent support is \widehat A=A\cup\{\beta+\gamma:\{\beta,\gamma\}\in\widehat E\}\cup\{2\beta:\beta\in B\}. For a symmetric partial Gram matrix having specified entries on the diagonal and on \widehat E, chordality gives a positive semidefinite completion exactly when every fully specified principal submatrix indexed by C_i is positive semidefinite and the shared entries agree. Accordingly, a term-sparse semidefinite constraint can be represented by clique matrices coupled through their overlaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A chordal extension adds monomial interactions so that positive semidefinite completion can be checked on maximal-clique matrices with consistent overlaps.
knowledge_statements.title: Chordal Support Completion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The leaf is appropriately represented as a chordal representation, but A is used without introduction and the record must distinguish PSD-completable partial matrices from sparse PSD decompositions. No supporting citation is supplied.

children.title: Support-Stabilization Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes where successive support completions cease to enlarge sparse blocks.

assumptions_latex: A support update F:2^{B+B}\to2^{B+B} is extensive and monotone on a finite monomial basis B.
The iteration is A^{(k+1)}=F(A^{(k)}).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequence (A^{(k)})_{k\ge0} is increasing and must reach a fixed point. If N=|B+B|, then either A^{(k+1)}=A^{(k)} or at least one previously absent exponent is added. Hence stabilization occurs after at most N-|A^{(0)}| strict extension steps. The stabilized support A^{(\infty)} is the least fixed point of F containing A^{(0)}. Earlier stabilization can occur when the initial term-support graph is already closed under the selected component or chordal completion rule.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite stabilization for monotone support extension on a fixed truncated basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequence (A^{(k)})_{k\ge0} is increasing and must reach a fixed point. If N=|B+B|, then either A^{(k+1)}=A^{(k)} or at least one previously absent exponent is added. Hence stabilization occurs after at most N-|A^{(0)}| strict extension steps. The stabilized support A^{(\infty)} is the least fixed point of F containing A^{(0)}. Earlier stabilization can occur when the initial term-support graph is already closed under the selected component or chordal completion rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any monotone support-extension process on a finite truncated basis stabilizes, after no more strict steps than there are initially missing admissible exponent sums.
knowledge_statements.title: Support-Stabilization Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-step bound fits complexity_bound, but the stated map F has codomain elements not explicitly restricted to subsets containing the input, while extensivity is only described informally. A specialized source and delimited TeX are required.

children.title: TSSOS Hierarchy Families
children.top_down_role: Term-sparsity hierarchy families based on support-driven block structure.

assumptions_latex: A polynomial optimization problem and a relaxation order d are fixed.
All objective and shifted constraint supports fit the degree-2d truncation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A TSSOS family is indexed by the relaxation order d and a support-extension depth k. Starting from the exponents occurring in the objective, constraints, and required diagonal terms, construct term-support graphs for the moment and localizing Gram bases, apply k support-extension steps, and replace each dense positive semidefinite Gram constraint by positive semidefinite blocks indexed by the completed graph components. The resulting optimum \rho_{d,k} is a lower bound on the polynomial minimum. For fixed d, nested support extensions give \rho_{d,k}\le\rho_{d,k+1}\le\rho_d^{\mathrm{dense}} whenever the feasible Gram cones are nested accordingly.

notation.meaning: TSSOS lower bound at indices d and k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-index term-sparse SOS relaxations using component-completed monomial graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A TSSOS family is indexed by the relaxation order d and a support-extension depth k. Starting from the exponents occurring in the objective, constraints, and required diagonal terms, construct term-support graphs for the moment and localizing Gram bases, apply k support-extension steps, and replace each dense positive semidefinite Gram constraint by positive semidefinite blocks indexed by the completed graph components. The resulting optimum \rho_{d,k} is a lower bound on the polynomial minimum. For fixed d, nested support extensions give \rho_{d,k}\le\rho_{d,k+1}\le\rho_d^{\mathrm{dense}} whenever the feasible Gram cones are nested accordingly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: TSSOS families use relaxation order and support-extension depth to generate increasingly strong block-semidefinite lower bounds bounded above by the dense SOS relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: TSSOS Hierarchy Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact initialization, localizing-graph construction, cone nesting, and lower-bound claim are family-specific and unsupported. The terminal container describes hierarchy families, for which representation may fit better than algorithm. TeX is undelimited.

children.title: Chordal-TSSOS Hierarchy Families
children.top_down_role: Term-sparsity hierarchy families using chordal completion structure.

assumptions_latex: A polynomial optimization problem, relaxation order d, and term-support extension depth k are fixed.
A chordal extension is selected for each resulting term-support graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A chordal-TSSOS relaxation constructs the order-d moment and localizing term-support graphs after k extension steps, replaces each graph by a chordal extension, and imposes positive semidefiniteness on matrices indexed by its maximal cliques, with common entries identified on clique overlaps. Its optimum \rho^{\mathrm{ch}}_{d,k} is a valid lower bound when these clique constraints represent an inner approximation of the corresponding dense SOS Gram cone. Enlarging the chosen chordal extensions yields nested Gram cones and nondecreasing lower bounds; completing every connected component to a clique recovers the component-block TSSOS member at the same indices.

notation.meaning: Maximal clique of a chordal term graph.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chordal-clique variant of term-sparse SOS relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A chordal-TSSOS relaxation constructs the order-d moment and localizing term-support graphs after k extension steps, replaces each graph by a chordal extension, and imposes positive semidefiniteness on matrices indexed by its maximal cliques, with common entries identified on clique overlaps. Its optimum \rho^{\mathrm{ch}}_{d,k} is a valid lower bound when these clique constraints represent an inner approximation of the corresponding dense SOS Gram cone. Enlarging the chosen chordal extensions yields nested Gram cones and nondecreasing lower bounds; completing every connected component to a clique recovers the component-block TSSOS member at the same indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Chordal-TSSOS replaces component-sized semidefinite blocks by maximal-clique blocks of chordal term graphs, trading smaller matrices for completion-dependent strength.
knowledge_statements.title: Chordal-TSSOS Hierarchy Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The claim mixes PSD completion language with an inner approximation of a Gram cone, so the lower-bound and monotonicity directions depend on the precise primal or dual formulation. The hierarchy-family leaf may call for representation rather than algorithm, and no source is cited.

children.title: Completion-Structure Comparison
children.top_down_role: Structural comparison of block patterns induced by the two hierarchy families.

assumptions_latex: Two completed term graphs G_1=(B,E_1) and G_2=(B,E_2) share the same monomial basis and satisfy E_1\subseteq E_2.
Both relaxations use the same coefficient-matching equations and relaxation order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every Gram matrix permitted by the E_1 sparsity pattern is also permitted by the E_2 pattern. Therefore the associated sparse SOS cones satisfy \Sigma(E_1)\subseteq\Sigma(E_2)\subseteq\Sigma_{n,2d}, and the corresponding minimization lower bounds satisfy \rho(E_1)\le\rho(E_2)\le\rho^{\mathrm{dense}}_d. A component completion maximizes fill within each connected component, whereas a chordal completion may retain several smaller maximal cliques. The latter can reduce semidefinite block sizes, but unless its completion representation is exact for the relevant cone, it can produce a weaker bound.

notation.meaning: Sparse SOS cone admitted by edge set E.
Relaxation lower bound admitted by edge set E.
Dense SOS cone of degree at most 2d.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison under nested Gram sparsity patterns at a fixed SOS order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every Gram matrix permitted by the E_1 sparsity pattern is also permitted by the E_2 pattern. Therefore the associated sparse SOS cones satisfy \Sigma(E_1)\subseteq\Sigma(E_2)\subseteq\Sigma_{n,2d}, and the corresponding minimization lower bounds satisfy \rho(E_1)\le\rho(E_2)\le\rho^{\mathrm{dense}}_d. A component completion maximizes fill within each connected component, whereas a chordal completion may retain several smaller maximal cliques. The latter can reduce semidefinite block sizes, but unless its completion representation is exact for the relevant cone, it can produce a weaker bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested completed edge sets yield nested sparse SOS cones and lower bounds; chordal completion may use smaller blocks than component completion but can be weaker.
knowledge_statements.title: Completion-Structure Comparison

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Property fits the comparison leaf, but Sigma(E) is not formally defined and edge inclusion alone does not resolve whether the construction uses sparse Gram matrices, PSD completion, or clique-sum decomposition. The cone and bound inclusions require a specialized source.

children.title: Correlative-Sparsity Layer
children.top_down_role: Variable-clique decomposition within combined sparse hierarchies.

assumptions_latex: A polynomial optimization problem \inf\{f(x):g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\} is given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The correlative-sparsity graph has variable vertices V=\{1,\ldots,n\}. Distinct variables i and \ell are adjacent whenever they occur together in a monomial of f or of some g_j; a constraint may additionally induce a clique on all variables on which it depends. After choosing a chordal extension with maximal cliques I_1,\ldots,I_p, each objective term and constraint is assigned to a clique containing its variable support. Moment and localizing objects are then formed clique-wise, subject to consistency on overlaps when the formulation requires shared moments.

notation.meaning: Variable vertices of the correlative graph.
Maximal variable cliques after chordal extension.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable-level decomposition used before monomial-level sparsification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The correlative-sparsity graph has variable vertices V=\{1,\ldots,n\}. Distinct variables i and \ell are adjacent whenever they occur together in a monomial of f or of some g_j; a constraint may additionally induce a clique on all variables on which it depends. After choosing a chordal extension with maximal cliques I_1,\ldots,I_p, each objective term and constraint is assigned to a clique containing its variable support. Moment and localizing objects are then formed clique-wise, subject to consistency on overlaps when the formulation requires shared moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The correlative layer groups variables into chordal cliques containing each polynomial's variable interactions, enabling clique-wise moment and localizing constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Correlative-Sparsity Layer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The description is locally relevant, but it blends two conventions: co-occurrence within individual monomials and clique completion over all variables of a constraint. The layer may be better classified as a representation, and the exact convention needs a source.

children.title: Term-Sparsity Layer
children.top_down_role: Monomial-support decomposition within combined sparse hierarchies.

assumptions_latex: A variable clique I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\} and relaxation order d are fixed.
The local monomial basis is B_{I,d}=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n:\operatorname{supp}(\alpha)\subseteq I,\ |\alpha|\le d\}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Within the variable clique I, construct a term-support graph on B_{I,d} by joining \alpha and \beta when the exponent sum \alpha+\beta is required by the local objective, a shifted local constraint support, a diagonal term, or a previous support-extension step. Complete or chordally extend this graph and impose positive semidefinite constraints only on the resulting monomial blocks or maximal cliques. Thus term sparsity refines a variable clique without introducing monomials involving variables outside I.

notation.meaning: Degree-d monomial exponent basis supported in I.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monomial-level refinement inside one correlative variable clique.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Within the variable clique I, construct a term-support graph on B_{I,d} by joining \alpha and \beta when the exponent sum \alpha+\beta is required by the local objective, a shifted local constraint support, a diagonal term, or a previous support-extension step. Complete or chordally extend this graph and impose positive semidefinite constraints only on the resulting monomial blocks or maximal cliques. Thus term sparsity refines a variable clique without introducing monomials involving variables outside I.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inside each variable clique, the term layer splits its monomial basis into completed interaction blocks and applies semidefinite constraints only to those blocks.
knowledge_statements.title: Term-Sparsity Layer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local monomial refinement matches the leaf, but its initialization and shifted-support rules are formulation-specific and unsupported. Because it describes a relaxation layer rather than defining one object, representation may fit better than definition.

children.title: Two-Level Sparsity Coupling
children.top_down_role: Interaction between variable-clique structure plus term-support blocks.

assumptions_latex: Variable cliques I_1,\ldots,I_p cover every objective term and constraint support.
For each I_t, a completed term graph on the local basis B_{I_t,d} has monomial cliques C_{t,1},\ldots,C_{t,q_t}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupled relaxation uses positive semidefinite moment or Gram blocks indexed by the pairs (t,r), with block C_{t,r}\subseteq B_{I_t,d}. Coefficient-matching equations couple term blocks belonging to the same variable clique, while shared moment variables or explicit equality constraints couple blocks across overlaps I_t\cap I_s. Hence correlative sparsity limits which variables may interact, and term sparsity further limits which monomials interact inside each variable clique. Completing every local term graph and taking one variable clique containing all variables recovers the corresponding dense order-d SOS relaxation.

notation.meaning: Term cliques within variable clique t.
Local degree-d monomial basis on variable clique t.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested variable-clique and monomial-clique decomposition at a fixed relaxation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The coupled relaxation uses positive semidefinite moment or Gram blocks indexed by the pairs (t,r), with block C_{t,r}\subseteq B_{I_t,d}. Coefficient-matching equations couple term blocks belonging to the same variable clique, while shared moment variables or explicit equality constraints couple blocks across overlaps I_t\cap I_s. Hence correlative sparsity limits which variables may interact, and term sparsity further limits which monomials interact inside each variable clique. Completing every local term graph and taking one variable clique containing all variables recovers the corresponding dense order-d SOS relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two-level coupling first separates variable cliques, then separates monomial interactions inside each clique, while overlap equations preserve consistency between the resulting semidefinite blocks.

children.title: Newton-Support Reduction Calculus

children.title: Newton-Polytope Support Reduction
children.top_down_role: Support pruning derived from faces, lattice structure, and polynomial support geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Newton-Polytope Support Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support reduction for an exact SOS representation of a real polynomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) and suppose \(p=\sum_{i=1}^m q_i^2\) for polynomials \(q_i\in\mathbb R[x]\). Then every exponent occurring in any \(q_i\) lies in \(\tfrac12\operatorname{Newt}(p)\cap\mathbb N^n\). Consequently, with \(B=\tfrac12\operatorname{Newt}(p)\cap\mathbb N^n\) and \(z_B=(x^\beta)_{\beta\in B}\), there exists a positive semidefinite matrix \(Q\) such that \(p=z_B^{\mathsf T}Qz_B\). Thus monomials outside \(B\) may be removed without excluding any SOS decomposition of \(p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every square factor of an SOS polynomial uses only lattice exponents in half its Newton polytope, yielding a complete reduced Gram basis.
assumptions_latex: \(p\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\)
\(p\) admits an exact sum-of-squares decomposition
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigcup_i\operatorname{supp}(q_i)\subseteq \tfrac12\operatorname{Newt}(p)\cap\mathbb N^n\)

notation.meaning: convex hull of the exponent support of p
column vector of monomials indexed by B

review_flags: Exact Newton-polytope SOS support theorem requires an authoritative locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Newton-polytope support theorem is mathematically plausible and fits the property container, but the strong claim covering every SOS decomposition requires an authoritative theorem or section locator.

children.title: Monomial Basis Reduction

knowledge_statements.title: Monomial Basis Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced Gram representation after choosing a support-compatible exponent set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite set \(B\subseteq\mathbb N^n\), define \(z_B=(x^\beta)_{\beta\in B}\). A polynomial \(p=\sum_\alpha p_\alpha x^\alpha\) has an SOS representation supported on \(B\) exactly when there exists \(Q\succeq0\) satisfying \[p_\alpha=\sum_{\substack{\beta,\gamma\in B\\\beta+\gamma=\alpha}}Q_{\beta\gamma}\quad\text{for every }\alpha.\] In that case \(p=z_B^{\mathsf T}Qz_B\). Taking \(B=\tfrac12\operatorname{Newt}(p)\cap\mathbb N^n\), followed by deletion of indices forced to have zero Gram rows and columns, preserves feasibility while reducing the semidefinite block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficient matching over a reduced monomial vector gives a smaller Gram matrix without changing SOS feasibility when the retained basis is complete.
assumptions_latex: \(B\subseteq\mathbb N^n\) is finite
\(p\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\in\Sigma[x]\iff \exists Q\succeq0:\ p=z_B^{\mathsf T}Qz_B\), provided \(B\) is SOS-complete for \(p\)
review_flags: A source for completeness-preserving Gram-basis pruning is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Gram coefficient equations are standard and the representation kind fits, but completeness of the half-Newton basis and subsequent forced-row pruning need a precise supporting source.

children.title: SOS Support Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Boundaries determining when geometric support reductions preserve the target certificate class.

knowledge_statements.title: SOS Support Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient-level compatibility of a proposed monomial set with an SOS Gram representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\subseteq\mathbb N^n\) be finite and let \(p=\sum_\alpha p_\alpha x^\alpha\). The set \(B\) is SOS-support compatible with \(p\) when the affine coefficient system \[p_\alpha=\sum_{\substack{\beta,\gamma\in B\\\beta+\gamma=\alpha}}Q_{\beta\gamma}\quad(\alpha\in B+B)\] admits a symmetric solution \(Q\succeq0\), and \(p_\alpha=0\) for every \(\alpha\notin B+B\). The inclusion \(\operatorname{supp}(p)\subseteq B+B\) is necessary but generally not sufficient, because the same positive semidefinite matrix must satisfy all coefficient equations simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proposed monomial basis is compatible exactly when one positive semidefinite Gram matrix matches every coefficient; support containment alone is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: \(B\subseteq\mathbb N^n\) is finite
\(p\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\) is compatible with \(p\iff\exists Q\succeq0\) satisfying all displayed coefficient equations

notation.meaning: set of pairwise sums of exponents in B
symmetric Gram matrix indexed by B

review_flags: The coefficient-compatibility characterization lacks a supplied SOS source locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated condition correctly characterizes compatibility through a common positive-semidefinite Gram matrix, but no inspectable source supports the characterization or the insufficiency claim.

children.title: Quotient-Ideal Reduction Calculus

children.title: Ideal-Based Polynomial Reduction
children.top_down_role: Hierarchy compression using polynomial equalities represented through an ideal.

knowledge_statements.title: Ideal-Based Polynomial Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal-form reduction of polynomial optimization data modulo equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an ideal \(I=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_s\rangle\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\), a term order, and a Gröbner basis \(G\) of \(I\), replace every polynomial \(f\) used in the relaxation by its division remainder \(\operatorname{NF}_G(f)\). Initialize with \(G\); reduce objectives, inequalities, and products entering coefficient constraints; formulate the relaxation using the reduced representatives; and output both the reduced system and the identities \(f-\operatorname{NF}_G(f)\in I\). For every \(x\in V_{\mathbb R}(I)\), one has \(f(x)=\operatorname{NF}_G(f)(x)\), so reduction preserves values on the equality-constrained variety.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduce every polynomial to its Gröbner normal form; the remainder agrees with the original polynomial on the equality variety.
assumptions_latex: \(I=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_s\rangle\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\)
\(G\) is a Gröbner basis of \(I\) for a fixed term order
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f-\operatorname{NF}_G(f)\in I\) and \(f|_{V_{\mathbb R}(I)}=\operatorname{NF}_G(f)|_{V_{\mathbb R}(I)}\)

notation.meaning: normal-form remainder of f modulo G

review_flags: A Gröbner-basis source connecting normal forms to SOS reductions is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Normal-form value preservation on the real variety is standard, but the proposed reduction of all relaxation products can affect the algebraic certificate formulation and needs a source specific to quotient or ideal-based SOS reductions.

children.title: Quotient-Ring Basis Reduction
children.top_down_role: Reduced polynomial representations modulo the equality ideal.

knowledge_statements.title: Quotient-Ring Basis Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional quotient representation induced by a zero-dimensional equality ideal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) be zero-dimensional and let \(G\) be a Gröbner basis. The standard monomials \(B=\{x^\beta:x^\beta\notin\langle\operatorname{LT}(G)\rangle\}\) form a basis of the finite-dimensional quotient algebra \(A=\mathbb R[x]/I\). Every class \([f]\in A\) therefore has the unique representation \[[f]=\sum_{x^\beta\in B}c_\beta[x^\beta],\] obtained from \(\operatorname{NF}_G(f)\). Multiplication in \(A\) is represented by reducing each product of basis monomials modulo \(G\), permitting moment and Gram coefficient equations to be written only in quotient-basis coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a zero-dimensional ideal, standard monomials form a finite quotient-ring basis in which reduced moment and Gram equations can be expressed.
assumptions_latex: \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) is zero-dimensional
\(G\) is a Gröbner basis for a fixed term order
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb R[x]/I=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{[x^\beta]:x^\beta\in B\}\) with unique coordinates

notation.meaning: leading terms of the Gröbner basis

review_flags: The standard-monomial quotient-basis theorem needs an authoritative locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The standard-monomial basis statement is appropriate for a zero-dimensional ideal and fits the representation container, but the quotient-basis theorem and its use in moment or Gram equations lack an authoritative locator.

children.title: Representative Selection in Quotient Classes
children.top_down_role: Basis and representative choices affecting compressed hierarchy size and conditioning.

knowledge_statements.title: Representative Selection in Quotient Classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical representative selection relative to a fixed Gröbner basis and term order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a term order and a reduced Gröbner basis \(G\) of an ideal \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\). For an input class \([f]\in\mathbb R[x]/I\), divide \(f\) by \(G\) and output \(r=\operatorname{NF}_G(f)\). The output contains no monomial divisible by any \(\operatorname{LT}(g)\) with \(g\in G\), satisfies \(f-r\in I\), and is independent of the chosen representative of \([f]\). Hence \(r\) is the unique standard-monomial representative for the fixed order. Different term orders may select different representatives but never different quotient classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gröbner normal form selects the unique standard-monomial representative of each quotient class for a fixed term order.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is the reduced Gröbner basis of \(I\)
A monomial term order is fixed
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \([f]=[r]\), where \(r=\operatorname{NF}_G(f)\) is unique for the fixed order

notation.meaning: residue class of f modulo I

review_flags: A precise normal-form uniqueness theorem locator is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-order Gröbner normal-form algorithm and uniqueness claim are standard and fit the leaf, but a specific normal-form theorem or section locator is required.

children.title: Invariant-Polynomial Reduction
children.top_down_role: Restriction of hierarchy certificates to invariant polynomial spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Invariant-Polynomial Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Averaging SOS certificates for polynomial problems invariant under a finite or compact group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite or compact group \(G\) act linearly on \(\mathbb R^n\), and let \(\mathcal R(f)=\int_G f(gx)\,d\mu(g)\) be the Reynolds operator. If the objective and defining polynomials are \(G\)-invariant and \(p\) has a feasible SOS certificate in a convex certificate cone preserved by the action, then averaging every certificate component yields another feasible certificate of the same degree and value. In particular, \(\mathcal R(p)=p\), and averaged Gram or moment data lie in the invariant subspace. Thus the hierarchy may be restricted to invariant certificate data without weakening its bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For invariant polynomial problems, group averaging converts any feasible SOS certificate into an invariant one of equal degree and objective value.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite or compact with normalized Haar measure
Problem data and the certificate cone are invariant under the induced action
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible certificate has a \(G\)-invariant feasible certificate with the same degree and bound
review_flags: A source for Reynolds averaging of SOS certificates is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The averaging principle fits invariant-polynomial reduction, but preservation of the full certificate, degree, and bound depends on the precise invariant cone and certificate structure and therefore requires a specific source.

children.title: Symmetry-Adapted Block Diagonalization
children.top_down_role: Representation-theoretic decomposition of moment and Gram matrices.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Adapted Block Diagonalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complex isotypic block form for invariant Hermitian moment or Gram matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be finite or compact and let a finite-dimensional unitary representation decompose as \(V\cong\bigoplus_{\lambda}(W_\lambda\otimes\mathbb C^{m_\lambda})\), where \(W_\lambda\) are pairwise inequivalent irreducibles of dimension \(d_\lambda\). Every Hermitian operator \(Q\) commuting with the action has, in a symmetry-adapted basis, the form \[Q\cong\bigoplus_\lambda\bigl(I_{d_\lambda}\otimes Q_\lambda\bigr),\qquad Q_\lambda=Q_\lambda^*.\] Moreover, \(Q\succeq0\) if and only if \(Q_\lambda\succeq0\) for every \(\lambda\). Hence an invariant moment or Gram constraint separates into smaller positive-semidefinite blocks indexed by irreducible representation types.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invariant Gram or moment matrix decomposes into smaller positive-semidefinite multiplicity blocks in a symmetry-adapted representation basis.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite or compact
\(V\) is a finite-dimensional unitary representation
\(Q\) is Hermitian and commutes with the action of \(G\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\succeq0\iff Q_\lambda\succeq0\) for all irreducible types \(\lambda\)
review_flags: A representation-theoretic block-diagonalization source locator is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complex commutant decomposition is mathematically standard and the representation kind fits. Its application to real SOS moment and Gram matrices requires a precise representation-theoretic or symmetry-reduction source.

children.title: Bounded-Degree SOS Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Hierarchy designs controlling semidefinite block degree.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Degree SOS Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed SOS-degree hierarchy with increasing nonnegative product degree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x:0\le g_j(x)\le1,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), fix \(d\in\mathbb N\), and define \(h_{\alpha\beta}=\prod_{j=1}^m g_j^{\alpha_j}(1-g_j)^{\beta_j}\). The bounded-degree SOS bound at product order \(k\) is \[\rho_{d,k}=\sup\left\{t:f-t=\sigma+\sum_{|\alpha|+|\beta|\le k}\lambda_{\alpha\beta}h_{\alpha\beta},\ \sigma\in\Sigma[x]_{2d},\ \lambda_{\alpha\beta}\ge0\right\}.\] The semidefinite Gram degree remains bounded by \(2d\), while increasing \(k\) enlarges the nonnegative product certificate and produces nondecreasing lower bounds \(\rho_{d,k}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SOS block degree is fixed while increasingly many nonnegative products of normalized constraints strengthen the lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(d,k\in\mathbb N\)
\(f,g_j\in\mathbb R[x]\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{d,k}\le\rho_{d,k+1}\le\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\)

notation.meaning: SOS polynomials of degree at most 2d
product of normalized constraints and complements

review_flags: The node may intend a specific BSOS variant; an exact hierarchy source is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a coherent bounded-degree SOS definition with valid monotonicity and soundness, but it appears to select a particular BSOS-style hierarchy not fixed by the title alone. A source identifying the intended variant is necessary.

children.title: Intermediate LP-SDP Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Hierarchy families interpolating between polyhedral and full semidefinite certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Intermediate LP-SDP Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hybrid conic certificates between diagonal nonnegative-square cones and block-SOS cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z=(z_1,\ldots,z_N)\) be a monomial vector, and let \(B_1,\ldots,B_s\) partition its indices. For \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,s\}\), define \[\mathcal C_S=\left\{\sum_{r\notin S}\sum_{i\in B_r}\lambda_i z_i^2+\sum_{r\in S}z_{B_r}^{\mathsf T}Q_rz_{B_r}:\lambda_i\ge0,\ Q_r\succeq0\right\}.\] Unselected blocks use nonnegative diagonal coefficients, whereas selected blocks use positive-semidefinite Gram matrices. If \(S\subseteq T\), then \(\mathcal C_S\subseteq\mathcal C_T\subseteq\Sigma[x]\), because a nonnegative diagonal block is a positive-semidefinite Gram block. Thus enlarging \(S\) gives a monotone interpolation from a polyhedral certificate cone to the full block-SOS cone associated with the partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selected monomial blocks receive positive-semidefinite Gram constraints while unselected blocks retain nonnegative diagonal-square certificates, producing a nested LP-to-SDP interpolation.
assumptions_latex: \(z\) is a finite monomial vector
\(B_1,\ldots,B_s\) partition the indices of \(z\)
\(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,s\}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\subseteq T\implies\mathcal C_S\subseteq\mathcal C_T\subseteq\Sigma[x]\)

notation.meaning: indices of blocks assigned positive-semidefinite Gram constraints
monomial subvector indexed by block B_r

review_flags: A precise source is required to identify this block-diagonal LP-SDP interpolation as the intended hierarchy family.

children.title: Multi-Order Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Nonuniform relaxation orders across constraints or sparse blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Order Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SOS relaxation with separate truncation orders for individual constraint multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), choose an objective order \(r_0\in\mathbb N\) and multiplier orders \(r_j\in\mathbb N\) satisfying \(2r_j+\deg g_j\le2r_0\) for \(j=1,\ldots,m\). Define \[\rho_{\mathbf r}=\sup\left\{t\in\mathbb R:f-t=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j,\ \sigma_0\in\Sigma[x]_{2r_0},\ \sigma_j\in\Sigma[x]_{2r_j}\right\}.\] If two admissible order vectors satisfy \(\mathbf r\le\mathbf r'\) componentwise, every certificate feasible at \(\mathbf r\) is feasible at \(\mathbf r'\). Consequently, \(\rho_{\mathbf r}\le\rho_{\mathbf r'}\le\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each constraint multiplier receives its own SOS order; componentwise increases of admissible orders produce nested relaxations and nondecreasing valid lower bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\)
\(r_0,r_1,\ldots,r_m\in\mathbb N\)
\(2r_j+\deg g_j\le2r_0\) for every \(j=1,\ldots,m\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbf r\le\mathbf r'\implies\rho_{\mathbf r}\le\rho_{\mathbf r'}\le\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\)

notation.meaning: vector of objective and multiplier relaxation orders
SOS multiplier associated with constraint j
lower bound at order vector r
SOS polynomials of degree at most 2r

knowledge_statements.title: Selective Constraint Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive componentwise order increases for selected constraint multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve, score constraints, and raise only selected multiplier orders; nested certificate cones ensure the lower bound cannot decrease.
assumptions_latex: The current order vector satisfies all degree-compatibility conditions
Each iteration selects a nonempty constraint set unless the stopping test holds
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{\mathbf r^{(k+1)}}\ge\rho_{\mathbf r^{(k)}}\) at every refinement step

prescribed refinement diagnostic for constraint j
