intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The refinement loop fits the algorithm container and monotonicity follows from nested admissible orders, but the scoring diagnostic, selection rule, stopping test, and ambient-order update are left design-dependent. A specific adaptive-refinement source is needed to determine the intended algorithm.

children.title: Selective Clique Refinement
children.top_down_role: Localized strengthening assigned to selected cliques in sparse hierarchy models.

assumptions_latex: The polynomial optimization problem admits clique-supported moment or SOS blocks indexed by \(C_1,\ldots,C_p\).
Each clique has an admissible initial relaxation order \(d_i^{(0)}\), and increasing an order preserves feasibility nesting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_i^{(t+1)}=d_i^{(t)}+\mathbf 1\{i\in I_t\}\), with \(I_t\subseteq\{1,\ldots,p\}\).

notation.meaning: Variable index set of clique i
Relaxation order assigned to clique i at iteration t
Cliques selected for refinement at iteration t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a family of adaptive sparse-SOS updates that increase only selected clique orders.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given clique blocks \(C_1,\ldots,C_p\), initial orders \(d^{(0)}=(d_1^{(0)},\ldots,d_p^{(0)})\), a computable score \(s_i^{(t)}\) for every clique, and a stopping tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), solve the relaxation at \(d^{(t)}\). If its prescribed residual or bound-gap test is at most \(\varepsilon\), stop and return the relaxation solution and bound. Otherwise, a fixed selection rule chooses a nonempty set \(I_t\) from the scores, and update
\[
d_i^{(t+1)}=d_i^{(t)}+\mathbf 1\{i\in I_t\},\qquad i=1,\ldots,p.
\]
All unselected clique orders remain unchanged; compatibility constraints on clique overlaps are retained at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the sparse relaxation, select cliques using prescribed scores, increase only their local orders, and stop when the chosen residual or bound-gap test meets tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Selective Clique Refinement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf and is internally coherent, but no citation supports this particular score-based selective clique-refinement family or its stopping and compatibility requirements.

children.title: Mixed Refinement Allocation
children.top_down_role: Coordination of constraint-level priorities with clique-level computational budgets.

assumptions_latex: The relaxation has clique blocks \(C_i\) and constraint-localizing blocks indexed by \(j\).
Every admissible increment preserves the degree requirements of its affected blocks.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers simultaneous allocation of refinement across clique orders and constraint-specific localizing orders.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize admissible orders \((d^{(0)},r^{(0)})\) for clique moment blocks and constraint-localizing blocks. At iteration \(t\), solve the current relaxation and compute prescribed clique scores \(s_i^{(t)}\) and constraint scores \(q_j^{(t)}\). If the stopping test is satisfied, return the current bound and solution. Otherwise choose nonnegative integer increments \(\Delta_i^{(t)}\) and \(\Gamma_j^{(t)}\), not all zero, under the refinement budget, and set
\[
d_i^{(t+1)}=d_i^{(t)}+\Delta_i^{(t)},\qquad r_j^{(t+1)}=r_j^{(t)}+\Gamma_j^{(t)}.
\]
The allocation must preserve all support, degree, and overlap-consistency requirements of the sparse relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocate each refinement budget jointly among clique moment orders and constraint-localizing orders, while preserving degree and overlap consistency.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Refinement Allocation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mixed allocation algorithm matches the container, but its joint refinement mechanism and preservation requirements have no cited authoritative source.

children.title: Dense Moment Block Growth

assumptions_latex: The dense moment relaxation uses \(n\) variables and moments through total degree \(2d\).
Monomials are indexed by total degree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_d(y)\in\mathbb S^{s(n,d)}\), where \(s(n,d)=\binom{n+d}{d}\), and \(s(n,d)=\Theta(d^n)\) for fixed \(n\).

notation.meaning: Dense moment matrix of order d
Number of n-variate monomials of degree at most d

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts the PSD block dimension and truncated-moment coordinates in a dense total-degree relaxation.

source_refs.locator: 3.2.1 Moment and localizing matrix p. 58

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(v_d(x)=(x^\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le d}\). The dense moment matrix \(M_d(y)=L_y(v_dv_d^{\mathsf T})\) has
\[
s(n,d)=\binom{n+d}{d}
\]
rows and columns, hence \(s(n,d)(s(n,d)+1)/2\) scalar positions in its symmetric PSD block. Its entries use the truncated moment coordinates \(y_\gamma\) with \(|\gamma|\le2d\), of which there are \(\binom{n+2d}{2d}\). Consequently, for fixed \(n\), the block dimension grows as \(\Theta(d^n)\); for fixed \(d\), it grows as \(\Theta(n^d)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense order-d moment matrix has binomial(n+d,d) rows and uses binomial(n+2d,2d) moments, producing polynomial growth in either fixed parameter regime.

children.title: Dense Gram Block Growth
children.top_down_role: Dimension and storage growth of dense Gram representations.

assumptions_latex: An \(n\)-variate polynomial of degree at most \(2d\) is represented in the full monomial basis through degree \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^{s(n,d)}\), with \(s(n,d)=\binom{n+d}{d}\) and \(s(n,d)(s(n,d)+1)/2\) symmetric scalar entries.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts the dense Gram PSD block for an SOS polynomial of degree at most \(2d\).

source_refs.locator: 3.2.1 Moment and localizing matrix p. 58
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A polynomial \(p\in\mathbb R[x]_{2d}\) is represented as a dense SOS precisely through an identity
\[
p(x)=v_d(x)^{\mathsf T}Qv_d(x),\qquad Q\succeq0,
\]
for some Gram matrix \(Q\) of order \(s(n,d)=\binom{n+d}{d}\). Thus the PSD block has \(s(n,d)(s(n,d)+1)/2\) symmetric scalar entries before coefficient-matching equations are imposed. For fixed \(n\), its matrix dimension is \(\Theta(d^n)\) and its scalar storage is \(\Theta(d^{2n})\); for fixed \(d\), these quantities are respectively \(\Theta(n^d)\) and \(\Theta(n^{2d})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dense SOS Gram matrix uses the same monomial count as the moment block; its symmetric scalar storage is quadratic in that count.
knowledge_statements.title: Dense Gram Block Growth

children.title: Moment-Gram Size Correspondence

assumptions_latex: Moment and SOS formulations use the same total-degree monomial vector \(v_d\).
The pairing is the coefficientwise linear functional \(L_y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_y(v_d^{\mathsf T}Qv_d)=\langle Q,M_d(y)\rangle\), and both PSD matrices have order \(\binom{n+d}{d}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the finite-dimensional pairing between dense moment and SOS Gram blocks at a common order.

source_refs.locator: 3.2.1 Moment and localizing matrix p. 58

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(v_d(x)=(x^\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le d}\), define \(M_d(y)=L_y(v_dv_d^{\mathsf T})\). Then every symmetric matrix \(Q\) satisfies
\[
L_y\!\left(v_d^{\mathsf T}Qv_d\right)=\langle Q,M_d(y)\rangle.
\]
Consequently, the primal moment PSD constraint \(M_d(y)\succeq0\) and the dual SOS Gram representation with \(Q\succeq0\) use PSD blocks of the identical order \(\binom{n+d}{d}\). Their affine data differ: moment entries reuse coordinates \(y_{\alpha+\beta}\), whereas Gram entries are aggregated by coefficient-matching equations indexed by \(\alpha+\beta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Moment and Gram formulations use equally sized PSD matrices, linked by the trace pairing between a Gram matrix and the moment matrix.

children.title: Localizing Block Growth
children.top_down_role: Block-size growth induced by individual polynomial constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Localizing Block Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts one dense localizing PSD block under the standard total-degree truncation convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Write \(g(x)=\sum_\gamma g_\gamma x^\gamma\) and let \(k=\lceil\deg(g)/2\rceil\). At relaxation order \(d\ge k\), the localizing matrix is indexed by monomials of degree at most \(d-k\) and has entries
\[
M_{d-k}(gy)_{\alpha,\beta}=\sum_\gamma g_\gamma y_{\alpha+\beta+\gamma}.
\]
It is therefore a PSD block of order \(\binom{n+d-k}{d-k}\), with \(\binom{n+d-k}{d-k}\bigl(\binom{n+d-k}{d-k}+1\bigr)/2\) symmetric positions. Increasing \(\deg(g)\) does not increase this block order at fixed \(d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degree-delta constraint creates a localizing block indexed through degree d-ceil(delta/2), determining its binomial matrix dimension; increasing the constraint degree cannot increase that dimension at fixed relaxation order.
assumptions_latex: The constraint polynomial \(g\in\mathbb R[x]\) has degree \(\delta\), and \(k=\lceil\delta/2\rceil\).
The relaxation order satisfies \(d\ge k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{d-k}(gy)\in\mathbb S^{\binom{n+d-k}{d-k}}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At order \(d\), a quadratic-module relaxation uses the moment block for the empty product and at most one localizing block for each generator, so
\[
B_{\mathrm{QM}}(d)\le m+1.
\]

\[
B_{\mathrm{pre}}(d)\le2^m.
\]

children.title: Sparse Clique Block Growth
children.top_down_role: Local hierarchy size governed by clique cardinality and clique-specific order.

assumptions_latex: The correlative-sparsity relaxation has cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_p\) with sizes \(w_i=|C_i|\).
Every clique uses the common total-degree order \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_d^{C_i}(y)\in\mathbb S^{\binom{w_i+d}{d}}\), and total symmetric storage is \(\sum_i s_i(s_i+1)/2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts clique-local moment blocks without asserting convergence conditions for the sparse hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each clique \(C_i\), let \(v_d^{C_i}\) contain monomials in variables indexed by \(C_i\) of degree at most \(d\). Then
\[
M_d^{C_i}(y)=L_y\!\left(v_d^{C_i}(v_d^{C_i})^{\mathsf T}\right)
\]
has order \(s_i=\binom{w_i+d}{d}\), where \(w_i=|C_i|\). The collection of clique PSD blocks therefore has aggregate row dimension \(\sum_{i=1}^p s_i\) and symmetric scalar storage \(\sum_{i=1}^p s_i(s_i+1)/2\). These quantities depend on clique sizes rather than directly on the total variable count, although repeated variables in overlapping cliques contribute to multiple blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse clique of size w contributes a binomial(w+d,d) moment block; aggregate storage sums the separate clique-block costs.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Clique Block Growth

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The clique-local binomial counts are mathematically plausible and fit the leaf, but no source is supplied for the sparse clique-block formulation or the aggregate-storage interpretation.

children.title: Clique-Overlap Growth
children.top_down_role: Additional representation size arising from shared variables across sparse blocks.

assumptions_latex: Two order-\(d\) clique blocks have sizes \(w_a\) and \(w_b\) and overlap size \(s=|C_a\cap C_b|\).
Their local moment coordinates are stored separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_{ab}(d)=\binom{s+2d}{2d}\) overlap-moment coordinates occur in both local descriptions.

notation.meaning: Number of moment coordinates on the overlap

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts duplicated truncated moments on one clique overlap under a local-copy implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S_{ab}=C_a\cap C_b\) and \(|S_{ab}|=s\). An order-\(d\) clique moment matrix uses moment coordinates through degree \(2d\). Hence the coordinates supported entirely on \(S_{ab}\) number
\[
D_{ab}(d)=\binom{s+2d}{2d}.
\]
If cliques \(C_a\) and \(C_b\) maintain separate local moment vectors, these \(D_{ab}(d)\) coordinates occur in both descriptions and must be identified or otherwise coordinated. For fixed \(d\), this overlap count is \(\Theta(s^{2d})\); for fixed \(s\), it is \(\Theta(d^s)\). The PSD block orders themselves remain \(\binom{w_a+d}{d}\) and \(\binom{w_b+d}{d}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An overlap of s variables duplicates binomial(s+2d,2d) truncated moments when neighboring cliques keep separate local moment vectors.
knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Overlap Growth

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The overlap count is correct under separate local moment copies, but that implementation convention and its required coordination are unsupported by a citation.

children.title: Separator Duplication Costs
children.top_down_role: Storage and consistency burdens associated with repeated separator information.

assumptions_latex: The clique-intersection graph is represented by a tree with edge separators \(S_e\).
Each clique stores a normalized local moment vector through degree \(2d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_{\mathrm{sep}}(d)=\sum_e\left[\binom{|S_e|+2d}{2d}-1\right]\) scalar consistency equalities suffice for edgewise identification.

notation.meaning: Separator associated with clique-tree edge e

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts edgewise separator equalities for local moment copies on a running-intersection clique tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a clique-tree edge \(e=(a,b)\), consistency of separate local moment vectors requires
\[
y_\alpha^{(a)}=y_\alpha^{(b)}\qquad
\text{for every nonzero }\alpha\text{ supported on }S_e\text{ with }|\alpha|\le2d.
\]
Because both constant moments are already normalized to one, the edge contributes \(\binom{|S_e|+2d}{2d}-1\) scalar equalities. Summing edgewise gives
\[
E_{\mathrm{sep}}(d)=\sum_e\left(\binom{|S_e|+2d}{2d}-1\right).
\]
Under the running-intersection property these edge equalities propagate agreement between all clique copies containing a given separator-supported moment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate clique moment vectors require one equality per nonconstant separator moment, producing a binomial cost on every clique-tree edge.
knowledge_statements.title: Separator Duplication Costs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equality count is coherent under normalized local copies and a running-intersection clique tree, but no source supports the separator-consistency formulation or propagation claim.

children.title: Certificate Complexity Parameter Family

children.title: Certificate-Degree Complexity
children.top_down_role: Computational growth associated with the degree required by SOS certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Degree Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines degree complexity for quadratic-module certificates of a fixed lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\) and \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\), define the quadratic-module certificate-degree complexity by
\[
d_{\mathrm{cert}}(f,\gamma)=\min\left\{d\in\mathbb N:\ \exists\,\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_m\in\Sigma[x]\text{ such that }f-\gamma=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j,\ \deg(\sigma_0)\le2d,\ \deg(\sigma_jg_j)\le2d\text{ for }j=1,\ldots,m\right\}.
\]
If no such identity exists, set \(d_{\mathrm{cert}}(f,\gamma)=+\infty\). Finite \(d_{\mathrm{cert}}(f,\gamma)\) certifies \(f(x)\ge\gamma\) for every \(x\in K\), and determines the smallest corresponding SOS relaxation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certificate-degree complexity is the least SOS relaxation order at which a quadratic-module identity proves the chosen global lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set is \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\).
A target lower bound \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\) is certified by a quadratic-module SOS identity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{\mathrm{cert}}(f,\gamma)=\min\{d\in\mathbb N:\exists\,\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_m\in\Sigma[x],\ f-\gamma=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j,\ \deg(\sigma_0)\le2d,\ \deg(\sigma_jg_j)\le2d\ \forall j\}\).

children.title: Coefficient-Encoding Complexity
children.top_down_role: Representation cost associated with coefficient magnitude and exact encoding.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Encoding Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit complexity of a rational SOS certificate at a fixed hierarchy order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For rational polynomials \(p,g_1,\ldots,g_m\) and a rational bound \(\gamma\), consider certificates \(p-\gamma=\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i\), where \(\sigma_i=z_i^{\mathsf T}Q_i z_i\), \(Q_i\succeq0\), and all entries of \(Q_i\) are rational. For a rational number \(a/b\) in lowest terms, set \(\ell(a/b)=1+\lceil\log_2(1+|a|)\rceil+\lceil\log_2(1+b)\rceil\). The coefficient-encoding complexity is \[L_{m cert}=\min\left\{\sum_{i=0}^m\sum_{u,v}\ell((Q_i)_{uv}): (Q_i)_{i=0}^m\text{ satisfy the certificate identity}\right\}.\] It is infinite when no rational certificate of the prescribed order exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The complexity is the minimum total binary encoding length of rational Gram-matrix entries among all certificates of the prescribed SOS order.
assumptions_latex: \(p,g_i\in\mathbb Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\) and \(\gamma\in\mathbb Q\).
The monomial vectors \(z_i\) and relaxation order are fixed.
Gram matrices are encoded entrywise as reduced rational numbers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\rm cert}\in\mathbb N\cup\{+\infty\}\) measures rational certificate encoding size.

notation.meaning: positive-semidefinite Gram matrix for the SOS multiplier
binary encoding length of a rational number

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: rational bitlength and Gram-matrix encoding are standard, but the precise SOS certificate convention needs an authoritative locator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the coefficient-encoding leaf and is internally coherent at fixed bases and order, but no source with an inspectable locator supports this particular entrywise rational encoding convention, including its treatment of symmetric Gram entries.

children.title: Numerical-Precision Complexity
children.top_down_role: Computational cost associated with precision requirements in hierarchy solution and validation.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical-Precision Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Working precision required for a normalized approximate SOS certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a candidate identity \(p-\gamma=\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i\) with \(\sigma_i=z_i^{\mathsf T}Q_i z_i\), and normalize the input coefficient vector to have norm at most one. For tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), its numerical-precision complexity is the least integer \(b\) for which matrices \(\widehat Q_i\) with \(b\)-bit floating-point entries satisfy \[\left\|p-\gamma-z_0^{\mathsf T}\widehat Q_0z_0-\sum_{i=1}^m(z_i^{\mathsf T}\widehat Q_i z_i)g_i\right\|_{\rm coeff,\infty}\leq\varepsilon,\qquad \lambda_{\min}(\widehat Q_i)\geq-\varepsilon.\] If no such matrices exist, the complexity is \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Precision complexity is the least mantissa length yielding Gram matrices whose coefficient residual and positive-semidefiniteness violations are at most the requested tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon>0\).
The polynomial bases and coefficient normalization are fixed.
Floating-point exponents have sufficient range to avoid overflow and underflow.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b_{\rm cert}(\varepsilon)\) is the least admissible working precision, or \(+\infty\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: residual and eigenvalue tolerances are standard numerical certificate diagnostics, but this exact complexity convention is source-dependent

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits numerical-precision complexity, but the exact value depends on an insufficiently specified floating-point model and normalization convention. No cited source supports the chosen residual, eigenvalue tolerance, or mantissa-bit definition.

children.title: Relaxation-Order Management
children.top_down_role: Policy families for allocating and escalating hierarchy strength.

children.title: Uniform Order Escalation
children.top_down_role: Global increase of hierarchy order.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Order Escalation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global hierarchy update that raises every active relaxation block together.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an initial admissible order \(r_0\), increment \(\Delta\in\mathbb N_{>0}\), tolerance \(\varepsilon\), and a termination predicate \(T\). At iteration \(k=0,1,\ldots\), set \(r_k=r_0+k\Delta\), construct every moment and localizing block at order \(r_k\), solve the resulting relaxation, and test \(T(r_k)\). If the predicate holds, return the relaxation bound and its validated certificate; otherwise continue with \(r_{k+1}=r_k+\Delta\). Thus all constraints and sparsity blocks use the same global order at each iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve successive SOS relaxations while increasing one common order for every block, stopping only when the prescribed certificate test succeeds.
assumptions_latex: \(r_0\) is large enough to represent the objective and every constraint polynomial.
\(\Delta\geq1\).
The predicate \(T\) is independently verifiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{k+1}=r_k+\Delta\) until \(T(r_k)=\mathrm{true}\).

notation.meaning: common hierarchy order at iteration k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: uniform order advancement is the canonical hierarchy schedule, but no supplied locator addresses SOS order management

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches uniform hierarchy-order escalation and uses an appropriate content kind, but no inspectable source supports this SOS scheduling and validated-termination formulation.

children.title: Selective Order Allocation
children.top_down_role: Nonuniform order allocation across certificates or sparse blocks.

children.title: Constraint-Selective Ordering
children.top_down_role: Nonuniform hierarchy orders assigned across certificate constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Selective Ordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive allocation of distinct SOS multiplier orders to individual constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constraints \(g_i(x)\geq0\), initialize multiplier orders \(s_i\geq0\) and choose a master order \(R\) satisfying \(R\geq s_i+\lceil\deg(g_i)/2\rceil\) for every \(i\). Solve the relaxation with \(\deg(\sigma_i)\leq2s_i\). From a specified diagnostic rule, select a nonempty index set \(I_k\) of constraints whose local certificates are inadequate, update \(s_i\leftarrow s_i+\Delta_i\) for \(i\in I_k\), leave the other orders unchanged, and raise \(R\) only as required by the displayed inequalities. Stop when the common certificate predicate succeeds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase multiplier degree only for constraints selected by a diagnostic rule, while maintaining the master-order degree constraints required by every localizing term.
assumptions_latex: Each constraint has the form \(g_i(x)\geq0\).
Each increment satisfies \(\Delta_i\in\mathbb N_{>0}\).
The selection diagnostic and stopping predicate are fixed before execution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_i^{k+1}=s_i^k+\Delta_i\mathbf 1_{\{i\in I_k\}}\) with \(R_{k+1}\geq\max_i\{s_i^{k+1}+\lceil\deg(g_i)/2\rceil\}\).

notation.meaning: SOS multiplier order assigned to constraint i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: degree admissibility follows directly from truncated quadratic modules, but the adaptive selection policy is not canonical

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The degree inequality is plausible for the stated multiplier convention, but constraint-selective escalation is not canonical and the diagnostic policy is left abstract. A dedicated source is required to establish the intended algorithm and its admissibility convention.

children.title: Clique-Selective Ordering
children.top_down_role: Nonuniform hierarchy orders assigned across sparse clique blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Selective Ordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive order allocation across cliques of a sparse SOS relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_q\) be a running-intersection clique cover and initialize admissible local orders \(r_j\). At iteration \(k\), solve the sparse moment relaxation using order \(r_j^k\) on clique \(C_j\), with equal moments on each separator \(C_j\cap C_\ell\) through degree \(2\min(r_j^k,r_\ell^k)\). Select cliques \(J_k\) by a fixed local residual, rank, or bound diagnostic and set \(r_j^{k+1}=r_j^k+\Delta_j\) for \(j\in J_k\), leaving other orders unchanged. Rebuild affected clique and separator constraints and stop when the global certificate predicate succeeds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase orders only on diagnostically selected sparse cliques and rebuild their separator-consistency equations, preserving a globally coherent sparse relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The clique cover satisfies the running-intersection property.
Every polynomial is assigned to a clique containing all its variables.
\(\Delta_j\in\mathbb N_{>0}\) for selected cliques.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_j^{k+1}=r_j^k+\Delta_j\mathbf 1_{\{j\in J_k\}}\), with separator consistency retained through the common available degree.

notation.meaning: local hierarchy order on clique j

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: clique-local moments and separator consistency are standard in sparse hierarchies, but selective escalation requires a dedicated source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits clique-selective ordering, but selective local escalation and separator matching only through the minimum available degree are formulation-dependent. No cited locator supports this precise sparse hierarchy construction.

children.title: Coupled Order Allocation
children.top_down_role: Joint allocation regimes linking constraint priorities to clique structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Order Allocation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility conditions coupling constraint, clique, and separator orders.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let constraint \(i\) use an SOS multiplier of order \(s_i\) and be represented on every clique in \(K_i\). Let clique \(j\) have moment order \(r_j\), and let \(q_{j\ell}\) be the enforced separator order between adjacent cliques. The allocation is admissible precisely when \[r_j\geq s_i+\left\lceil\frac{\deg(g_i)}2\right\rceil\quad(i,\ j\in K_i),\qquad q_{j\ell}\leq\min(r_j,r_\ell),\] together with the analogous objective-degree requirement on each supporting clique. A shared multiplier or separator therefore couples all incident local orders; changing one order may force changes in several blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An allocation is admissible when every clique can represent its assigned multiplier terms and every separator order is supported by both incident clique orders.
assumptions_latex: Each polynomial has a specified supporting clique family.
Clique and multiplier orders are nonnegative integers.
Separator moments are equated through degree \(2q_{j\ell}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((r,s,q)\) is admissible exactly when all displayed degree and separator inequalities hold.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the inequalities express basic degree compatibility, but terminology and coupling conventions vary among sparse SOS formulations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed inequalities are plausible degree-compatibility conditions, but the claim that they characterize admissibility precisely is unreliable without a specified sparse SOS formulation. The objective requirement is also only described as analogous rather than stated explicitly.

children.title: Certificate-Driven Termination
children.top_down_role: Termination families based on exactness, extraction, or validated bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Driven Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound stopping conditions based on verified exactness, extraction, or certified gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a polynomial minimization problem, let \(L_r\) be a certified relaxation lower bound and let \(x_r\) be a verified feasible point with \(U_r=f(x_r)\). Termination at order \(r\) is certificate-driven if at least one independently checked condition holds: an exact rational SOS identity proves that \(f-L_r\) belongs to the truncated quadratic module and \(U_r=L_r\); a flat moment extension permits extraction of feasible global minimizers whose objective equals \(L_r\); or validated arithmetic proves \(0\leq U_r-L_r\leq\varepsilon\). In either of the first two cases, exact global optimality is certified; in the third case, \(x_r\) is globally \(\varepsilon\)-optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop after verifying an exact SOS lower-bound certificate together with a feasible point attaining that bound, a flat extraction attaining the bound, or a validated feasible-point gap within tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The problem is polynomial minimization over the stated semialgebraic feasible set.
\(L_r\) is a rigorously certified lower bound.
\(x_r\) is verified feasible and \(U_r=f(x_r)\).
\(\varepsilon\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f^*=L_r\) under either exact certificate with attainment or flat extraction, while \(0\leq f(x_r)-f^*\leq\varepsilon\) under the validated-gap condition.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: matching certified lower and feasible upper bounds, flat extraction, and validated gaps are standard stopping principles

children.title: Semidefinite Computational Interface

children.title: Facial Reduction for Degenerate Hierarchy Models
children.top_down_role: Reduction of hierarchy SDPs to smaller semidefinite faces.

knowledge_statements.title: Facial Reduction for Degenerate Hierarchy Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exposing-vector reduction of a degenerate hierarchy SDP to its minimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a hierarchy SDP with feasible matrices \(X\succeq0\) satisfying \(\mathcal A(X)=b\). Find a nonzero exposing matrix \(W\succeq0\) such that \(\langle W,X\rangle=0\) for every feasible \(X\). If the columns of \(V\) form a basis of \(\ker W\), replace \(X\) by \(VYV^{\mathsf T}\), impose \(Y\succeq0\), and substitute this expression into all affine equations. Repeat with exposing matrices for the reduced problem until no further proper face is exposed. The resulting SDP has the same feasible images and objective values as the original model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expose faces containing every feasible Gram or moment matrix, parameterize those faces by smaller PSD matrices, and repeat until no further reduction is found.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) is linear and the feasible set is nonempty.
Each computed \(W\) is rigorously verified to expose all feasible matrices.
\(V\) has full column rank and \(\operatorname{range}(V)=\ker W\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X=VYV^{\mathsf T}\) with \(Y\succeq0\) gives an equivalent SDP on a smaller semidefinite face.

notation.meaning: basis matrix for the exposed kernel

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exposing-vector facial reduction is standard SDP theory, but application to SOS hierarchy models needs a supporting locator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exposing-vector reduction is mathematically consistent and the algorithm kind fits the leaf, but no cited locator supports its application to degenerate SOS hierarchy models or the stated termination at the minimal face.

children.title: Chordal PSD Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition of sparse semidefinite constraints into clique blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Chordal PSD Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clique-sum representation of chordally sparse positive-semidefinite matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be chordal with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_q\), and let \(E_j\) select the coordinates indexed by \(C_j\). Denote by \(\mathbb S_G\) the symmetric matrices whose off-diagonal entries vanish outside \(E\). Then the chordally sparse positive-semidefinite cone has the representation \[\mathbb S_+^{|V|}\cap\mathbb S_G=\left\{\sum_{j=1}^q E_j^{\mathsf T}X_jE_j:X_j\in\mathbb S_+^{|C_j|}\right\}.\] Consequently, a sparse PSD constraint in this cone can be modeled using clique-sized PSD blocks and linear assembly equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a chordal sparsity graph, every sparse PSD matrix is a sum of embedded PSD matrices supported on maximal cliques, and conversely.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite chordal undirected graph.
\(C_1,\ldots,C_q\) are all maximal cliques of \(G\).
\(E_j\) is the coordinate-selection matrix for \(C_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb S_+^{|V|}\cap\mathbb S_G=\sum_{j=1}^q E_j^{\mathsf T}\mathbb S_+^{|C_j|}E_j\).

notation.meaning: symmetric matrices with sparsity pattern G

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the clique-sum identity is a standard chordal sparse-PSD theorem, but no relevant authoritative locator was supplied

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The clique-sum identity is the appropriate chordal sparse-PSD representation and fits the container, but it is a nontrivial theorem and no authoritative source with a theorem, section, or page locator is cited.

children.title: Polynomial Basis Conditioning Calculus
children.top_down_role: Conditioning improvements through polynomial bases and numerical scaling.

children.title: Polynomial Basis Scaling
children.top_down_role: Rescaling of polynomial coordinates and coefficient magnitudes for improved numerical conditioning.

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Basis Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal rescaling of a polynomial basis and its Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(x)\) be a polynomial basis vector and let \(D\) be an invertible diagonal matrix. Define the scaled basis \(v_s(x)=Dv(x)\). Every Gram representation \(s(x)=v(x)^{\mathsf T}Qv(x)\) transforms as \[s(x)=v_s(x)^{\mathsf T}Q_s v_s(x),\qquad Q_s=D^{-\mathsf T}QD^{-1}.\] Congruence preserves positive semidefiniteness, so \(Q\succeq0\) if and only if \(Q_s\succeq0\). Thus nonzero diagonal scaling changes the numerical coordinates of an SOS model without changing the represented polynomial or the SOS cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling basis elements by nonzero factors induces an inverse congruence of Gram matrices and leaves the represented polynomial and PSD condition unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(v(x)\) is a finite linearly independent polynomial basis vector.
\(D\) is diagonal with no zero diagonal entry.
\(Q\) is symmetric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v^{\mathsf T}Qv=v_s^{\mathsf T}D^{-\mathsf T}QD^{-1}v_s\) and \(Q\succeq0\iff D^{-\mathsf T}QD^{-1}\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Gram matrix in the scaled basis

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the formula follows from an elementary basis congruence, but an SOS numerical-conditioning source is still required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inverse-congruence formula is correct and the representation kind fits basis scaling. An inspectable source is still required for its placement and interpretation as an SOS numerical-conditioning device.

children.title: Polynomial Basis Orthogonalization
children.top_down_role: Use of orthogonal or near-orthogonal polynomial coordinates in hierarchy representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Basis Orthogonalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal basis construction under a positive-definite polynomial inner product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(x)\) be a polynomial basis and let \(H\) be its positive-definite Gram matrix under an inner product, so \(H_{ij}=\langle v_i,v_j\rangle\). Choose an invertible matrix \(R\) satisfying \(R^{\mathsf T}HR=I\), and define \(\psi(x)=R^{\mathsf T}v(x)\). Then \(\langle\psi_i,\psi_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}\). Moreover, every representation \(s(x)=v(x)^{\mathsf T}Qv(x)\) becomes \[s(x)=\psi(x)^{\mathsf T}Q_\psi\psi(x),\qquad Q_\psi=R^{-1}QR^{-\mathsf T},\] and \(Q\succeq0\) if and only if \(Q_\psi\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite basis Gram matrix yields an orthonormal polynomial basis; the SOS Gram matrix transforms by inverse congruence and remains PSD.
assumptions_latex: The polynomial inner product is positive definite on \(\operatorname{span}(v)\).
\(H_{ij}=\langle v_i,v_j\rangle\).
\(R\) is invertible and satisfies \(R^{\mathsf T}HR=I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle\psi_i,\psi_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}\) and \(Q_\psi=R^{-1}QR^{-\mathsf T}\succeq0\iff Q\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Gram matrix of the original basis under the inner product

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: orthogonalization and congruence transformation are standard linear algebra, but an SOS-basis conditioning locator is absent

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The orthonormalization and inverse-congruence formulas are internally consistent, but no source with a specific locator supports this construction in the SOS basis-conditioning context.

children.title: Scaling-Orthogonalization Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Interaction between magnitude normalization and orthogonal basis selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Orthogonalization Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of compatible scaling and orthogonalization transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\succ0\) be the inner-product Gram matrix of a basis \(v\), let \(D\) be invertible diagonal, and choose \(R\) with \(R^{\mathsf T}HR=I\). After scaling to \(v_s=Dv\), the Gram matrix is \(H_s=DHD\). Setting \(R_s=D^{-1}R\) gives \[R_s^{\mathsf T}H_sR_s=I,\qquad R_s^{\mathsf T}v_s=R^{\mathsf T}v.\] Hence scaling followed by the compatibly transformed orthogonalization produces exactly the same orthonormal polynomial basis as direct orthogonalization. The associated Gram-matrix congruences therefore represent the same polynomial and preserve positive semidefiniteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the orthogonalizer is transformed inversely with a diagonal basis scaling, scaling then orthogonalizing yields the same orthonormal basis as direct orthogonalization.
assumptions_latex: \(H\succ0\) and \(R^{\mathsf T}HR=I\).
\(D\) is an invertible diagonal matrix.
\(H_s=DHD\) and \(R_s=D^{-1}R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_s^{\mathsf T}H_sR_s=I\) and \(R_s^{\mathsf T}v_s=R^{\mathsf T}v\).

notation.meaning: orthogonalizer compatible with the scaled basis

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the compatibility identities follow from coordinate transformations, but a polynomial-basis conditioning source is required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The compatibility identities are algebraically correct for an invertible diagonal scaling and the property kind fits the leaf, but no cited source provides an inspectable locator for this polynomial-basis conditioning result.

children.title: Interior-Point Solver Interface
children.top_down_role: High-accuracy solution interface for moderate-size hierarchy SDPs.

knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Point Solver Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual interior-point interface for a finite-dimensional SOS relaxation in SDP form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the primal-dual pair \[\min_{X\succeq0}\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b\},\qquad \max_y\{b^{\mathsf T}y:S=C-\mathcal A^*(y)\succeq0\},\] initialize \(X_0\succ0\), \(S_0\succ0\), and \(y_0\). At iteration \(k\), compute a Newton direction for the primal equation, dual equation, and perturbed complementarity equation \(X_kS_k\approx\mu_k I\); choose a fraction-to-boundary step preserving positive definiteness; and reduce \(\mu_k\). Stop when the normalized primal residual, dual residual, and duality gap are at most \(\varepsilon\). Return \((X_k,y_k,S_k)\), together with these residuals and the decoded SOS Gram matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the hierarchy SDP by primal-dual Newton steps, preserve positive definiteness, and return Gram matrices only after primal, dual, and gap tolerances are met.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear.
Strictly positive definite primal and dual initial matrices are available.
\(\varepsilon>0\) is the requested KKT tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((X_k,y_k,S_k)\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-accurate primal-dual SDP solution under the stated residual convention.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard primal-dual interior-point interface for semidefinite programming

children.title: First-Order Solver Interfaces

knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Solver Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: ADMM interface using affine projection and positive-semidefinite projection for large hierarchy SDPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Rewrite the SDP as \[\min_{X,Z}\ \langle C,X\rangle+I_{\{\mathcal A(X)=b\}}(X)+I_{\mathbb S_+^n}(Z)\quad\text{subject to}\quad X=Z.\] For penalty \(\rho>0\), initialize \(Z^0,U^0\in\mathbb S^n\) and iterate \[X^{k+1}=\mathop{\rm argmin}_{\mathcal A(X)=b}\left\{\langle C,X\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|X-Z^k+U^k\|_F^2\right\},\] \[Z^{k+1}=\Pi_{\mathbb S_+^n}(X^{k+1}+U^k),\qquad U^{k+1}=U^k+X^{k+1}-Z^{k+1}.\] Stop when prescribed primal and dual residual tolerances hold; return the projected matrix \(Z^{k+1}\), objective value, and residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expose the hierarchy SDP through affine and PSD projections, iterate ADMM updates, and return an approximate feasible Gram matrix with explicit residuals.
assumptions_latex: The affine subproblem and \(\Pi_{\mathbb S_+^n}\) can be computed to the declared accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface returns an approximate SDP solution whose declared accuracy is determined by its primal and dual residuals.

notation.meaning: indicator function of a set C
Euclidean projection onto the PSD cone

children.title: Low-Rank Solver Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces exploiting low-rank semidefinite representations or parameterizations.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Solver Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Burer–Monteiro augmented-Lagrangian interface for hierarchy SDPs expected to admit low-rank Gram matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\), impose the factorization \(X=RR^{\mathsf T}\) with \(R\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\). Given \(R^0\), \(y^0\), and \(\rho>0\), approximately minimize at iteration \(k\) \[L_\rho(R,y^k)=\langle C,RR^{\mathsf T}\rangle+(y^k)^{\mathsf T}(\mathcal A(RR^{\mathsf T})-b)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|\mathcal A(RR^{\mathsf T})-b\|_2^2,\] then update \[y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho\bigl(\mathcal A(R^{k+1}(R^{k+1})^{\mathsf T})-b\bigr).\] Stop only after reporting feasibility and stationarity residuals. Return \(R\), \(X=RR^{\mathsf T}\), and the residuals; failure to attain them is not an SDP optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize a low-rank Gram factor with an augmented Lagrangian, reporting feasibility and stationarity while treating unsuccessful convergence as noncertifying.
assumptions_latex: A factor rank \(1\le r\le n\) is selected.
The SDP data and constraint map are finite-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned \(X=RR^{\mathsf T}\) is automatically PSD, but global SDP optimality requires an additional verifiable certificate.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard Burer–Monteiro factorization with augmented-Lagrangian constraint handling
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The low-rank augmented-Lagrangian algorithm fits the terminal container and correctly avoids claiming global optimality from stationarity alone. children.title: Scalable Solver Suitability Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Scalable Solver Suitability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational selection rule among interior-point, first-order, and low-rank SDP interfaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an SDP block of order \(n\), equality map \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\), memory budget \(B\), and target KKT tolerance \(\varepsilon\), select an interior-point interface when its Newton-factorization storage fits within \(B\) and high accuracy is required. Select a first-order interface when matrix-vector operations and PSD projections fit within \(B\), while moderate accuracy and explicit residual reporting are acceptable. Select a rank-\(r\) factor interface only when storing \(nr\) parameters fits within \(B\) and feasibility, stationarity, and an independent lower-bound or dual certificate will be checked. No scalability regime alone converts an approximate iterate into a valid polynomial certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose the solver by memory, accuracy, projection cost, and expected rank; scalable approximations still require independent certificate validation.
assumptions_latex: The hierarchy relaxation has a finite SDP representation.
The required accuracy and available memory are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Solver suitability is determined jointly by resource feasibility and the availability of verifiable residual or certificate checks.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conventional resource-and-accuracy tradeoff among SDP solver families

children.title: Rational Certificate Recovery
children.top_down_role: Exact reconstruction of polynomial certificates from numerical solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Rational Certificate Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recovery and verification of rational Gram certificates from floating-point SDP output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_s\in\mathbb Q[x]\) and let numerical matrices approximate a certificate \[f-\gamma=z_0^{\mathsf T}Q_0z_0+\sum_{j=1}^s g_jz_j^{\mathsf T}Q_jz_j.\] Round \(\gamma\) and the independent matrix entries to rationals, then project the rounded data onto the rational affine space obtained by equating polynomial coefficients. Verify the resulting coefficient identity exactly over \(\mathbb Q\), and verify every \(Q_j\succeq0\) using exact rational factorization or exact principal-minor tests. Output the rational identity only if all checks pass; otherwise increase reconstruction precision, alter the rational denominator bounds, or report recovery failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Round numerical Gram data to rationals, enforce coefficient equations exactly, and accept the recovered polynomial certificate only after exact PSD verification.
assumptions_latex: The input polynomials have rational coefficients.
Finite monomial bases \(z_j\) are fixed.
Numerical Gram data and rational reconstruction bounds are supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful output is an exactly checkable rational SOS or quadratic-module certificate for \(f-\gamma\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard exact rational reconstruction and Gram-matrix verification workflow
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind exactly fits rational certificate recovery, and the record appropriately requires exact coefficient and PSD checks after reconstruction. An authoritative source is still needed for this recovery-and-verification workflow and its stated alternatives after failure.

children.title: Validated Residual Certificate Checks
children.top_down_role: Validated numerical checking of bounds and certificate residuals.

children.title: Interval-Based Validation

knowledge_statements.title: Interval-Based Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rigorous lower-bound validation on a box using outward-rounded interval arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in[a,b]:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,s\}\) and suppose computed data satisfy \[f-\gamma=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^s\sigma_jg_j+r,\qquad \sigma_j=z_j^{\mathsf T}Q_jz_j.\] Outward-rounded interval factorization must certify \(Q_j\succeq0\) for every \(j\), and interval polynomial evaluation or subdivision must produce a rigorous bound \(r(x)\ge-\eta\) for all \(x\in[a,b]\). These two checks certify \(f(x)\ge\gamma-\eta\) on \(K\). Merely obtaining an interval residual that contains zero is not sufficient to establish an exact coefficient identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interval PSD checks plus a rigorous residual lower bound certify a weakened polynomial lower bound on the constrained box.
assumptions_latex: The box \([a,b]\subset\mathbb R^n\) is compact.
All interval operations use directed outward rounding.
Each \(g_j\) is nonnegative on \(K\) by definition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in K\), \(f(x)\ge\gamma-\eta\).

children.title: Certificate Residual Validation
children.top_down_role: Assessment of algebraic and conic residuals in computed certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Residual Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient-norm validation of the residual left by an approximate Gram certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a candidate identity \[f-\gamma=z_0^{\mathsf T}Q_0z_0+\sum_{j=1}^s g_jz_j^{\mathsf T}Q_jz_j+r,\qquad r(x)=\sum_{\alpha\in D}r_\alpha x^\alpha,\] compute every \(r_\alpha\) with certified arithmetic. If \(|r_\alpha|\le\eta_\alpha\) and \(|x_i|\le R_i\) on \(K\), then \[|r(x)|\le\Delta:=\sum_{\alpha\in D}\eta_\alpha\prod_{i=1}^n R_i^{\alpha_i}.\] If all \(Q_j\succeq0\) and \(g_j\ge0\) on \(K\), the validated residual therefore certifies \(f(x)\ge\gamma-\Delta\) for every \(x\in K\). Exact certification at \(\gamma\) requires \(r=0\) or a separate nonnegative-residual proof.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified coefficient errors yield a uniform residual bound and hence a rigorously weakened lower bound over a bounded feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\{x:|x_i|\le R_i\}\).
The residual coefficients have certified error bounds.
Each Gram matrix is PSD.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)\ge\gamma-\Delta\) for all \(x\in K\).

notation.meaning: certified bound on a residual coefficient

children.title: Validation Consistency Checks

knowledge_statements.title: Validation Consistency Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cross-checks ensuring all decoded pieces describe one coherent hierarchy certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A decoded hierarchy certificate is consistent only if the following exact or validated checks share the same polynomial data and relaxation order: every monomial basis respects its degree bound; all Gram matrices have the dimensions induced by those bases; the single value \(\gamma\) used in the objective is also used in the coefficient identity; coefficient matching covers the complete monomial support; and every claimed PSD, primal-feasibility, dual-feasibility, and objective-gap tolerance is satisfied under one declared norm and scaling. Passing only a subset does not certify the lower bound. Passing all checks, together with PSD Gram validation, certifies the displayed quadratic-module identity at the stated residual allowance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Verify compatible bases, dimensions, bound values, coefficient identities, PSD claims, residual norms, and objective data before accepting a certificate.
assumptions_latex: A candidate certificate and its originating relaxation metadata are available.
All numerical tolerances and scaling conventions are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Jointly passing the consistency and PSD checks validates one coherent certificate at its stated residual allowance.

children.title: Spectral Flatness Validation System
children.top_down_role: Reliability assessment for flatness and extraction decisions.

children.title: Numerical Rank Validation
children.top_down_role: Reliability assessment of moment-matrix rank used in flatness decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Rank Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-dependent numerical-rank test for moment-matrix flatness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_d\) and its prescribed principal truncation \(M_{d-q}\) be symmetric moment matrices, with eigenvalues ordered nonincreasingly. For relative tolerance \(\tau>0\), define \[\operatorname{rank}_\tau(M):=\#\{i:\lambda_i(M)>\tau\max(1,\lambda_1(M))\}.\] Numerical flatness at order \(d\) is accepted only when \[\operatorname{rank}_\tau(M_d)=\operatorname{rank}_\tau(M_{d-q})\] and neither matrix has an eigenvalue below \(-\tau\max(1,\lambda_1(M))\). The reported decision must include \(\tau\), both spectra, both numerical ranks, and the truncation offset \(q\); without these data, numerical flatness is not reproducible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Declare numerical flatness only when thresholded ranks of consecutive prescribed moment truncations agree and neither matrix significantly violates PSD.
assumptions_latex: \(M_{d-q}\) is the hierarchy-prescribed principal truncation of \(M_d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed equality and PSD-tolerance tests constitute the declared \(\tau\)-numerical flatness condition.

notation.meaning: moment matrix at relaxation order d

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: thresholded spectral rank comparison is a standard numerical proxy for exact moment-matrix flatness

children.title: Spectral Gap Validation
children.top_down_role: Use of eigenvalue separation to assess extraction stability.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Gap Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation-stable validation of a proposed numerical rank from an eigenvalue gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\in\mathbb S^n\) have eigenvalues \(\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n\), and suppose a proposed rank \(r<n\) satisfies \(g:=\lambda_r(M)-\lambda_{r+1}(M)>0\). If a symmetric perturbation \(E\) obeys \(\|E\|_2<g/2\), then the two eigenvalue clusters remain separated because \[\lambda_r(M+E)-\lambda_{r+1}(M+E)\ge g-2\|E\|_2>0.\] Consequently, any cutoff chosen strictly between \(\lambda_{r+1}(M)+\|E\|_2\) and \(\lambda_r(M)-\|E\|_2\) assigns rank \(r\) to every matrix in that perturbation ball. A small or unvalidated gap provides no robust rank decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank decision is perturbation-stable when the separating eigenvalue gap exceeds twice the certified matrix-error norm.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) and \(E\) are real symmetric.
\(\|E\|_2<\bigl(\lambda_r(M)-\lambda_{r+1}(M)\bigr)/2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The spectral clusters, and hence an intervening rank cutoff, remain separated under the perturbation.

notation.meaning: spectral gap at the proposed rank

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct Weyl eigenvalue perturbation bound for symmetric matrices
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits spectral-gap validation, and the displayed separation estimate is the standard symmetric eigenvalue perturbation consequence. No section, theorem, or page citation is supplied for that nontrivial perturbation claim.

children.title: Flatness Decision Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Boundary cases where rank evidence does not support a stable extraction decision.

knowledge_statements.title: Flatness Decision Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instability of thresholded flatness decisions when an eigenvalue lies near the numerical cutoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a numerical-rank cutoff \(\tau>0\) and \(0<\delta<\tau\). The matrices \[M_- =\operatorname{diag}(1,\tau-\delta),\qquad M_+=\operatorname{diag}(1,\tau+\delta)\] are positive definite moment matrices of centered two-point measures, yet the rule counting eigenvalues strictly larger than \(\tau\) assigns ranks \(1\) and \(2\), respectively, while \(\|M_+-M_-\|_2=2\delta\). Thus arbitrarily close admissible moment data can yield different numerical flatness decisions. Whenever the certified eigenvalue uncertainty intersects the rank cutoff, flatness must be reported as ambiguous rather than accepted or rejected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If eigenvalue uncertainty crosses the rank threshold, arbitrarily close moment matrices can receive different flatness decisions, so the result is ambiguous.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\delta<\tau\).
Numerical rank counts eigenvalues strictly exceeding \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Thresholded flatness is not robust when the cutoff lies within the certified eigenvalue uncertainty interval.

notation.meaning: nearby PSD moment matrices on opposite sides of the cutoff

children.title: Nonnegative-but-Not-SOS Gap
children.top_down_role: Separation between global polynomial nonnegativity and SOS representability.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonnegative-but-Not-SOS Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Motzkin’s bivariate sextic separates global nonnegativity from sums of polynomial squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Motzkin polynomial \[m(x,y)=x^4y^2+x^2y^4+1-3x^2y^2\] satisfies \(m(x,y)\ge0\) for every \((x,y)\in\mathbb R^2\), but there do not exist polynomials \(q_1,\ldots,q_N\in\mathbb R[x,y]\) such that \[m=\sum_{i=1}^N q_i^2.\] Hence the cone of globally nonnegative real polynomials strictly contains the SOS cone; replacing nonnegativity by an unconstrained SOS condition can therefore exclude valid nonnegative polynomials even when no domain constraints are present.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Motzkin sextic is globally nonnegative but is not a sum of polynomial squares, proving the two cones differ.
assumptions_latex: \(x,y\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m\in\mathbb R[x,y]\) is globally nonnegative and \(m\notin\Sigma[x,y]\).

notation.meaning: cone of sums of squares in the real polynomial ring

children.title: Quadratic-Module Nonsaturation
children.top_down_role: Nonnegative polynomials absent from the selected quadratic module.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Module Nonsaturation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a constraint-generated quadratic module to contain every polynomial nonnegative on its feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\ge 0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) and let \(M(g)=\{\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i:\sigma_i\in\Sigma[x]\}\). The module is saturated when \(M(g)=\{p\in\mathbb R[x]:p|_K\ge0\}\). Quadratic-module nonsaturation means that there exists \(p\in\mathbb R[x]\) such that \(p(x)\ge0\) for every \(x\in K\), but \(p\notin M(g)\). For such a polynomial, \(0\) is a valid lower bound for minimizing \(p\) on \(K\), but it has no finite-degree certificate of the form \(p=\sigma_0+\sum_i\sigma_i g_i\); this does not assert that \(\inf_{x\in K}p(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonsaturation occurs when a polynomial is nonnegative on the feasible set but has no certificate in the quadratic module generated by its constraints; zero is then a valid, though not necessarily exact, uncertified lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(g_1,\ldots,g_m,p\in\mathbb R[x]\).
\(K\ne\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.title: Description-Dependent Hierarchy Strength
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-order SOS bounds depend on the chosen generators, even when their basic closed feasible sets coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(K=\{g_i\ge0:i=1,\ldots,m\}=\{h_j\ge0:j=1,\ldots,r\}\). For relaxation order \(d\), define \(M_d(g)\) and \(M_d(h)\) by retaining terms whose degrees do not exceed \(2d\), and define \(\rho_d^g=\sup\{\gamma:f-\gamma\in M_d(g)\}\) and \(\rho_d^h=\sup\{\gamma:f-\gamma\in M_d(h)\}\). Equality of the represented sets does not imply equality of the truncated modules; hence \(\rho_d^g\) and \(\rho_d^h\) need not agree. Adding a redundant valid generator can enlarge a truncated module and improve its finite-order lower bound without changing \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two polynomial descriptions of the same feasible set can yield different finite-order SOS cones and lower bounds; redundant constraints may strengthen a relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_i,h_j\in\mathbb R[x]\).
Both generator families define the same nonempty set \(K\).

children.title: Certificate-Degree Requirements

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Degree Requirements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree threshold required for a quadratic-module certificate to appear in a specified SOS relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M_d(g)=\{\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i:\sigma_i\in\Sigma[x],\ \deg(\sigma_0)\le2d,\ \deg(\sigma_i g_i)\le2d\}\), define \(d_{\min}(p;g)=\inf\{d\in\mathbb N:p\in M_d(g)\}\), with value \(+\infty\) if no such order exists. The order-\(d\) SOS relaxation can certify a lower bound \(\gamma\) for \(f\) exactly through this module only if \(d\ge d_{\min}(f-\gamma;g)\). Thus positivity of \(f-\gamma\) on the feasible set alone does not determine the relaxation order required for certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound appears at order d only when its polynomial certificate admits SOS multipliers whose products with the constraints have degree at most 2d.
assumptions_latex: \(f,p,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\).
The hierarchy uses the degree convention \(\deg(\sigma_i g_i)\le2d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f-\gamma\in M_d(g)\) requires \(d\ge d_{\min}(f-\gamma;g)\).

notation.meaning: Least relaxation order admitting a module certificate for p.

children.title: Active-Order Limitations
children.top_down_role: Certificate terms excluded by the currently selected hierarchy order.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Order Limitations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificates exceeding the active truncation degree are invisible to the current semidefinite relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At active order \(d\), the hierarchy searches only over identities \(f-\gamma=\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i\) satisfying \(\deg(\sigma_0)\le2d\) and \(\deg(\sigma_i g_i)\le2d\). If every quadratic-module certificate for \(f-\gamma\) contains a term of degree greater than \(2d\), then \(f-\gamma\notin M_d(g)\), even when a higher-order certificate exists. In particular, if \(f^*=\min_{x\in K}f(x)\) and \(d<d_{\min}(f-f^*;g)<\infty\), the order-\(d\) relaxation cannot certify the exact optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The active relaxation cannot use a valid certificate whose required multiplier degree exceeds its truncation, so exactness may occur only at a higher order.
assumptions_latex: \(K=\{x:g_i(x)\ge0\}\ne\varnothing\).
The minimum \(f^*\) is finite and attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d<d_{\min}(f-f^*;g)\) implies that order \(d\) cannot certify \(f^*\) through \(M_d(g)\).

notation.meaning: Global minimum of f on K.

children.title: Degree-Order Mismatch Diagnostics

knowledge_statements.title: Degree-Order Mismatch Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An exact polynomial identity diagnoses whether a proposed SOS certificate fits the active relaxation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given SOS multipliers satisfying the exact identity \(f-\gamma=\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i\), set \(d_{\mathrm{req}}=\max\{\lceil\deg(\sigma_0)/2\rceil,\max_i\lceil\deg(\sigma_i g_i)/2\rceil\}\). This identity is a verifiable order-\(d\) certificate precisely when each multiplier is SOS, the coefficient identity holds, and \(d\ge d_{\mathrm{req}}\). If \(d<d_{\mathrm{req}}\), the identity certifies the bound only at a higher order and diagnoses a degree-order mismatch rather than failure of nonnegativity. Numerical residuals alone do not establish the coefficient identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute the largest half-degree among certificate terms. If it exceeds the active order, the certificate is valid only for a later relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g_i,\sigma_i\in\mathbb R[x]\).
Every \(\sigma_i\) is represented by an exact positive-semidefinite Gram matrix or exact SOS decomposition.

children.title: Non-Archimedean Constraint Descriptions
children.top_down_role: Constraint systems outside the standard quadratic-module convergence regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Non-Archimedean Constraint Descriptions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Negation of the Archimedean condition for the quadratic module generated by a polynomial description.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), the generated quadratic module \(M(g)\) is Archimedean when there exists \(R>0\) such that \(R-\|x\|_2^2\in M(g)\). The constraint description is non-Archimedean when no such \(R\) exists. This is a property of the chosen generators, not merely of \(K\); even a compact set can have a non-Archimedean description. Without this condition, the standard Archimedean Positivstellensatz argument for asymptotic convergence of the SOS hierarchy is unavailable, although convergence may still follow from other hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A description is non-Archimedean when its quadratic module contains no polynomial ball constraint. Compactness of the represented set alone need not prevent this.
assumptions_latex: \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The description is non-Archimedean exactly when \(R-\|x\|_2^2\notin M(g)\) for every \(R>0\).

children.title: Uncontrolled Unbounded Geometry
children.top_down_role: Noncompact geometry lacking an effective hierarchy compactification.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncontrolled Unbounded Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Escape to infinity without a polynomial-module bound removes the usual compact moment-control mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x:g_i(x)\ge0\}\) be unbounded and suppose there is a sequence \(x^k\in K\) with \(\|x^k\|_2\to\infty\). If the chosen quadratic module contains no coercive sublevel constraint, in particular no \(R-\|x\|_2^2\), then feasibility does not impose uniform bounds on moments of arbitrary representing probability measures on \(K\). Consequently, compactness-based extraction of convergent moment subsequences and the standard Archimedean SOS convergence theorem do not apply. This boundary identifies absence of a guarantee, not a claim that every such hierarchy diverges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When feasible points escape to infinity and the module supplies no coercive bound, moment sequences may lack compactness and standard SOS convergence guarantees cease to apply.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty basic closed semialgebraic set.
The hierarchy uses the quadratic module generated by its displayed inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unbounded escape without module coercivity prevents invoking compact moment bounds or the standard Archimedean convergence theorem.

children.title: Finite Infimum without a Minimizer
children.top_down_role: Nonattained objective values and absent optimizer-supported measures.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Infimum without a Minimizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A polynomial problem with finite, nonattained infimum and no optimizer-supported representing measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(K=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:xy=1,\ x\ge0\}\) and minimize \(f(x,y)=x^2\). For every \(t>0\), the point \((t,t^{-1})\) lies in \(K\), so \(\inf_K f=0\). No point of \(K\) has \(x=0\); hence the infimum is not attained. Moreover, no probability measure \(\mu\) supported on \(K\) satisfies \(\int_K x^2\,d\mu=0\), because this equality would imply \(x=0\) almost surely. Thus an optimal moment representation supported on minimizers does not exist, despite the finite infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the hyperbola xy=1 with x positive, minimizing x squared has infimum zero along points escaping to infinity, but no minimizer or optimal measure.
assumptions_latex: The equality \(xy=1\) is imposed as a polynomial equality.
Representing measures are probability measures supported on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{(x,y)\in K}x^2=0\), but \(\operatorname*{argmin}_K x^2=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: The noncompact feasible branch of the hyperbola.
A probability measure supported on K.

children.title: Weak Infeasibility
children.top_down_role: Hierarchy relaxations whose affine constraints approach the semidefinite cone without feasible intersection.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Infeasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic infeasibility with zero distance between the affine constraints and the closed cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space and let \(L\) be an affine subspace. The conic feasibility system \(z\in C\cap L\) is weakly infeasible when \(C\cap L=\varnothing\) but \(\operatorname{dist}(C,L)=0\). Equivalently, it is infeasible and there exist sequences \(c_k\in C\) and \(\ell_k\in L\) with \(\|c_k-\ell_k\|_2\to0\). Unlike strongly infeasible systems, the two sets admit no strict separating hyperplane with positive separation margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic system is weakly infeasible when it has no feasible point but the affine constraints approach the cone arbitrarily closely.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
\(L\) is a nonempty affine subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Weak infeasibility is characterized by \(C\cap L=\varnothing\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(C,L)=0\).

notation.meaning: Infimum Euclidean distance between C and L.

children.title: Finite-Level Duality Gaps
children.top_down_role: Primal-dual value discrepancies at a fixed hierarchy order.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Level Duality Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict separation between primal and dual values of one finite semidefinite or conic relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the conic primal problem \(p_d=\inf\{\langle c,x\rangle:Ax=b,\ x\in C\}\), its dual is \(q_d=\sup\{\langle b,y\rangle:c-A^*y\in C^*\}\). Weak duality gives \(q_d\le p_d\). A finite-level duality gap occurs when both values are finite and \(q_d<p_d\). Failure of a suitable constraint qualification, such as strict feasibility on the relevant cone or minimal face, permits such a gap but does not by itself prove one. The gap concerns a fixed relaxation order and is distinct from the hierarchy's asymptotic approximation gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed conic relaxation, a finite duality gap means that the finite primal optimum strictly exceeds the finite dual optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a closed convex cone in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
The displayed primal and dual values are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A finite-level duality gap is the strict inequality \(q_d<p_d\).

notation.meaning: Adjoint of the linear map A.
Primal and dual values at relaxation order d.

children.title: Feasibility-Duality Interaction
children.top_down_role: Conic irregularity linking unstable feasibility status to unreliable primal-dual values.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Duality Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation certificates connect conic feasibility status to dual behavior and constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ax=b\), \(x\in C\), any \(y\) satisfying \(A^*y\in C^*\) and \(\langle b,y\rangle<0\) certifies infeasibility, because feasibility would imply \(0\le\langle A^*y,x\rangle=\langle b,y\rangle\). Such a strict certificate yields positive separation after normalization and therefore cannot exist for a weakly infeasible system. At a feasible relaxation, strict feasibility relative to the appropriate cone face supplies the regularity normally used for strong duality and dual attainment; absent that regularity, gaps or nonattainment become possible but are not automatic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict dual separators certify strong infeasibility, while weak infeasibility lacks them. Relative strict feasibility is the regularity supporting strong duality and attainment.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a closed convex cone.
\(A\) is linear and \(b\) belongs to its codomain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Weak infeasibility excludes a strict certificate \(A^*y\in C^*\), \(\langle b,y\rangle<0\); relative strict feasibility supports strong duality.

children.title: Facial Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Hierarchy models confined to proper faces of the semidefinite cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Facial Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible semidefinite slacks occupy a proper cone face, destroying ambient strict feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider affine semidefinite slacks \(S(y)=S_0+\sum_{i=1}^m y_iS_i\) constrained by \(S(y)\succeq0\). Let \(F_{\min}\) be the smallest face of the positive-semidefinite cone containing every feasible slack. Facial degeneracy occurs when the system is feasible and \(F_{\min}\) is a proper face of that cone, equivalently when no feasible slack is positive definite in the ambient matrix space. A feasible slack may nevertheless lie in the relative interior of \(F_{\min}\); reformulating over this minimal face can restore relative strict feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Facial degeneracy means all feasible PSD slacks lie in a proper face, so ambient strict feasibility fails even though relative strict feasibility may remain.
assumptions_latex: \(S_0,S_1,\ldots,S_m\) are real symmetric matrices of a common size.
The semidefinite feasibility system is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Facial degeneracy holds exactly when \(F_{\min}\subsetneq\mathbb S_+^N\), hence no feasible \(S(y)\) satisfies \(S(y)\succ0\).

notation.meaning: Minimal face containing all feasible slacks.
Cone of N-by-N real positive-semidefinite matrices.

children.title: Conic Nonattainment
children.top_down_role: Finite conic optimal values lacking attained feasible optimizers.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a closed convex cone, \(A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is linear, and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
The feasible set \(S=\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\) is nonempty and \(v=\inf_{x\in S}\langle c,x\rangle\) is finite.

source_refs.locator: 2.13.3 Conic Programming p. 80

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Conic nonattainment occurs when the conic program has a finite infimum but no feasible optimizer. Explicitly, there exists a sequence \((x_k)\subseteq S\) satisfying \(\langle c,x_k\rangle\to v\), while
\[
\{x\in K:Ax=b,\ \langle c,x\rangle=v\}=\varnothing.
\]
Thus every feasible point has objective strictly greater than \(v\), although feasible objective values approach \(v\) arbitrarily closely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic program is nonattaining when its finite optimal value is approached by feasible points but achieved by none.

children.title: Minimal-Face Attainment Boundary

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal-Face Attainment Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment after restricting a conic formulation to its minimal feasible face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Because \(S\subseteq F\subseteq K\), replacing \(K\) by \(F\) leaves the feasible set and its objective values unchanged:
\[
S=F\cap\{x:Ax=b\}.
\]
The minimal-face attainment boundary separates the case \(S\cap\{x:\langle c,x\rangle=v\}\neq\varnothing\) from the case \(S\cap\{x:\langle c,x\rangle=v\}=\varnothing\). Facial reduction can remove lack of strict feasibility in \(K\), but it cannot turn a genuinely unattained finite infimum into an attained one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting to the minimal feasible face preserves the feasible set, value, and whether the finite infimum is attained.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a closed convex cone and \(S=K\cap\{x:Ax=b\}\neq\varnothing\).
\(F\) is the minimal face of \(K\) containing \(S\), and \(v=\inf_{x\in S}\langle c,x\rangle\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v\) is attained exactly when \(S\cap\{x:\langle c,x\rangle=v\}\neq\varnothing\), whether the cone is represented as \(K\) or reduced to \(F\).
