children.title: Polynomial Conditioning Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Numerical instability from polynomial bases and coefficient scaling.

children.title: Basis-Induced Ill-Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Instability arising from poorly conditioned polynomial coordinate systems.

assumptions_latex: \(z_B(x)\) is a polynomial basis vector and \(p(x)=z_B(x)^{\mathsf T}Qz_B(x)\).
\(\mathcal A_B\) is the linear map taking the symmetric Gram matrix \(Q\) to the coefficient vector of \(p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Basis-induced ill-conditioning is present when \(\kappa_2(\mathcal A_B)=\sigma_{\max}(\mathcal A_B)/\sigma_{\min}^{+}(\mathcal A_B)\) is large.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning of coefficient matching in an SOS Gram representation.

source_refs.locator: 2.4 SOS and Nonnegative Polynomials p. 52
source_refs.source_title: Moment and Polynomial Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z_{B'}(x)=Tz_B(x)\) for an invertible basis transformation \(T\). The same polynomial has Gram matrices related by \(Q=T^{\mathsf T}Q'T\), so coefficient matching uses the transformed operator \(\mathcal A_{B'}\). Basis-induced ill-conditioning occurs when
\[
\kappa_2(\mathcal A_{B'})=\frac{\sigma_{\max}(\mathcal A_{B'})}{\sigma_{\min}^{+}(\mathcal A_{B'})}
\]
is large, making small coefficient or rounding perturbations compatible with much larger changes in identifiable Gram-matrix directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial basis is ill-conditioned when its Gram-to-coefficient map has a large positive-singular-value condition number.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Induced Ill-Conditioning

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4 SOS and Nonnegative Polynomials p. 52
source_witnesses.source_title: Moment and Polynomial Optimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited SOS-representation section does not specifically establish the proposed positive-singular-value condition number as the boundary for basis-induced ill-conditioning. An authoritative numerical SOS or Gram-map conditioning source is required.

children.title: Scale-Induced Ill-Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Instability arising from disparate variable, coefficient, or matrix magnitudes.

assumptions_latex: \(p(x)=\sum_{\alpha}p_{\alpha}x^{\alpha}\) is represented in a fixed monomial support.
Variables and the polynomial are rescaled by \(x=Dy\) and \(p(x)=\rho\,\widetilde p(y)\), where \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)\) is nonsingular and \(\rho\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scale-induced ill-conditioning occurs when \(\max_{\alpha}|\rho^{-1}p_lpha d^lpha|/min_{lpha:,p_lphaneq0}|\rho^{-1}p_lpha d^lpha|\) is large.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic-range failure caused by variable and objective scaling.

source_refs.locator: 2.4 SOS and Nonnegative Polynomials p. 52
source_refs.source_title: Moment and Polynomial Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under \(x=Dy\), the scaled coefficients satisfy \(\widetilde p_{\alpha}=\rho^{-1}p_{\alpha}d^{\alpha}\). Scale-induced ill-conditioning is the regime in which the nonzero coefficient dynamic range
\[
R(\widetilde p)=\frac{\max_{\alpha}|\widetilde p_{\alpha}|}{\min_{\alpha:\,\widetilde p_{\alpha}\neq0}|\widetilde p_{\alpha}|}
\]
is large, or the associated coefficient-matching operator has a large condition number. Finite-precision arithmetic may then lose constraints carried by coefficients small relative to the largest scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable or objective scaling causes ill-conditioning when transformed coefficients span a large dynamic range or degrade coefficient matching.
knowledge_statements.title: Scale-Induced Ill-Conditioning

source_witnesses.locator: 2.4 SOS and Nonnegative Polynomials p. 52
source_witnesses.source_title: Moment and Polynomial Optimization

A numerical conditioning source is required before selecting a definitive formulation.

children.title: Conditioning Interaction Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes where basis geometry amplifies scale disparities in hierarchy data.

assumptions_latex: \(z_{B'}(y)=Tz_B(Dy)\) combines an invertible basis transformation \(T\) with a nonsingular diagonal variable scaling \(D\).
\(\mathcal A_{T,D}\) is the resulting Gram-to-coefficient map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interaction regime is quantified by \(\kappa_2(\mathcal A_{T,D})\), which must be assessed for the combined representation rather than inferred from either transformation alone.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint effect of basis choice and polynomial scaling on SOS linear algebra.

source_refs.locator: 2.4 SOS and Nonnegative Polynomials p. 52
source_refs.source_title: Moment and Polynomial Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the combined representation \(z_{B'}(y)=Tz_B(Dy)\), the relevant numerical object is the full map \(\mathcal A_{T,D}\), not the basis and scaling transformations in isolation. The interaction is adverse when
\[
\kappa_2(\mathcal A_{T,D})\gg\min\{\kappa_2(\mathcal A_{T,I}),\kappa_2(\mathcal A_{I,D})\}.
\]
It is compensating when the combined condition number is smaller than both individual values. Hence basis normalization can amplify or mitigate scale-induced dynamic range.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Basis and scaling effects interact through the combined coefficient map and may amplify or compensate for each other.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning Interaction Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The comparison with the minimum of the two isolated condition numbers is not a justified general boundary for adverse interaction. The cited SOS section does not support this comparative criterion.

children.title: Spectral Rank-Decision Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Uncertain flatness and extraction decisions caused by clustered spectra.

children.title: Rank-Threshold Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Variation in inferred moment-matrix rank across plausible numerical thresholds.

assumptions_latex: \(M\succeq0\) is a symmetric numerical moment matrix with eigenvalues \(\lambda_1\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_N\geq0\).
Numerical rank at threshold \(\tau\geq0\) is \(r_\tau(M)=|\{i:\lambda_i>\tau\}|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\lambda_j\in(\tau_1,\tau_2]\), then \(r_{\tau_1}(M)\neq r_{\tau_2}(M)\).

notation.meaning: ordered eigenvalues of the moment matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold dependence of moment-matrix numerical rank.

source_refs.locator: 4.3 Extraction of Solutions p. 80
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For thresholds \(0\leq\tau_1<\tau_2\),
\[
r_{\tau_1}(M)-r_{\tau_2}(M)=|\{i:\tau_1<\lambda_i\leq\tau_2\}|.
\]
Consequently, a rank decision is threshold-sensitive exactly when the interval between two admissible thresholds contains an eigenvalue. In particular, flat-extension tests based on thresholded ranks are not invariant under the threshold choice unless every relevant moment matrix has a spectral gap containing the entire admissible threshold interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerical rank changes with the threshold exactly when an eigenvalue lies between the competing thresholds.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Threshold Sensitivity

source_witnesses.locator: 4.3 Extraction of Solutions p. 80
source_witnesses.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

children.title: Near-Degenerate Spectral Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Uncertain eigenspace separation caused by clustered or nearly vanishing eigenvalues.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is symmetric, \(\widehat M=M+E\), and \(\|E\|_2\leq\varepsilon\).
Rank is decided by comparing eigenvalues with a threshold \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only eigenvalues of \(M\) lying in \([\tau-\varepsilon,\tau+\varepsilon]\) can have an uncertified threshold classification under all admissible perturbations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral uncertainty near a numerical-rank threshold.

source_refs.locator: 4.3 Extraction of Solutions p. 80
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every ordered eigenvalue, spectral perturbation gives
\[
|\lambda_i(\widehat M)-\lambda_i(M)|\leq\varepsilon.
\]
Thus the classification of \(\lambda_i(M)\) relative to \(\tau\) is stable when \(|\lambda_i(M)-\tau|>\varepsilon\). It is potentially ambiguous when \(|\lambda_i(M)-\tau|\leq\varepsilon\), because an admissible perturbation may move that eigenvalue across the threshold and change the reported numerical rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An eigenvalue within the perturbation radius of the rank threshold can cross it, making its rank classification ambiguous.
knowledge_statements.title: Near-Degenerate Spectral Ambiguity

source_witnesses.locator: 4.3 Extraction of Solutions p. 80
source_witnesses.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The claim relies on an eigenvalue perturbation theorem not specifically supported by the cited extraction section. A source with a theorem-level locator for the spectral perturbation bound is required.

children.title: Extraction Decision Instability
children.top_down_role: Unstable flatness or support-recovery decisions induced by ambiguous spectral evidence.

assumptions_latex: \(M_d(y)\) and \(M_{d-r}(y)\) are nested moment matrices used in a flat-extension extraction test.
Their numerical ranks are computed with threshold \(\tau\) from data perturbed within spectral error \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The extraction decision is robust only if the relevant spectra avoid \([\tau-\varepsilon,\tau+\varepsilon]\); otherwise the rank equality may change under admissible perturbations.

notation.meaning: moment matrix of relaxation order d

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stability boundary for flat-extension-based optimizer extraction.

source_refs.locator: 4.3 Extraction of Solutions p. 80
source_refs.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A thresholded flat-extension decision accepts extraction when
\[
r_\tau(M_d(y))=r_\tau(M_{d-r}(y)).
\]
If either matrix has an eigenvalue in \([\tau-\varepsilon,\tau+\varepsilon]\), admissible perturbations can alter one rank without altering the other, switching acceptance to rejection or conversely. If both spectra avoid this interval, every perturbation of spectral norm at most \(\varepsilon\) preserves the individual thresholded ranks and hence the extraction decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flat-extension extraction is unstable when spectral uncertainty can change either of the two ranks used by the test.
knowledge_statements.title: Extraction Decision Instability

source_witnesses.locator: 4.3 Extraction of Solutions p. 80
source_witnesses.source_title: Moments, Positive Polynomials and Their Applications

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A near-threshold eigenvalue makes rank change possible in an unconstrained matrix perturbation model, but it does not by itself show that admissible perturbations of the shared moment data can change only one nested rank. The perturbation model and supporting source must be specified.

children.title: Numerical-Algebraic Certification Gap
children.top_down_role: Floating-point feasibility insufficient for reliable algebraic certification.

children.title: Solver-Tolerance Acceptance
children.top_down_role: Feasibility and optimality judgments made within floating-point solver tolerances.

assumptions_latex: A numerical SOS relaxation returns primal-dual variables \((u,v)\) for linear equations \(Au=b\), cone membership \(u\in K\), and dual equations \(A^{\mathsf T}v+s=c\), \(s\in K^*\).
Nonnegative tolerances \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_K,\varepsilon_g\) are prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance under positive tolerances establishes approximate feasibility and complementarity only, not an exact SOS identity or exact cone membership.

notation.meaning: distance to a set in the chosen solver norm

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic residual-based acceptance for a conic SOS relaxation.

source_refs.locator: 2.13.3 Conic Programming p. 80
source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Global Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A residual-based solver accepts \((u,v,s)\) when
\[
\|Au-b\|\leq\varepsilon_p,\quad \|A^{\mathsf T}v+s-c\|\leq\varepsilon_d,
\]
\[
\operatorname{dist}(u,K)\leq\varepsilon_K,\quad \operatorname{dist}(s,K^*)\leq\varepsilon_K,
\quad |\langle u,s\rangle|\leq\varepsilon_g.
\]
These inequalities define numerical acceptance. Unless all tolerances vanish and arithmetic is exact, they do not imply exact primal-dual feasibility, an exact polynomial coefficient identity, or an algebraically valid SOS certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver accepts when residuals and cone violations meet tolerances, which certifies only approximate conic feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Tolerance Acceptance

source_witnesses.locator: 2.13.3 Conic Programming p. 80
source_witnesses.source_title: Convex Analysis and Global Optimization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The listed residual tests are a proposed generic acceptance rule rather than a universal conic-solver criterion. The cited conic-programming section does not specifically support these tolerances, norms, or complementarity test.

children.title: Certificate Residual Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Computed outputs whose algebraic residuals remain too large for reliable certification.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Residual Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual test for a polynomial SOS lower-bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the residual polynomial
\[
r=p-\gamma-\sigma_0-\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j.
\]
An exact certificate requires every coefficient of \(r\) to equal zero and every Gram matrix defining \(\sigma_j\) to be positive semidefinite. A certificate residual mismatch occurs when a numerical solver accepts the coefficient equations within tolerance but \(r\neq0\) in exact arithmetic. The resulting approximate identity alone does not prove \(p(x)\geq\gamma\) on \(\{x:g_j(x)\geq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero exact residual invalidates an SOS identity even when its numerical coefficient residual lies within solver tolerance.
assumptions_latex: A proposed identity is \(p-\gamma=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j\), where each \(\sigma_j\) is represented by a Gram matrix.
All polynomials are expanded in one fixed monomial basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The proposed certificate is algebraically exact if and only if \(r=0\) coefficientwise and every Gram matrix is positive semidefinite.

children.title: Tolerance-to-Certification Gap
children.top_down_role: Cases where numerical solver success does not transfer to certificate validity.

knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-to-Certification Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar counterexample separating tolerance acceptance from exact certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(0<\delta\leq\varepsilon\), \(p=0\), \(z=1\), \(\gamma=\delta\), and \(Q=-\delta\). Then the coefficient identity \(p-\gamma=z^{\mathsf T}Qz\) holds exactly, while \(\operatorname{dist}(Q,\mathbb{S}_+^1)=\delta\leq\varepsilon\), so a tolerance test may accept \(Q\) as approximately positive semidefinite. Nevertheless, \(Q\not\succeq0\) and the claimed bound \(p\geq\gamma\) is false because \(0<\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximately positive semidefinite Gram matrix can pass tolerance checks while yielding a false SOS lower bound.
assumptions_latex: A solver accepts scalar cone violations and equality residuals of magnitude at most \(\varepsilon>0\).
An SOS lower bound is encoded by \(p-\gamma=z^{\mathsf T}Qz\) with \(Q\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive numerical tolerance does not by itself imply an exact SOS certificate or a valid lower bound.

children.title: Sparse Scalability Failure Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Loss of convergence, strength, consistency, or computational accessibility in scalable hierarchy variants.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Chordal-TSSOS: A Moment-SOS Hierarchy That Exploits Term Sparsity with Chordal Extension
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Distinction between scalable chordal variants and available convergence guarantees
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Chordal-TSSOS: A Moment-SOS Hierarchy That Exploits Term Sparsity with Chordal Extension

children.title: Running-Intersection Failure
children.top_down_role: Clique geometry outside standard sparse convergence structures.

assumptions_latex: \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\subseteq\{1,ldots,n\}\) are variable cliques used by a sparse moment-SOS construction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Running-intersection failure means that no permutation of the cliques satisfies \(C_k\cap\bigcup_{i<k}C_i\subseteq C_{j(k)}\) for every \(k\geq2\).

notation.meaning: an earlier clique containing the separator

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial failure of the standard running-intersection property for sparse SOS cliques.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The clique family has the running-intersection property if its members can be ordered so that, for every \(k=2,ldots,m\), there exists \(j(k)<k\) with
\[
C_k\cap\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^{k-1}C_i\right)\subseteq C_{j(k)}.
\]
Running-intersection failure occurs when no ordering has this property. Equivalently, in every ordering at least one clique has an overlap with preceding cliques that is not contained in any single preceding clique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Running-intersection fails when no clique ordering places each new clique's accumulated overlap inside one earlier clique.
knowledge_statements.title: Running-Intersection Failure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The combinatorial definition is recognizable, but no source is supplied and both the assumptions and statement contain malformed instances of the index range. An authoritative sparse moment-SOS source with a specific running-intersection locator is required.

children.title: Inconsistent Clique Moments
children.top_down_role: Local moment data lacking a compatible global representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Inconsistent Clique Moments
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Overlap inconsistency in a clique-sparse truncated moment relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1,\ldots,C_s\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be variable cliques and let \(y^{(i)}=(y^{(i)}_\alpha)\) be truncated moment data on \(C_i\). Each local moment and localizing matrix may satisfy its required positive-semidefinite constraints. However, if some \(i,j\) and monomial \(x^\alpha\) supported on \(C_i\cap C_j\) satisfy \(y^{(i)}_\alpha\ne y^{(j)}_\alpha\), then no global truncated sequence \(y\) can restrict to every \(y^{(i)}\). Consequently, the clique data cannot be moments of one common representing measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Locally feasible clique moments admit no common global representation when their values disagree on an overlap monomial.
assumptions_latex: \(C_i\cap C_j\ne\varnothing\) for at least one pair \(i,j\).
All compared overlap moments occur within the common truncation order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists i,j,\alpha:\ y^{(i)}_\alpha\ne y^{(j)}_\alpha\implies \nexists y\text{ with }y|_{C_k}=y^{(k)}\ \forall k.\)

notation.meaning: local truncated moment sequence on clique i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The overlap-consistency obstruction is mathematically appropriate and the failure_boundary kind fits, but no source supports the sparse moment compatibility claim.

children.title: Overaggressive Support Sparsification
children.top_down_role: Loss of certificate strength through insufficient support completion.

knowledge_statements.title: Overaggressive Support Sparsification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate loss caused by restricting SOS Gram supports too severely.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix relaxation order \(d\), let \(Q_d\) be the full truncated quadratic module, and let \(Q_{d,\mathcal A}\subseteq Q_d\) retain only SOS Gram representations supported on prescribed monomial sets \(\mathcal A\). If the support completion is insufficient, strict containment can occur: \(Q_{d,\mathcal A}\subsetneq Q_d\). Hence there exists a polynomial \(p\in Q_d\setminus Q_{d,\mathcal A}\); the full order-\(d\) relaxation certifies \(p\ge0\) on the feasible set, while the sparsified relaxation cannot certify it at that order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An undersized monomial support can exclude valid degree-bounded SOS certificates and thereby weaken the relaxation bound.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_{d,\mathcal A}\) is formed by deleting admissible Gram monomials from \(Q_d\).
Both modules use the same constraints and degree order \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_{d,\mathcal A}\subsetneq Q_d\implies \exists p\in Q_d\setminus Q_{d,\mathcal A}.\)

notation.meaning: full quadratic module truncated at order d

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cone-inclusion argument matches the support-sparsification failure and its content kind, but the asserted relationship between support completion and strict certificate loss lacks a cited source.

children.title: Representation-Capacity Explosion
children.top_down_role: Combinatorial representation growth limiting attainable hierarchy order.

children.title: Basis-Cardinality Explosion
children.top_down_role: Combinatorial growth in monomial or reduced-basis cardinality.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Cardinality Explosion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense monomial-basis growth in an order-d moment/SOS relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\) variables, the monomials of total degree at most \(d\) form a basis of cardinality \(N(n,d)=\binom{n+d}{d}\). A dense order-\(d\) moment matrix or SOS Gram matrix therefore has dimension \(N(n,d)\), contains \(N(n,d)(N(n,d)+1)/2\) independent symmetric entries, and requires quadratic matrix storage. For fixed \(d\), \(N(n,d)=\Theta(n^d)\); for fixed \(n\), \(N(n,d)=\Theta(d^n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dense degree-d monomial basis has binomial size, making Gram and moment matrix storage quadratic in that cardinality.
assumptions_latex: \(n,d\in\mathbb N\).
The relaxation uses every monomial of total degree at most \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N(n,d)=\binom{n+d}{d},\qquad \#\operatorname{sym}(M_d)=\frac{N(n,d)(N(n,d)+1)}2.\)

notation.meaning: number of monomials in n variables of degree at most d
dense order-d moment or Gram matrix

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The basis cardinality and asymptotic bounds are standard and complexity_bound fits the leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Memory-Capacity Exhaustion
children.top_down_role: Storage limits arising from matrices, coefficient maps, and solver workspace.

knowledge_statements.title: Memory-Capacity Exhaustion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary storage threshold for a dense moment or Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N=\binom{n+d}{d}\) and suppose each stored scalar requires \(b>0\) bytes. Storing one dense symmetric order-\(d\) moment or Gram matrix requires at least \(bN(N+1)/2\) bytes when only one triangle is retained, before solver workspaces and factorization fill are counted. Thus a memory budget \(B\) cannot accommodate even the matrix data whenever \(bN(N+1)/2>B\); a full dense array requires \(bN^2\) bytes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense relaxation is impossible within budget once the triangular matrix data alone exceed available memory.
assumptions_latex: \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) and \(b,B>0\).
The order-\(d\) matrix uses the full total-degree monomial basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\frac{b}{2}\binom{n+d}{d}\left(\binom{n+d}{d}+1\right)>B\implies\text{matrix storage exceeds }B.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The threshold is correct for an explicitly materialized packed symmetric matrix and complexity_bound is defensible, but the storage model and SOS implementation claim require an authoritative citation.

children.title: Attainable-Order Ceiling
children.top_down_role: Maximum practical hierarchy order imposed by representation size and memory capacity.

knowledge_statements.title: Attainable-Order Ceiling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Largest dense relaxation order permitted by an explicit packed-matrix storage budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\ge 1\), let each stored scalar occupy \(b>0\) bytes, and let the memory budget satisfy \(B\ge b\). Define \(N(n,d)=\binom{n+d}{d}\) and let \(d_{\max}\) be the largest nonnegative integer satisfying \(bN(n,d)(N(n,d)+1)/2\le B\). Then no explicitly stored dense moment or Gram matrix of order \(d>d_{\max}\) fits within the budget even with packed triangular storage. Additional solver workspaces and factorization fill can only reduce the practically attainable order below this storage-only ceiling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For at least one variable and a budget large enough to store the order-zero matrix, the storage ceiling is the largest order whose packed triangular dense matrix fits in memory.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb N\) with \(n\ge 1\).
\(b>0\) and \(B\ge b\).
Only explicit packed-triangular storage of one dense symmetric matrix is counted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d_{\max}=\max\left\{d\in\mathbb N_0:\frac{bN(n,d)(N(n,d)+1)}{2}\le B\right\},\qquad N(n,d)=\binom{n+d}{d}.\]

notation.meaning: cardinality of the total-degree monomial basis
bytes occupied by each explicitly stored scalar

children.title: Accuracy-Scalability Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Loss of bound or certificate quality in scalable sparse or numerical variants.

knowledge_statements.title: Accuracy-Scalability Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic loss of relaxation strength under certificate-cone restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimization of a polynomial \(f\) on a fixed feasible set. Let \(Q_d^{\mathrm{sc}}\subseteq Q_d^{\mathrm{full}}\) be scalable and full certificate cones at the same order, and define \(\rho(Q)=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma\in Q\}\). Then \(\rho(Q_d^{\mathrm{sc}})\le\rho(Q_d^{\mathrm{full}})\le f^*\). Reducing support, block size, or cone strength may lower computational cost, but strict cone inclusion can produce a strictly weaker lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting the certificate cone for scalability cannot improve the minimization lower bound and may make it strictly worse.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_d^{\mathrm{sc}}\subseteq Q_d^{\mathrm{full}}\).
Every element of \(Q_d^{\mathrm{full}}\) is nonnegative on the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(Q_d^{\mathrm{sc}})\le\rho(Q_d^{\mathrm{full}})\le f^*.\)

notation.meaning: full certificate cone at the same order

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bound monotonicity follows from cone inclusion and the property kind fits the tradeoff leaf, but no SOS hierarchy source supports the scalable-cone interpretation.

children.title: Extraction Failures
children.top_down_role: Regimes where strong or exact bounds do not yield stable and complete optimizer recovery.

children.title: Nonflat Optimal Moment Data
children.top_down_role: Optimal moment solutions lacking finite-rank extraction structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonflat Optimal Moment Data
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the finite-rank flat-extension criterion at an optimal relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y^*\) be an optimal truncated moment sequence at order \(d\), and let \(r\) be the largest degree shift required by the constraints. Standard finite-atomic extraction applies when \(\operatorname{rank}M_d(y^*)=\operatorname{rank}M_{d-r}(y^*)\). If instead \(\operatorname{rank}M_d(y^*)>\operatorname{rank}M_{d-r}(y^*)\), the data are nonflat: this rank certificate does not establish a finitely atomic representing measure, so optimizer extraction from multiplication matrices is not certified at that order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal moment solution with increasing truncated ranks lacks the flatness certificate needed for finite-atomic optimizer extraction.
assumptions_latex: \(y^*\) satisfies the order-\(d\) moment and localizing constraints.
\(d\ge r\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}M_d(y^*)>\operatorname{rank}M_{d-r}(y^*)\implies\text{flat extraction is not certified}.\)

notation.meaning: moment matrix of order k formed from the optimal data

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement carefully limits its conclusion to failure of a flatness certificate, and failure_boundary fits. An authoritative flat-extension result is needed to validate the constraint-dependent shift r and extraction conditions.

children.title: Incomplete Multiple-Minimizer Recovery
children.top_down_role: Failure to recover all isolated optimizers from a selected moment solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Multiple-Minimizer Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An optimal moment solution may represent only one of several isolated minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Minimize \(f(x)=(x^2-1)^2\) over \([-1,1]\). The global minimum is \(0\), attained at the two isolated points \(-1\) and \(1\). The measure \(\mu=\delta_1\) is an optimal representing measure, and its moments satisfy \(y_k=1\) for every retained degree \(k\). Any exact atomic extraction from these moments returns only the support point \(1\), although \(-1\) is also a global minimizer. Thus one selected optimal moment solution need not encode all minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a polynomial with minimizers at both endpoints, the optimal Dirac moment solution at one endpoint omits the other.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation order is sufficient to represent \(f\) and the interval constraints.
The selected optimal moment solution is generated by \(\delta_1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{supp}(\delta_1)=\{1\}\subsetneq\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in[-1,1]}(x^2-1)^2=\{-1,1\}.\)

notation.meaning: k-th scalar moment of the selected measure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit Dirac-measure example is correct and counterexample fits the leaf, but no source is supplied for the link between a selected optimal moment measure and exact atomic extraction.

children.title: Continuum Extraction Nonuniqueness
children.top_down_role: Nonunique measure representations on positive-dimensional minimizer sets.

children.title: Continuum-Support Minimizer Sets
children.top_down_role: Extraction regimes involving positive-dimensional or continuously supported minimizer sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuum-Support Minimizer Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A continuum of minimizers can generate persistently nonflat moment data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Minimize the zero polynomial on \([0,1]\). Every point of \([0,1]\) is a global minimizer. If \(\mu\) is Lebesgue probability measure on \([0,1]\), then \(y_k=\int_0^1x^k\,dx=1/(k+1)\). For every \(d\ge1\), the Hankel moment matrix \(M_d(y)=(1/(i+j+1))_{i,j=0}^d\) is positive definite and has rank \(d+1\), whereas \(M_{d-1}(y)\) has rank \(d\). Hence flat finite-atomic extraction never occurs along these truncations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lebesgue moments for a zero objective on an interval remain nonflat because the entire interval consists of minimizers.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set is \([0,1]\).
The selected optimal measure is normalized Lebesgue measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}M_d(y)=d+1> d=\operatorname{rank}M_{d-1}(y)\quad(d\ge1).\)

notation.meaning: k-th moment of normalized Lebesgue measure on the interval

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Hilbert moment matrices have the stated ranks and the counterexample fits continuum-support extraction failure, but the positive-definiteness and flat-extraction interpretation lack cited support.

children.title: Representing-Measure Nonuniqueness
children.top_down_role: Moment data compatible with multiple representing measures.

knowledge_statements.title: Representing-Measure Nonuniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite truncated moments need not determine a unique representing measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \([-1,1]\), consider the degree-one truncated sequence \(y_0=1\) and \(y_1=0\). Both \(\mu_1=\delta_0\) and \(\mu_2=(\delta_{-1}+\delta_1)/2\) are probability measures supported on \([-1,1]\), and both satisfy \(y_k=\int x^k\,d\mu_i\) for \(k=0,1\). Since \(\mu_1\ne\mu_2\), these feasible truncated moment data have multiple representing measures with different supports.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mass at zero and equal mass at the two endpoints share the same degree-one moments but are different measures.
assumptions_latex: Only moments through degree one are specified.
Representing measures are probability measures supported on \([-1,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y=(1,0)\text{ is represented by both }\delta_0\text{ and }(\delta_{-1}+\delta_1)/2.\)

notation.meaning: specified truncated moment of degree k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two measures do share the degree-zero and degree-one moments, and counterexample fits representing-measure nonuniqueness, but no inspectable source is provided.

children.title: Nonunique Extraction Outcomes
children.top_down_role: Ambiguity in recovered support or measure interpretation despite valid optimal moment data.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique Extraction Outcomes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identical truncated optimal data can support distinct compatible extraction outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Minimize the zero polynomial on \([-1,1]\) and retain only \(y_0=1\) and \(y_1=0\). The compatible measures \(\delta_0\) and \((\delta_{-1}+\delta_1)/2\) are both optimal and agree on all retained moments, yet their extracted supports are respectively \(\{0\}\) and \(\{-1,1\}\). Therefore an extraction procedure that selects a representing extension of these truncated data has no unique outcome unless additional moments, rank conditions, or selection rules are imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The same optimal truncated moments can yield either one interior point or two endpoints, depending on the representing extension selected.
